But four Springs are two pairs of opposites, and they cannot be gathered without a clash. Start with neighbors, Tide and Strata, and throw in Ember and Gale twice over: half of each goes to murk. That is the price, and it is better known in advance.

kp: Quickdust from the Crucible Живая пыль из Тигля
Живая пыль Quickdust Живая пыль Quickdust
nodes.hint: The dust that wakes flux can be brewed. Read redstone dust with the Loupe.

pages.t: A glint is a living light that never goes out and a store of Halo in a bottle: released, it circles its place forever, and at the Flux Workbench it takes the place of a lantern's prism and dust. It is never born in the world on its own: the Crucible lights it. Gather three parts of Halo in the distillate — the flux of the world that sleeps in shards, crystals and quickdust — and no fewer than three parts of any other current. Throw glowstone dust in last, and a glint rises from the brew.

The heat must be gentle: at a strong boil the spark dies before it catches. The strongest current in the distillate besides Halo colors the glint's heart and trail, and three parts of it go with the glint. Three Tide shards give a Tide glint; for another color, pour in more of another current.

A glint circles over its Crucible for a few minutes, then dims and goes out. One Crucible never has more than three: while three circle over it, the glowstone dust will not sink. A glint is skittish — creep up on it crouching, with an empty glass bottle in hand. Once caught, it lives in the bottle as long as you like.

Use the bottle on a block to let the glint out: it circles that spot and never goes out again. A bottled glint carries Halo and its own current — the Loupe will show it, and the Crucible will dissolve it. On the Flux Workbench a glint stands in for the prism and glowstone dust of a firefly lantern.

kp: Светлячковый фонарь Firefly Lantern Огонёк в бутылочке Bottled Glint
nodes.hint: A spark of living flux can be brewed and caught. Learn Halo — it sleeps in current shards.

pages.t: A seed is your own shard farm: planted, it grows into a current crystal, and you no longer need to hunt for nests in caves. A shard is set flux, and on its own it does not grow: there is no life in it. Brew it with Bloom, the current of life, and with its own current, and the shard comes alive as a seed. Only the six primal currents have seeds.

Gather two parts of Bloom and two parts of the shard's own current in the distillate, then throw the shard in last; any heat will do. Bloom is in bread, apples and eggs, and a dissolved shard of the same current gives four parts — enough for two seeds.

Plant the seed on any solid face — floor, wall or ceiling, like an amethyst bud. It grows in three steps — a small, a medium and a large bud — and at last into a crystal of its current. Every step takes a little flux from the land around; in drained land the seed waits until the flux comes back.

A broken bud gives its seed back whole — you can replant it, but the flux it took does not come back. A grown crystal broken with a pickaxe yields shards and half the flux it drank: seeds make no flux of their own, and a large farm needs land with living flux — by a river, not in a desert.

kp: Затравка кристалла Прилива Tide Crystal Seed Затравка кристалла Прилива Tide Crystal Seed
nodes.hint: A crystal can be grown, not only found. Learn Bloom — read an apple or bread with the Loupe.

pages.t: A vessel stores currents for later: Confluence, devices and the Crucible take from it, so you need not brew from a single cauldron. A vessel — glass blown on opaline in rings of old bronze — holds one current, up to a hundred and ninety-two parts. A siphon above the neck fills it, a siphon at the side or under the base draws from it. Broken by hand, a vessel carries its contents along.

Flint and steel struck on a vessel burns the rune of the current inside onto its bronze tag. A branded vessel keeps its current even when empty: it takes nothing else and calls its own along the siphons. An axe scrapes the brand off.
Bindwax seals the neck: a sealed vessel neither gives nor takes. An axe chips the seal off.

What is spilled is not lost for nothing. Tip a vessel over with an empty hand while sneaking — or let a blast shatter it — and the distillate lies in a puddle. In ten seconds the puddle dries, and a quarter of what was spilled settles into the land as murk.

A spillway vessel keeps its own current, and whatever it cannot take — its own surplus and any other current — it passes to the vessel beneath, if that one accepts it; its own surplus with no such vessel spills onto the ground. Stack spillway vessels on top of one another, and they sort the currents among themselves: each keeps its own.

A vessel can be carried in hand too, like a large vial. Take it and click another holder — a vessel, an Alembic, a Gyre: empty or holding the same current, it draws that current, as much as fits. With nothing to draw — the other is empty or yours is full — the vessel pours its own back, as much as is taken. Only the same current moves; brands and seals are kept, and nothing spills over the rim from your hand. To set a vessel down next to a holder, sneak.

The Lumenash Filter goes into Alembics, Strainer Siphons and the Purifier: lumenash cleans murk by itself, so everything that sorts or cleans currents is built around its sieve. String is stretched crosswise in a rim of lumenash planks and bound with bronze.

kp: Сосуд Vessel Переливной сосуд Spillway Vessel Ясеневый фильтр Lumenash Filter Сосуд Vessel
nodes.hint: A current in liquid form can be kept: it is poured into vessels. Read glass with the Loupe.

pages.t: Siphons link the Crucible, vessels and devices: distillate runs along them by itself, without your hands. A siphon is a glass tube in bronze clamps; it flows like water: down and level, but never up. A siphon at the side draws distillate from the Crucible, a siphon above the neck fills a vessel — so a vessel stands below the Crucible.

A siphon takes a part from a Crucible or a vessel only if some holder down the tube will take it right now — and passes it straight there. A vessel's brand calls its own current; the fullest of what is awaited leaves the Crucible first. The nearest holder comes first, equal ones take turns. Poured into a Crucible from above, distillate mixes by the rules of the Wheel.

There are no plugs: a current with nowhere to go is never taken in — it stays in its holder, and a drop of it trembles at the outlet. The Loupe on such a siphon says "No receiver". Set out a vessel that will take that current, and it flows.
A gate valve shuts a siphon: the handle along the tube — open, across it — shut. A redstone signal shuts it for as long as it lasts.
A strainer siphon lets through only the current of its brand; to any other it is a wall. The brand is burned with flint and steel while that current stands in the sieve.
A Brewing Casing is forged copper in speculum sheets with runes along its band. It keeps hot distillate on its course: the Pump, the Separator and the Mixing Vat are built from it.

kp: Сифон Siphon Задвижка Gate Valve Сифон с ситом Strainer Siphon Варочный кожух Brewing Casing Сифон Siphon
nodes.hint: Glass tubes along which distillate flows by itself. Discover Drift, the current of motion.

pages.t: The Gyre is a large shared store: any currents in one sphere, and the Confluence Heart takes whatever it needs from it. It holds up to one thousand five hundred and thirty-six parts at once. A sphere of blown glass on a bronze foot, two blocks tall: the currents in it neither blend nor clash — each circles the axis as its own strand, and the brass band of the Wheel glows while the sphere is filled.
A siphon over the neck fills the Gyre with any current while there is room. A siphon at its side or under its foot draws from it — first the fullest of what is awaited down the tube.
Set the Gyre by a Confluence Heart: the Heart draws from it any current the Confluence needs — as it does from vessels nearby.
Broken by hand, the Gyre carries what it holds away with it. A blast shatters it: the fullest current lies in a puddle, and the rest settles into the land as murk at once.

nodes.hint: A great store where currents swirl without mixing. Read a vessel with the Loupe.

pages.t: A vial carries distillate where no siphon reaches: scoop eight parts in one place and pour them out in another. It is a narrow tube of glass under a copper stopper. A vial used on a vessel, an Alembic or a Gyre scoops as much as fits: from a vessel its current, from a Gyre the fullest one, and into a vial that already holds distillate only its own current. A vial does not scoop from a Crucible: it is not a store.

When there is nothing to scoop — the vial is full, or its current is not there — it pours out instead: into a vessel, a Gyre or the Crucible, as much as they take. In the Crucible what is poured mixes by the rules of the Wheel. A vial thrown into the Crucible dissolves with what it holds. A vessel carried in hand pours the same way (the "Distillate" entry).

nodes.hint: Distillate can be carried — eight parts at a time.

pages.t: Distillation takes things apart into currents on its own — no water, no catalyst, no hands — and sorts them into Alembics. A retort is a stone hearth under a copper gourd: put a thing with currents in it and feed the hearth coal — the thing breaks down, and its currents rise as vapor into the gourd's neck. Things go in by hand or by hopper from above, fuel by hand or by hopper from the side.

Alembics catch the currents — vessels with a beak, stacked on the retort's neck, up to four. Each current goes where it already is, or else into the first empty alembic. With nowhere to go, it waits in the retort, and no new thing is taken. Siphons at the alembics' sides draw the distillate away.

Distillation is not free: a sixth of the currents is lost and settles as murk. A brazier briquette — coal boiled down in the Crucible with Ember and Spark — burns in the hearth four times as long as coal.

The retort and its column of alembics are on the diagram. Optionally, two more columns on side outlets at its flanks and a settling vat behind: the entry "Side Outlets and the Settling Vat" tells of them. "Place ghost" sets it all in the world.

kp: Реторта Retort Алембик Alembic Жаровой брикет Brazier Briquette Реторта Retort
nodes.hint: A thing need not be dissolved — it can be distilled, and its currents rise on their own. Read fire with the Loupe.

nodes.n: Side Outlets and the Settling Vat

pages.t: Side Outlets give a retort more columns of Alembics — more currents at once — and a Settling Vat catches what is lost as silt instead of murk. An outlet is set flush against the side of a retort, its tube toward it, and another column of Alembics rises on its neck. Outlets fit any retort.

A settling vat is a bog-oak tub beside a retort. What distillation loses settles in it as silt instead of murk: eight parts make one silt. Take the silt out with an empty hand; a full vat catches nothing more. Dissolved in the Crucible, silt gives Murk.

kp: Side Outlets and the Settling Vat Отводы и Отстойник
Отвод Side Outlet Отстойник Settling Vat Отвод Side Outlet
nodes.hint: More columns and less murk at the retort.

nodes.n: Valves, Narrows, Pumps and the Dipstick

pages.t: These four fittings rule a siphon network: where to flow, who goes first, how to lift it up and how much is where. A Check Valve passes distillate only in the direction of the arrow on its body. A level tube flows both ways; the valve divides it — nothing flows back. It is placed with the arrow pointing away from you.
Narrows is a tube pinched by a clamp. A holder beyond it gets distillate only once every nearer one is full — and twice as slowly. So one outlet feeds the main store first and the spare after.

A pump — a standpipe with bronze bellows — is the only thing that lifts distillate. It enters the pump from the siphon below and leaves upward; stack pumps to lift higher. Each part lifted takes a little of the chunk's flux: on drained land the pump stands still.

A dipstick is a brass rod with notches: touch a vessel, a Gyre, the Crucible or a siphon with it, and you learn exactly how much is inside. Sneaking, touch a siphon's arm and it closes, so two networks side by side do not merge; touch it again and it opens.

kp: Valves, Narrows, Pumps and the Dipstick Клапан, Сужение, Насос и Щуп
Обратный клапан Check Valve Сужение Narrows Насос Pump Щуп Dipstick Обратный клапан Check Valve
nodes.hint: Steer the distillate, decide who comes first, and lift it up.

pages.t: A Holding Chamber feeds the Crucible in portions, and it brews on its own: the chamber measures out twelve parts and gives them all at once when the holder below it is empty. The chamber is a flask in a bronze cage. A siphon above fills it with any currents until a portion is gathered. A full chamber waits, and while it gives, it takes nothing from above.

So one siphon feeds the Crucible portion by portion: the chamber above gives a portion, the Crucible brews, empties — and receives the next. The shutter handle on the drain stands along it while the chamber gives. A broken chamber spills its portion in a puddle.

kp: Камера Holding Chamber Камера Holding Chamber
nodes.hint: Measure out a portion and give it all at once.

pages.t: A Separator turns a compound current back into its parents: spare Drift becomes Gale and Tide again, and any current can be brought down to the Springs and Poles. It is a glass drum with brass paddles. A siphon above fills it with compound currents only; the paddles split two parts of a compound by the Wheel into a part of each parent, and a parent that is itself compound splits once it has a pair.

Siphons at its sides and below draw only Springs and Poles from the drum. A lone part of a compound waits in the drum for its pair — the Loupe tells you who waits. Nothing is lost and nothing is born: as many parts leave as went in.

nodes.hint: Split a compound current into its parents.

pages.t: A Brewing Tower brews Crucible recipes on its own: feed it by siphon, give it catalysts and take what is made; it needs neither water nor fire. Set a Crucible on a fluxsteel retort and throw a pinch of quickdust on it: the retort becomes the firebox, the Crucible the dome, and together they wake as a Brewing Tower. The Crucible's distillate passes into the dome.

The tower brews the Crucible recipes it remembers. Strike it with a recipe's catalyst and it remembers the most demanding one you know; sneaking with an empty hand makes it forget the last one. The tower itself remembers one recipe, each abacus beside it two more. The tower brews no creatures: a glint needs the Crucible.

A siphon over the dome pours only what the remembered recipes need — no more than two brews' worth. Catalysts go in by hand or by a hopper from the side or top, the brew comes out by an empty hand or a hopper below. The tower needs no water and no fire: the chunk's flux heats each brew, and on drained land the tower stands still.

The whole tower is on the diagram: the retort below, the Crucible on it, abacuses at the sides of both halves, hoppers behind and below. "Place ghost" sets it in the world where you look: build along it, then sprinkle a pinch of quickdust on the Crucible.

kp: Счёты Abacus Варочная башня Brewing Tower
nodes.hint: A Crucible-samovar: it brews by itself while it is fed. A milestone of alchemy.

pages.t: A Mixing Vat combines currents without a Crucible: two parts of different currents become a part of their compound when the one you need is scarce in the world. It is a copper vat with a stirrer. Siphons above pour currents in; two parts of currents that combine on the Wheel become a part of the compound. Siphons at the sides and below draw only the compound; parts still waiting for a pair stay in the vat.

Opposite Springs — Tide with Ember, Strata with Gale — merge only when the vat stands below both holders they flow from: as in the basin of a Riverbed puzzle. Otherwise the arriving part clashes and goes to murk. Two parts become one; a separator gives back one part of each parent from two parts of the compound — no breeding of currents this way.

kp: Смесительный чан Mixing Vat Смесительный чан Mixing Vat
nodes.hint: Add two currents into one — by the rules of the basin.

pages.t: An Atomizer gives a potion as a cloud to everyone nearby and pays for it in distillate, not bottles: the pattern stays. It is a copper body with a glass flask and a brass nozzle. Put a potion in the flask as a pattern; a siphon above fills it with distillate of the potion's currents. On a redstone signal the Atomizer breathes a cloud of that potion out before the nozzle, paying half the potion's currents.

The cloud lasts ten seconds; rain washes it away three times sooner. A potion's currents are those of its last ingredient plus Brew for each brewing step: the Loupe on the atomizer tells you what a puff costs.

nodes.hint: A potion as a cloud — paid in distillate, not in bottles.

pages.t: A band makes a vessel bigger without pouring it out: fitted on a standing vessel, Spillway Vessel or Alembic, it keeps the contents, and the holder holds more — a speculum band by half again, a fluxsteel band twice as much. A second band will not go over the first, but a stronger one takes the place of a weaker, and the removed one comes back to your hands; a vessel broken by hand carries its band along.
A bright band — four times as much. Brightsteel holds no murk: a vessel under it, broken other than by hand, spills not a puddle but silt — a handful for every eight parts.

A wootz band — six times as much: the distillate in it is compressed. But Murk cannot bear the pressure: a vessel more than nine tenths full of Murk bursts — a pool of mire ooze where it stood, and the chunk grows murky.

A still band — three times as much, and a vessel with it does not freeze in the Stillness: where nothing flows, siphons still fill and drain it. Without it, a vessel in the Stillness stands like the water — until a thaw lantern's circle.

A freshet band — ten times as much. What a spillway vessel under it spills does not go to murk as a puddle but returns to the chunk as flux — one unit for every four: the only overflow that does not murk.

kp: Бронзовый обруч Speculum Band Флюкс-стальной обруч Fluxsteel Band Ясный обруч Bright Band Булатный обруч Wootz Band Стылый обруч Still Band Вешний обруч Freshet Band Флюкс-стальной обруч Fluxsteel Band
nodes.hint: A vessel need not be replaced — it can be banded.

pages.t: A fluxsteel retort distills twice as fast and loses half as much, and under a Crucible it wakes a Brewing Tower. Reforge the retort's gourd in fluxsteel: a thing breaks down twice as fast, and only a twelfth of its currents is lost.

kp: Флюкс-стальная реторта Fluxsteel Retort Флюкс-стальная реторта Fluxsteel Retort
nodes.hint: A gourd of fluxsteel holds the flux steady.

pages.t: A still retort loses not a single part: everything that breaks down reaches the Alembics, with no murk and no silt. It distills a thing a second, like a bright one. But in a murky chunk time stands in it: while the murk there is a third of the bed or more, the retort stands still and does not burn its fuel — clean the place and it runs on its own. The Stillness has no murk, so the retort runs there; its Alembics need still bands.

The heart of the retort is the Still Casing: two shells of stillmetal around a frozen drop. A Confluence makes it (a middling one): a block of stillmetal in the middle, a Hubstone, two stillmetal plates and an Hour Dial on the plinths, Still, Lattice and Tempo in the vessels. The Hubstone gives the casing its spoke of Fray and returns without it: decay leaves the retort for good.

kp: Стылая реторта Still Retort Стылый кожух Still Casing Стылая реторта Still Retort
nodes.hint: In a still casing time stands — and nothing is lost. Study the Bright Retort and Stillmetal.

pages.t: Panning doubles your ore: in a furnace, concentrate gives two ingots where the ore would give one. In raw ore the metal is mixed with waste rock. A Sluice Box parts one from the other: water entering its upper edge washes away the light, and the heavy settles at the brass riffles as black sand — concentrate.

A sluice box faces the way the water drains. It needs water at its upper end — a source or a flow — and somewhere for it to drain off the lower end. Ore goes in by hand or by a hopper from above and the sides; concentrate comes out by an empty hand or a hopper below. Raw iron, gold, copper and antimony wash — and the same raw ores of other mods.

kp: Промывочный лоток Sluice Box Железный шлих Iron Concentrate
nodes.hint: Water carries off the waste rock — the heavy stays. Read raw iron.

pages.t: A Druse Vat grows shards from distillate — no caves, no pickaxe. It is a vat of blown glass. Lay a block of shards on its bottom as the pattern. A siphon above fills it with distillate, and a druse grows on the pattern — shards of its current. Eight parts of the pattern's current and a little of the land's flux make one shard; on drained land the vat waits.

The vat takes a compound current too, if the pattern's current is in it: it splits it along the Wheel like a separator — the pattern's share stays, the rest goes to murk. Growing from a pure primal current is cheaper. Take the grown shards with an empty hand or a hopper below; sneak with an empty hand to take the pattern back.

kp: Друзный чан Druse Vat Друзный чан Druse Vat
nodes.hint: Shards can be grown from distillate — after a pattern.

pages.t: Current grit makes an Atomizer's cloud last longer and seasons food: whoever eats it gets the effect of its currents. Lay a shard of a primal current on the ground and drop an anvil, sand, gravel or a dripstone point on it: the shard crumbles into three pinches of current grit. Grit carries its current like a shard — only finely.
A pinch of grit in an atomizer's nozzle makes its cloud last twice as long — for one puff. The nozzle holds sixteen pinches; grit poured in does not come back out.

Food can be seasoned at a crafting table — up to three pinches. Whoever eats it gets the currents' effects: Ember wards off fire, Tide lets you breathe underwater, Gale makes you fall slowly, Strata hardens, Lattice lends spare health. Pinches add up on the Wheel, as in the Crucible: Gale with Tide is Drift, Ember with Lattice is Gleam; opposite Springs hiss and lose half, yet Tide with Ember still gives Bloom — healing. A water cauldron washes the seasoning off.

A drop of distillate seasons food too: lay a distillate vial beside the food at a crafting table — it gives one part of its current and stays on the grid one part lighter. That is how currents with no grit of their own get onto food. Echo grants Keen Hearing; Halo grants half a minute of Hush if you eat without moving; Mind leaves a note for the chapter of the seasoning's second current — at most three per chapter; Murk clouds your sight and leaves a Ripple in your mind.

kp: Grit and Seasoning Крошка и приправа
nodes.hint: A shard can be crushed — by weight.

pages.t: A bright retort distills without murk: what is lost goes into silt, not into the land. Reforge a fluxsteel retort in brightsteel: it distills just as fast and loses the same twelfth. With a Settling Vat nearby the loss settles there, and without one, in a box under the retort's own hearth. Take the silt in the retort's window, crouching with an empty hand, or by hopper from below; when the box is full, losses go to murk again.

kp: Ясная реторта Bright Retort Ясная реторта Bright Retort
nodes.hint: Brightsteel holds no murk — nor does a retort of it.

pages.t: A wootz retort not only makes no murk but adds: the place's currents yield extra parts in distillation. Reforge a bright retort in wootz. Each part of a current that is among the place's currents has a one-in-five chance to give another — for one flux of the chunk; when the chunk is drained there is no bonus. The Loupe reads the place's currents when aimed at empty air.

kp: Булатная реторта Wootz Retort Булатная реторта Wootz Retort
nodes.hint: The pattern of wootz remembers the currents of the place.

pages.t: Reforge a wootz retort with freshet steel: a thing breaks down twice as fast, and its losses, as with the bright one, settle as silt, without murk. And while the chunk's flux is above the bed — by a Spring, by a river at full moon — every part of any current gives one more with a chance of one in two, for a unit of the surplus flux; the retort never touches the bed.

kp: Вешняя реторта Freshet Retort Вешняя реторта Freshet Retort
nodes.hint: Freshet steel remembers the flood.

pages.t: The Counterflow is a weapon of distillate: the jet wounds and acts by its current, and against the opposite Spring it strikes half again as hard. It is a hand pump on a vial of distillate: keep the vial in your other hand or in your inventory. Each squeeze presses out one part, and the jet flies in an arc: Ember guards against fire, Drift hastens, Gloom blinds.

Counterflow: when the jet's Spring is opposite the Spring of the creature's leading current — Tide against a fiery beast, Ember against a drowned — the blow is half as strong again, and a pinch of murk sinks into the ground beneath the target, as with a clash in the Crucible. A loupe tells the target's leading current.

nodes.hint: A pump that shoots distillate.

pages.t: Veil Varnish hides armor from the eye: the protection and enchantments stay, and the look is yours. Brew Gloom and Prism in the Crucible over a gentle heat and throw an empty vial in last — two vials of Veil Varnish come out. Gloom hides, Prism lets light straight through.

Lay a piece of armor next to a vial of varnish at a crafting table: once coated, it is not seen on its wearer — on you, a creature or an armor stand. Protection and enchantments stay. The varnish hides from eyes, not from the flux: whoever wears diviner's spectacles or holds a loupe sees the armor as it is. A water cauldron washes it off.

kp: Лак-вуаль Veil Varnish Лак-вуаль Veil Varnish
nodes.hint: A varnish that hides armor from eyes, not from the flux.

pages.t: Caustic Brine is a trap and a breaker at once: creatures die in it with shards on top of their drops, and things thrown in melt into shards of their primal currents. Brew Ash, Brew and Fray in the Crucible and throw an empty bucket in last — it floats up full of Caustic Brine. The brine eats into everything living that steps in; a creature that dies in it gives shards of the primal currents of its table and vials of the compound ones.

A thing dropped in the brine melts pinch by pinch: its primal currents drop out as shards, with a share of luck, the rest goes to murk. Dissolving spends the brine — now and then a pool turns into plain water. Shards, grit and distillate vials do not melt in it.

kp: Ведро едкого рассола Bucket of Caustic Brine Ведро едкого рассола Bucket of Caustic Brine
nodes.hint: A liquid that dissolves the living and things. Read rotten flesh.

pages.t: Seeding Brine hurries a crystal farm: seeds next to its pool grow faster. Brew Prism, Lattice and Tide in the Crucible and throw an empty bucket in last — it floats up full of Seeding Brine. Pour it next to crystal seeds: those within two blocks of the pool grow faster.

The brine makes no flux: it hurries growth only with the flux above the bed. On drained land, and by a river running level with its bed, it does nothing; in a brimming place the seeds ripen before your eyes.

The Seeding Bed shows how to keep the brine from spreading and let it reach every seed: a brine source in a masonry basin, seeds on its rim. The brine tries seeds no farther than two blocks from its source, four tries at a time, so the more seeds around it, the more often a try finds one. It must be a source: flowing brine grows no seeds.

kp: Ведро затравочного рассола Bucket of Seeding Brine Ведро затравочного рассола Bucket of Seeding Brine
nodes.hint: A brine that makes crystal seeds grow faster.

pages.t: Current pods are a current from the garden bed: the seeds grow in their own place, and the Crucible dissolves a ripe pod into its current. Throw wheat seeds into a Crucible where Root and any current are boiling, and Seeds of that current float up. Root teaches the seed to grow, the current what to become.

Current seeds grow on farmland, but only where their current — or both of its parents — flows in the land: Drift by a river, Rime in the snows. Elsewhere the crop stands still and takes no bone meal. A ripe crop gives pods: thrown into the Crucible, a pod dissolves into its current. Seeds of different currents look alike — hold Shift in a window and runes show on the icons.

Crossing gives seeds of a combined current straight from the garden bed, without a Crucible. Plant crops of two currents that combine on the Wheel side by side: Tide and Ember give Bloom, Strata and Lattice give Prism. When a ripe crop is harvested and its partner is ripe next to it, on any of the four sides, one time in six Seeds of the combined current drop with the harvest. Whether they grow here is up to the land, as with every current crop.

kp: Семена течения Current Seeds Стручок течения Current Pod
nodes.hint: A current can be grown. Read wheat seeds.

pages.t: Keen Hearing shows sounds: a ring of ripples spreads from every source nearby, and you can see where a sound comes from. Brew Echo and Brew in the Crucible and throw an empty bottle in last — a Potion of Keen Hearing floats up. The rings the drinker sees are the color of Echo.
A sound that is too loud deafens: after an explosion nearby the rings vanish for a few seconds. The potion also suits an atomizer — as a cloud on everyone standing in it.

nodes.hint: Sound can be seen. Read a note block.

pages.t: The Cradle of Currents is a creature farm without a pen: it casts a creature from its imprint out of distillate of its currents. Three lumps of clay in a row make two raw Imprint Tablets. Press a tablet to a living creature: the creature is unharmed, and the clay dries with its imprint. Hosts, guardians and people give no imprint.

The cradle is made by Confluence from a Brewing Tower, terracotta, clay, an egg and gold. Set the tablet in its head and pour the distillate of the creature's currents from above — as much as the loupe hears in it. In the dark the cradle casts it at its foot.
No more than six of a kind stand near a cradle. The cast remember no life and give no experience. Every birth leaves a pinch of murk in the land: a farm needs a Purifier.

kp: Оттисковая табличка Imprint Tablet Колыбель течений Cradle of Currents Колыбель течений Cradle of Currents
nodes.hint: A creature's currents can be poured. Study the Brewing Tower and read a Snarl.

pages.t: Speculum is the metal of optics and casings: bronze bands and mirrors, pendants and watches, Dam armor, the Gauge Rod and automaton hulls are made of it. An antimony regulus alloyed with copper gives a bronze so bright you can see yourself in it, as in a mirror. There is no magic here: three copper ingots and a regulus are mixed into a charge on a crafting table, and the charge is smelted in a furnace.
Speculum goes into optics and cases: the Flux Workbench rolls ingots into sheets — three ingots, three sheets. Nine ingots pack into a block and part again.

kp: Шихта зеркальной бронзы Speculum Blend Слиток зеркальной бронзы Speculum Ingot Лист зеркальной бронзы Speculum Sheet Блок зеркальной бронзы Block of Speculum Слиток зеркальной бронзы Speculum Ingot
nodes.hint: Copper and antimony — bronze brighter than a mirror. Read copper.

pages.t: The Crucible brews the game's potions — the same ones a brewing stand makes, but from currents: no stand, no blaze powder and no special ingredient for each potion. Brew and the current of the effect in the distillate, a glass bottle thrown in last — and a potion floats up. One bottle per throw.

Brew is in nether wart, fermented spider eyes and antimony reguli. The current of the effect is the same one that acts when you eat it as a seasoning: Drift — swiftness, Tide — water breathing, Gleam — night vision, Prism — invisibility, Wing — leaping, Rime — slowness, Bloom — regeneration, Spark — strength, Hollow — weakness, Venom — poison, Ash — harming, Gale — slow falling. Two parts of each; gentle heat only: at a strong boil the potion curdles.

Stronger means more of the effect's current: four parts instead of two give the second level, lasting half as long. Slowness and the Turtle Master: the strong form is its own, and its card stands next to the potion. No second level: night vision, invisibility, fire resistance, water breathing, weakness, slow falling, wind charging, weaving, oozing, infestation.

Longer means Tempo: two parts of Tempo and the potion lasts nearly three times as long. Tempo is in clocks; a Mixing Vat puts it together from Drift and Lattice. No long form: healing, harming, wind charging, weaving, oozing, infestation.

A potion to throw takes Blast: two parts of Blast (gunpowder gives it), and a splash potion floats up. Two more parts of Weave make it lingering: the cloud stays in place, and arrows tipped in it on a crafting table carry the effect. Weave is in enchanted books and bottles o' enchanting.

Of the recipes that fit the brew, the Crucible brews the most demanding one: a stray current changes the potion. An antimony regulus gives clean Brew; nether wart also carries Ember and Root, a fermented eye — Venom and Sense. Watch the distillate with the Loupe and drain what is extra. A Brewing Tower brews potions by itself: strike it with the potion you want — it will remember it — and feed it glass bottles as the catalyst.
Life and strength: healing gives health back at once, regeneration bit by bit, strength adds to every blow.
Protection: with fire resistance, fire and lava do no harm; the Turtle Master takes blows but slows you. The strong one raises both levels and lasts just as long.
For the road: swiftness to run faster, leaping to jump higher, slow falling to come down from any height unharmed.
To see and breathe: night vision brings light into dark caves, invisibility hides you from eyes, water breathing lets you live underwater.
Against enemies — brew them as splash potions: harming wounds at once, poison bit by bit, weakness softens an enemy's blow.
To hold: slowness drags an enemy down. The strong one is the fourth level at once, not the second, and brief.
Aftermath potions act when the one they touched dies: wind charging throws everything around back in a gust, weaving leaves cobwebs.
Oozing leaves slimes behind after death; infestation lets silverfish out when the one it touched is hurt. They are thrown at enemies.

A stand and a Crucible brew the same things by different roads: a village herb woman put remedies in water, a fluxionist puts in currents. Nether wart steeps water with Brew — which is why a stand brews nothing without it.

nodes.hint: The Crucible brews the game's potions from currents. Read nether wart with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Crucible also brews what a brewing stand cannot: haste, resistance, absorption, health boost, dolphin's grace, luck — effects the world gives only through a beacon, a golden apple or a raid. The price is murk: every such potion leaves a share of murk in the land by the Crucible.

Brew, levels and forms are as with every potion: stronger is twice the lead current, longer is Tempo, to throw is Blast, a cloud takes Weave as well. The murk price is written under every recipe. No second level: bad luck, mining fatigue, glowing, the Hero of the Village, conduit power, dolphin's grace, blindness, nausea, darkness. No long form: saturation, levitation, the Hero of the Village, hunger, withering, darkness.
Work and grit: haste to dig and chop faster, resistance to take less damage, absorption for hearts beyond your own.
Health and fullness: health boost raises your limit of hearts, saturation feeds you at once — fullness without food.
The sea: dolphin's grace to swim fast, conduit power to breathe, see and dig underwater. Conduit power murks twice as much.

Luck — Halo and Want: the world's current carries you to what you want, and rare finds in structure chests turn up more often. Halo is rare — shards and crystals of currents give it; the second level takes twice as much.
The Crucible brews the Hero of the Village weaker than a raid gives it: the first level for two minutes — Kin, Want and Ward — with twice the murk.
For enemies — brew them as splash potions: bad luck takes luck away, mining fatigue weighs down the arm with the pick, blindness puts out the sight.
More for enemies: nausea makes the view swim, hunger eats fullness away, withering blackens hearts and wounds.
Darkness dims the light in waves; glowing outlines a target — it shows even through walls; levitation lifts into the air, but briefly: a long rise would kill on the fall.
Not brewed: Bad Omen — an ominous bottle gives it, and the raid and trial omens follow from it; the Breath of the Nautilus — the same water breathing, and a nautilus gives it.

The Reckoners held that every effect is a current, and every current can be poured into a bottle. The world does not argue with them, nor does it forgive: what it gives only for labor comes out of the Crucible with murk.

nodes.hint: Potions no brewing stand makes: haste, resistance, luck. Read a golden apple, a beacon or a totem of undying.

pages.t: A Spring tincture makes you its current for three minutes: Gale jumps two blocks high and glides, Ember does not burn and swims in lava, Strata cannot be moved, Tide swims and breathes underwater. Each guise has its own weakness. A Crucible brews the tincture over gentle heat: Brew 2, the Spring 4 and Soul 2, a glass bottle last.

Gale: almost half your weight is gone — you jump two blocks high and, running, twice as far; you fall softly and take no damage (crouch to drop fast); your blows throw enemies farther. The weakness: you are blown back harder yourself. Gale is kindred on peaks under the open sky and foreign underground.

Ember: fire and lava do no harm, burning goes out by itself, in lava you see as with fire resistance and swim as in water; your blow sets an enemy alight for 4 seconds. The weakness: water quenches you — in water and rain you take damage every second. Ember is kindred in the Nether, in deserts and in lava, foreign in the rain.

Strata: no blow or blast can move you, you dig half again as fast, your skin is like stone (+4 armor). The weakness: weight — 15% slower, and you sink in water: you cannot swim up, so walk out along the bottom and the shore. Strata is kindred in caves, mountains and underground, foreign high in the sky.

Tide: you swim like a dolphin, your air does not run out underwater, water does not cloud your sight, and you dig there unhindered. The weakness: on dry land you are a quarter slower, unless you are in water or rain. Tide is kindred by rivers and seas, in water and rain, foreign in deserts and the Nether.

Drink a tincture while a guise lasts and the currents meet on the Wheel. Neighbors blend: Gale and Tide make Drift (a quarter faster, steps up a block, swims like a dolphin; but slides as on ice), Strata and Ember make Alloy (+8 armor, does not burn, cannot be moved; heavy and sinks), Ember and Gale make Spark (+3 to blows, quicker strikes, faster running; but burns out twice as fast).

Tide and Strata are neighbors with no blended current: the guise simply changes. Opposites — Tide and Ember, Strata and Gale — clash as they do in a Crucible: the guise tears apart in steam or dust, the tincture is lost, murk sinks into the ground and your sight ripples. A blended guise holds only its own two tinctures: any third Spring is opposite to one of them.

A guise grows stronger where its current is the current of the place: in a kindred place it is half again as strong and lasts twice as long, in a foreign one it is weaker and wanes twice as fast. The place is what the Loupe reads in the air and what you stand in: water and rain are Tide, lava and fire are Ember, stone overhead is Strata, height is Gale. The guise medallion in the corner shows the time and the place.

While a guise lasts it takes a little flux from the chunk; where flux is below a quarter of the riverbed, the guise has nothing to breathe and wanes. A guise ends by itself, by another tincture or with the Shed Guise key. After it, for half a minute, no tincture can be drunk: the current in you must settle. Six minutes in a row in a guise and your sight begins to ripple.

The Reckoners argued whether a fluxionist flows himself. One of them drank Gale and walked a stair of wind for half a day; the records say he came back heavier than he left, and never drank Strata again.

kp: Настой Порыва Gale Tincture Настой Жара Ember Tincture Настой Пласта Strata Tincture Настой Прилива Tide Tincture Настой Порыва Gale Tincture
nodes.hint: Drink a current and become it. Read a glint, a blaze or a breeze with the Loupe.

pages.t: A Swirl herds without leads: while a redstone signal reaches the bowl it pulls creatures in or drives them away. Use it to bring animals into a pen, set calves apart from the herd, gather villagers in a trading hall or keep monsters off a door.

The radius is half the signal strength, up to seven and a half blocks; a spiral of Drift shows on the ground to the edge of the circle, turning inward or outward. Sneaking, empty hand — pull or push. An Imprint Tablet in the front socket — the Swirl takes only its kind; an empty hand on the tablet takes it out. An empty hand on the bowl picks by age: everyone, adults only, the young only.

The Swirl never touches players, masters, guardians or automatons, nor creatures on a lead or carrying a rider; what a Totem of the Fold holds it cannot drive out of that circle. It pays the chunk's flux for every creature in the circle while it works; when the ground has nothing to pay, it stops. Without a signal it sleeps.

nodes.hint: Flux water can pull the living. Read a cow or a sheep.

pages.t: The Flux Workbench crafts everything an ordinary one does, and flux recipes besides: instrument parts, devices and the fluxionist's gear. They are paid for with the flux of the land under the workbench and the currents of the place. A pinch of quickdust on a crafting table — and the oak darkens, veins of flux run through it, bronze binds its corners, and the crafting grid turns into the Wheel of Currents.

In the middle of the Wheel lies the grid, and around it six sockets for shards: the four Springs in the order of the Wheel and the two Poles, Lattice above and Fray below. To the right are the bowl where the thing appears and the lens-vessel with the flux of the place, the same as the Loupe's: what the craft will draw shimmers on the flux itself. What you lay out stays on the workbench when you step away.

A flux recipe asks for more than things — it needs the currents of the place. Tide flows by rivers, Strata in mountains and caves, Ember in deserts and the Nether, Gale everywhere, and Lattice is rare: it flows in the snows. The socket of a current that flows here glows in its color.

What the place lacks, a shard from its socket provides — one per craft. But such crafting is rougher: a borrowed current settles into the land as murk. Where to work is the fluxionist's choice: by a river, in the mountains, or with a store of crystals.

Crafting draws flux from the land beneath the workbench, and it seeps back by itself — from the bed and from the land around. Below the bed floor crafting takes nothing. In a drought, shards come to the rescue: each is set flux, eight measures of it, clean, without murk.
The first things the workbench gives are parts for instruments: drives that turn on flux, a coil, glass backed with antimony and a prism that splits a beam of flux into currents.

kp: Простой привод Simple Drive Сложный привод Compound Drive Токовая катушка Flux Coil Посеребрённое стекло Silvered Glass Делительная призма Splitting Prism Верстак тока Flux Workbench
nodes.hint: Crafting that draws flux straight from the land. Read a clock and something keen with the Loupe — a compass, a carrot, your own Loupe.

pages.t: The spectacles show what a Crucible, a vessel or a device holds — with no Loupe in hand: your hands stay free for the work. Diviners of old sought water with a willow fork; a fluxionist wears spectacles: opal lenses in a brass frame with a flux coil on the bridge. Look through them at a Crucible, and what it holds rises as a bowl of runes. To everything else the spectacles keep quiet: the flux of the land, the bed and the currents of things are the Loupe's work.

The spectacles cannot read: new currents, notes and entries still come only from the Loupe. But your hands are free and your view is clear: while you look at nothing in particular, the spectacles show nothing — and at a crucible that is worth a lot.

kp: Очки лозоходца Diviner's Spectacles Очки лозоходца Diviner's Spectacles
nodes.hint: To see what is in a Crucible without taking up the Loupe.

pages.t: A Firefly Lantern lights the dark corners around it by itself — no torch on every wall. Fireflies live behind its panes — clots of living Gleam. When dusk falls they fly out one by one and settle as little lights wherever it is dark: in corners, under stairs, in the caves around. At dawn they fly home.
Their light is as bright as a torch's, yet you can see it: warm sparks that quietly flicker. Gleam is made of Ember and Lattice — and that is what the lantern asks of the place.

kp: Светлячковый фонарь Firefly Lantern Светлячковый фонарь Firefly Lantern
nodes.hint: A lantern whose fireflies settle in dark corners. Read Gleam — in a torch's light, in glowstone.

pages.t: Float lanterns are light on the water: set them from the bank straight onto the surface, and a pond or a canal glows in sixteen colors. Fluxionists cast no candles: honeycomb wax goes into a raft, and above it sits a lantern of colored paper.
A float needs Tide: by a river or the sea it costs nothing, in a dry place it takes a Tide shard.

kp: Оранжевый фонарь-поплавок Orange Float Lantern Оранжевый фонарь-поплавок Orange Float Lantern
nodes.hint: Wax lanterns that float on water.

pages.t: A Catchment gives a Flux Workbench the flux of nine pieces of land instead of one: costly recipes no longer drain the workbench's own spot. Flux does not stand still: underground it runs in veins, like water. A Catchment is a stone well where the veins of all the land around drain together; set it beside a Flux Workbench.

The Catchment takes more where the land is fuller and dries the country evenly instead of draining the nearest piece to the bottom. The flux in the well is a gauge: high means the land around is full, at the very bottom it has run dry. Above the well hangs a diviner's pendulum of opaline; when the workbench crafts, the veins run to it.

nodes.hint: A well where the veins of flux from all the land around drain together.

pages.t: A Flux Reservoir is a store for a drought: it hoards flux while the land is full and gives it back when crafting, a device or a Conduit drains it. The fluxionists' Leyden jar: a jar of silvered glass in a foil of fluxsteel, with a ball on its rod. While the land of its chunk is full, the jar skims the top of the flux; in a drought it pours its store back, like a reservoir.

A Flux Workbench draws on the Reservoirs in its land at once, right after the land itself: costly crafting becomes possible even in a dry place. How much the jar holds shows in the segments of the window in its foil; the Loupe and the spectacles show the number — the flux in the jar reads as Halo, the flux of the world. A broken jar gives its store back to the land.

kp: Хранилище тока Flux Reservoir Хранилище тока Flux Reservoir
nodes.hint: A jar that hoards flux while the land is full and gives it back in a drought.

pages.t: Fluxsteel tools cut like diamond and work faster in land full of flux; the armor speeds up a workshop's devices. The flux of the land you work in runs through the steel: a pickaxe, an axe, a shovel and a hoe go faster in a full chunk and drag in a dried-out one; a sword strikes quicker there too. They wear out sooner than diamond.

Fluxsteel armor is workshop wear: flux runs off it into the devices nearby, and a Reservoir, a Charging Basin and the rest take and give it faster. The steel conducts: walking, it gathers static — from half full sparks run over it; in the full armor crouch twice and the static leaps in arcs at the three nearest foes. Lightning strikes such armor harder, but fills the static at once.

kp: Флюкс-стальная кирка Fluxsteel Pickaxe Флюкс-стальной топор Fluxsteel Axe Флюкс-стальной меч Fluxsteel Sword Флюкс-стальная лопата Fluxsteel Shovel Флюкс-стальная мотыга Fluxsteel Hoe Флюкс-стальной шлем Fluxsteel Helmet Флюкс-стальная кираса Fluxsteel Chestplate Флюкс-стальные поножи Fluxsteel Leggings Флюкс-стальные сапоги Fluxsteel Boots Флюкс-стальная кирка Fluxsteel Pickaxe
nodes.hint: Tools and armor of a steel the flux of the land runs through.

pages.t: A Charging Basin charges things that hold a store of flux — the Grapnel and others — with the flux of the land. The basin fills with flux like a font with water, but never below the bed floor. Lay such a thing in it: it rises over the flux and drinks until it is full — thin streams run into it, the flux in the basin sinks and rises again.
Take the thing out with an empty hand. Fluxsteel armor nearby makes it drink faster. How much flux is in the basin, the Loupe and the spectacles show as a Halo rune.

The Flux Ruling Pen never runs dry for good: it draws channels at the Reckoning Desk and circles on Flowstone like a plain Ruling Pen, but drinks flux instead of ink. Put an empty one in a Charging Basin — a division per flux, ninety-six divisions when full. With it in your inventory the Loupe writes Hour Marks without a sheet of paper: a mark costs a division.

The Flux Trowel builds a structure to its ghost by itself. Place a ghost from a schematic in the Codex and press Build — with the Build Structure Ghost key, the button on the schematic or a right-click with the trowel in hand: the blocks in your inventory fly to their places on threads of flux, from the bottom up. It never breaks other blocks; it names what ran short, and the ghost waits. A block costs a unit of charge, a full trowel holds ninety-six. It lays four blocks a second and one more per step of Finesse. In creative a ghost builds without it.

The basin gives distillate too — to a thing whose charge is a current rather than flux: the Prism Rod drinks Prism. Run a siphon into the side of the basin (the thing floats above it) from a vessel of Prism and the rod fills by itself, no vial in hand: one part per step of the siphon, until it is full. The basin takes no other current and gives the siphons nothing. How much is in the thing, the Loupe writes under the basin's name.

Mod armor holds a charge of flux, and its features spend it: double-crouch moves, the vow and the wards, keen hearing, rime on the plate, the pattern's answer. How much is left shows in the Gear Charge row right above your armor: cells split by piece — helmet, cuirass, leggings, boots, belt, trinkets; a piece that runs dry dims and blinks its sign. An empty set is plain armor: its protection and flaws stay, its features sleep until it is topped up.

Living land tops up the armor you wear by itself, a little at a time: a unit every four seconds while the flux of the chunk is above the bed floor. A drained chunk, a Toll Tap and the Stillness do not — go there full. Faster is this basin: a piece of armor fills in it in seconds. A new piece comes full. What a set spends its charge on, the piece's tooltip tells, and whether the chunk tops you up — the Loupe under its flux vessel.

kp: Подзарядная чаша Charging Basin Токовый рейсфедер Flux Ruling Pen Мастерок тока Flux Trowel Подзарядная чаша Charging Basin
nodes.hint: A basin that things holding a charge of flux drink from.

pages.t: The Grapnel lifts and carries you: wherever the hook catches, the cord pulls you there — up a cliff, across a chasm, to a cave ceiling. A three-pronged hook on a fluxsteel shank, its cord on a drive-reel. Throw it — wherever it catches on stone or wood, the cord reels you there while the Grapnel is in your hand. Once there, you hang under the hook, and the cord slowly slips down. Use it again to let go.
A throw costs charge: the Charging Basin fills the Grapnel. An empty Grapnel only clicks.

nodes.hint: A hook on a cord: wherever it catches, it pulls you there.

pages.t: A Cascade is a threshold for a redstone signal: it passes it on only when it is no weaker than the threshold, and gives a strength of its own. It is carved from slate like a garden waterfall: the signal enters from behind and fills the left steps — as much as is poured, so strong it is. When the water reaches the bronze weir it spills to the right and runs down to the peg, and from the spout in front comes a signal as strong as where the peg stands.
Use it to set the threshold a step higher; sneak-use to move the peg. Everything shows on the steps themselves: what came in, where the threshold is and what goes out.

nodes.hint: Steps that a signal runs down like water. Read Spark — in redstone dust, in a comparator.

pages.t: An Ear Trumpet turns sound into a redstone signal: a note block playing its note or a bell within ten blocks sets a mechanism going. An old brass ear trumpet on a dark oak stem, with an opal membrane in place of an ear: sound runs down the throat and touches it, and it quivers and glows.
Use it to tune the trumpet a semitone higher — it sounds its note. Sneak-use flips the little lever: "pulse" gives a signal for a moment, "toggle" turns it on and off with every sound.

kp: Слуховая трубка Ear Trumpet Слуховая трубка Ear Trumpet
nodes.hint: A trumpet that hears a note and a bell. Read Echo — in a bell, in an amethyst shard.

pages.t: A Fish Trap gathers things from the water on its own: whatever floats within four blocks, the current carries to its mouth. It is woven from weeping willow switches, and over its mouth a lure stamped with the Tide rune hangs on a little rod. Whatever touches the trap lies down in it, and the funnel won't let it back out.
You can see the catch through the switches. Take it with an empty hand; a hopper under the trap empties it like a chest.

kp: Верша Fish Trap Верша Fish Trap
nodes.hint: A wicker trap that water itself carries things into.

pages.t: An Updraft is a lift and an air chute: a stream of wind carries creatures and things up, sideways or down, wherever the mouth faces, up to ten blocks. A vent of windslate, and in its bronze mouth a whirligig of eight feathers on an opal hub: Gale flux spins it, and a visible stream blows from the mouth — to the first obstacle.
Chain Updrafts into an air chute: where one stream meets another, the second carries on. In a rising stream, sneak to sink. A redstone signal stills the Updraft.

kp: Восходящая тяга Updraft Восходящая тяга Updraft
nodes.hint: A stream of wind that carries things along it. Read Wing — in a feather, in a firework rocket.

pages.t: A Chart Table shows the flux around as a map: where it is full, where drained, where flooded or murky — and where to set a workshop. Parchment is stretched on a dark oak table, and an opal alidade lens on a brass arm sweeps above it; a chart of the nine by nine chunks around rises on the parchment: deep turquoise is full flux, pale sand is dried out, gold is a flood above the bed, a violet bloom is murk.

Strokes show where the flux flows — toward the neighbor that has less — and drops run along them. The table's own chunk is framed in gold. North on the chart is north in the world. Where to set a workshop and a Catchment is clear at a glance.

kp: Стол лоции Chart Table Стол лоции Chart Table
nodes.hint: A live chart of the flux all around. Read Halo — the flux of the world, in a shard or in quickdust.

pages.t: A Flux Forge smelts ore three at a time, faster than a blast furnace and without coal — on the flux of the land; it has work of its own too: recycling worn metal, opaline and flowstone. Build a cube three blocks to a side: copper at the eight corners, a Magma Block at the heart, a Copper Grate in the middle of the front — the tap grate — and in the middle of the top — the throat; Flowstone Bricks everywhere else. A pinch of quickdust on any of its blocks — the copper binds the masonry, veins of flux show in the seams, and the magma wakes as the heart of the forge.

Throw ore onto the top of the forge or feed it into the throat with a hopper: the forge melts three things at once, faster than a blast furnace, and gives the result out of the tap grate — into a chest or hopper set in front of it, or onto the ground if the way is free; behind a wall the result waits inside for pipes. Break any block of the forge, and it falls apart into what it was built from.

By itself the forge grants no luck: without additives there are no extra ingots. Instead, with every third ore Current Slag runs into the tap grate — dark glass that remembers its ore. Dissolve it in a Crucible, and the ore gives up its currents. If the land runs dry, the forge smolders and waits for flux.

The forge also has work of its own that no furnace knows. Worn-out metal — a sword, a pickaxe, mail, horse armor — flows again: the forge gives back nuggets, less than half of what went into the thing, and fewer still from a worn one. Enchantments do not pass on, the work takes twice as long, and every third thing leaves Slag that remembers it. What was bought from a villager the forge melts like a furnace: into one nugget.

An opal nodule opens whole in the heat of the forge and gives two layers of Opaline — a furnace takes only one. Dripstone grew drop by drop, Flowstone grew in a stream: the forge drives the flux of its land through a Dripstone Block, and veins rise in it. This spends flux generously.

Additives are currents in the forge: more from ore, faster smelting, tempered gear. Pour them by a siphon over the top or a vial on the forge: up to 32 parts of each (four vials), a part for every item.
More from ore — Prism: raw ore gives one more three times in four (2 parts; a stack becomes nearly 1¾), an ore block always (3 parts; a stack becomes two). No luck for concentrate or scrap.
Faster — Ember, a part per item: twice as fast, up to four times with bellows.
Wind for bellows — Gale, a part per item: the bellows blow as on Gale and can blow iron; where Gale flows, each adds another third of the pace.
More metal from scrap — Edge, 2 parts per item: 60% of the recipe metal, not 45%. Bought gear still gives one nugget.
Flux to the land, not Slag — Gleam, a part per ore or scrap: instead of Slag, up to 4 flux to the land, never more than the forge took.
A cleaner chunk — Halo, a part per item while the chunk is murky: each item clears a unit of murk.
A gamble — Ember with Tide, a part of each per ore: half the ores give triple, a quarter double, a quarter is lost and fouls the chunk; on average like Prism.
Cheaper gems — Prism with Gleam: a gem ore block always gives one more for 2 Prism and 1 Gleam, not 3 Prism.

Sturdier gear — Rime, 4 parts per item: an iron, gold, copper or fluxsteel tool or armor piece comes out of the forge whole instead of as scrap, with a quarter more durability than usual. Only once: tempered gear comes out as it went in. While Rime is in the forge, such things are not melted — they wait to be tempered.
Hardening — Rime with Ember together: heat, then cold, as a smith does it — half again the usual durability, for one more part of Ember.
More experience — Mind, a part per item: smelting ore and anything furnaces smelt gives twice the experience.
Master's memory — Mind with Edge: enchanted scrap gives back its enchantments' experience, as a grindstone would — a part of Mind per item.
Scrap and tempering twice as fast — Tempo, a part per long item: long work fits into an ordinary cycle.
Smelting on dry land — Strata, a part for every 2 flux an item takes: the forge drinks land from the vial and takes no flux from the chunk. Gleam then has nothing to give back to the land.
A vein — Strata with Prism: Strata gives the ore back its stratum, and raw ore and ore blocks alike always give one more for 2 Prism.

kp: Опалин Opaline Струйчатый камень Flowstone Горн тока Flux Forge
nodes.hint: A kiln three blocks to a side that burns flux instead of coal. Read the air of the Nether — in any of its valleys.

pages.t: A Gale Fan speeds up a Flux Forge — three bellows make it three times faster — and only with it does the forge blow iron into fluxsteel. Carved boards of old oak and folds of oxhide; at the nose, a copper pipe with an opal bead. Set the bellows with their nose into a tuyere — the copper socket in the middle of a side or the back of the forge — and they breathe by themselves: Gale of the place pumps them. Each Gale Fan adds two thirds of the forge's own pace.
Where Gale does not flow, the bellows have nothing to breathe — they pump at half strength.

Bellows speed up a retort too: set a Gale Fan with its nose into the side or back of a retort (the front is the firebox door), and the hearth distills faster — each fan by two thirds on Gale of the place, by a third without Gale; up to three fans. Less fuel goes to each thing. How many fans blow and how much faster, the Loupe writes under the retort's name.

Only bellows on Gale blow through iron: the wind of the place passes through the melt, and the flux of the land enters the ingot. Nearly half the metal burns off as scale; the rest comes out as Fluxsteel Nuggets. Where there is no Gale, the ingot waits in the charge.
The forge with three bellows is on the diagram: the bellows at the tuyeres, nose to the forge; in front is the tap grate where the result comes out. "Place ghost" sets them in the world.

kp: Поддув Gale Fan Самородок флюкс-стали Fluxsteel Nugget Поддув Gale Fan
nodes.hint: Bellows that fan the Flux Forge and a retort's hearth.

pages.t: The Fluxionist's Garb makes crafting and casting cheaper: the thread in the weave catches the flux that the Flux Workbench and the Conduit would spill. Wool stitched with a thread of fluxsteel is flux cloth; sewn into clothes, it barely protects, but it spares: the coat an eighth of the flux, the trousers a little less, the boots less still; Diviner's Spectacles do too.

Thrift adds up, but never past half: crafting on the Flux Workbench and casting with the Conduit never cost less than half the price. It does not spare the shards paid for the currents of the place. The flux thread also damps spells — potions of harming, witches, an evoker's fangs: a tenth for each piece — and keeps murk off: Clouding and Silting last shorter, and on the whole garb they do not take hold.

The garb takes dye like leather armor: put it with a dye on a crafting table — the cloth takes the color, while the brass, the leather and the flux thread stay their own; the coat, the trousers and the gaiters of the boots are dyed apart. A cauldron of water washes the dye out.

kp: Ткань тока Flux Cloth Сюртук флюксиониста Fluxionist's Coat Штаны флюксиониста Fluxionist's Trousers Башмаки флюксиониста Fluxionist's Boots Сюртук флюксиониста Fluxionist's Coat
nodes.hint: A coat, trousers and boots of cloth with a current in it.

pages.t: The Molder makes a crafting table recipe by itself, after your template — once a second, on the flux of the land. It is a press-mold of dark oak bound in bronze. Set it between two containers: raw goods above, the place for the finished below. The press strikes, and the product and leftovers — the empty bucket from milk — drop below. Each costs one flux of the land.

Use it to open its template plate: touch a cup with an item and its imprint stays in the bronze, while the item stays in your hand. An imprint is a pattern: oak planks in the template will take spruce ones too if the recipe accepts any. The cups with imprints glow on the Molder's face. A redstone signal stops the press.

nodes.hint: An apprentice that crafts a recipe from your template. Read Craft — in a book and quill, in a smithing template.

pages.t: A Flux Mill feeds the machines of other mods with the flux of the land: set it beside them, and they need no generator of their own. A stream of flux runs down the flume, turns a small wheel, and a copper coil in a bronze shroud makes from the flux the power those machines understand. One flux makes eight hundred of its units, up to forty a moment.

The mill pushes power into the machines and cables beside it and gives it to those that draw it themselves. With no one to take it, the wheel stands still and the flux of the land is not spent; below the bed floor the mill takes nothing.

kp: Мельница тока Flux Mill Мельница тока Flux Mill
nodes.hint: A wheel that the flux of the land turns — for other folk's machines.

pages.t: A towpath speeds your way and carries things by itself, and a boundary keeps monsters and automatons behind a line. A towpath is paving of deepslate flags with a channel in the middle; Drift flux runs along the channel. Whoever walks with the current is carried faster than running; whoever walks against it bogs down. Things float along by themselves. Lay it with the channel pointing where it should flow; a sneaking walker stands firm.

Boundary stones are set in pairs — at one height, in one line, no farther than sixteen blocks apart. Between them a boundary stretches — a veil of Ward two blocks high. To monsters and automatons it is a wall, while people, animals and things pass through it: a boundary keeps an automaton in its yard. A Grapnel hook catches on it. Take a stone away and the boundary fades.

kp: Towpath and Boundary Бечевник и межа
Бечевник Towpath Межевой камень Boundary Stone Бечевник Towpath
nodes.hint: A road that carries you itself, and a boundary no monster crosses.

pages.t: A stencil puts the rune of any current on a banner and a shield — the mark of your workshop. Fluxionists weave no banners of their own — they mark others'. Put the stencil in a loom beside a banner and a dye: any of the forty-two runes of the Wheel goes onto the cloth, and from a banner onto a shield. The stencil is not used up.

kp: Трафарет руны Rune Stencil Трафарет руны Rune Stencil
nodes.hint: The runes of the Wheel — for a banner and a shield.

pages.t: A block of shards stores nine shards in one place and serves as the pattern for a druse vat. Nine shards of one current, packed tight, fuse into a block — and part again into nine. The block glows softly and keeps its current within; there are blocks of the six primal currents only.
A block of shards is the pattern of a druse vat: laid on its bed, it teaches the vat which shards to grow.

kp: Блок осколков Прилива Block of Tide Shards Блок осколков Прилива Block of Tide Shards
nodes.hint: Nine shards fuse into a block. Read any current shard.

pages.t: A Shard Lantern shows the flux without a Loupe: the fuller the land, the brighter it burns — a lantern on a workshop wall tells at once whether the land needs a rest. The shard burns in its own color: above the bed it shines, on drained land it dims.
An opaline lamp holds an orb behind opaline tracery. Walk around it — the light shifts like the play of colors in opaline.

kp: Фонарь осколка Shard Lantern Опалиновая лампа Opaline Lamp Фонарь осколка Shard Lantern
nodes.hint: A light that shows the flux. Read a firefly lantern.

pages.t: A current circle works a field on its own: it waters, tills, feeds, reaps and replants, draws dropped things in, carries things along — which of these, the currents in its three sockets decide.
1. Lay nine flowstone bottom slabs as a 3 × 3 square — level, not in water.
2. Run a ruling pen over the middle slab: the circle spreads over all nine, its arrow pointing the way you face. It costs 24 divisions of ink.
3. Put shards of primal currents or distillate vials into the sockets — right-click any slab of the circle.

Twenty-five slabs, 5 × 5, make a great circle: 48 divisions of ink, and it works two blocks wider; a great Through-Circle leads between worlds too. A small circle grows into a great one if you lay sixteen more slabs around it and run the ruling pen over it: the items in its sockets stay. The land's flux decides how far any circle works: on drained land two blocks, in a flood five.

Tide waters farmland, if Tide flows in the land. Three Strata till the ground. Bloom and Root feed the crops. Edge and Root reap the ripe; with a third socket of Lattice they reap and replant. Three Hollows draw dropped things to the circle.

The sockets add up along the Wheel: two currents that make a third are read as it too. Gale with Tide is Drift: such a circle carries things and small creatures the way its arrow points. Every deed takes the flux of its chunk, but never below the bed's bottom. The Loupe reads a circle and says what it does; sneak with an empty hand to take a socket back, sneak with a ruling pen to erase the circle. Break any slab and the circle falls apart, the socket items dropping at its middle. An old one-slab circle has faded: lay slabs around it and run the ruling pen over it — it grows and keeps its items.

nodes.hint: Currents in the sockets of a circle work a field. Read a flowstone slab.

pages.t: A Crystal Tapper harvests shards by itself: it cuts a grown crystal back and lets it regrow — by full land, a harvest without end. It faces a current crystal with its chisel and cuts it back to a large bud: the shard goes into the box behind it, and the land pays two flux for the cut. The bud grows back on its own, on the land's flux.

A tapper takes only the surplus: in a chunk whose flux is below its bed, it stands still. Putting one in a dry place is pointless — by a river or a willow it works tirelessly. A redstone signal stops it.

kp: Подсочник Crystal Tapper Подсочник Crystal Tapper
nodes.hint: A crystal can be tapped like a tree. Read a current crystal.

pages.t: A Wellspring pours flux back into the land: set it in a dry place or by a drained workshop, and the Flux Workbench, the Conduit, Confluence and the devices around it work at full strength again. Feed it Halo distillate from a siphon above: one part of Halo is four flux in the chunk. The land fills up to one and a half beds, and the surplus flows to the neighbors — a Wellspring waters the whole neighborhood, not just one chunk.

A Wellspring cannot hoard flux: above one and a half beds it waits until the land gives the surplus to its neighbors. Crystal nests grow by a Wellspring — on the flux above the bed. A Wellspring makes no murk: it is a stone basin, and its surface glows from within while the spring runs.

nodes.hint: Flux can be poured into the land. Read a bottled glint or a skein.

pages.t: Brightsteel is the metal without murk: devices made of it lose silt rather than murk into the chunk; the bright retort, band and prism, the Crystal Tapper and the bardiche are made of it. Lumenash cleans the murk around it, and its charcoal keeps that gift: throw a lumenash log into a Flux Forge, and out comes lumenash charcoal, ash-silver, with golden embers in its cracks.

Lay lumenash charcoal and a fluxsteel ingot in the forge: the charcoal draws the stagnant flux out of the steel, and a brightsteel ingot and a pinch of silt come out of the chute, and the chunk grows a little cleaner. In a murky chunk — where murk is above a third of the bed — there is no annealing: the ingot comes back out as fluxsteel. Without charcoal, too.
Brightsteel holds no murk: devices of it lose their waste as silt, not as murk in the chunk. Brightsteel sheets and a Splitting Prism make a Bright Prism — it splits without murk.

kp: Лист ясной стали Brightsteel Sheet Ясная призма Bright Prism Блок ясной стали Block of Brightsteel Слиток ясной стали Brightsteel Ingot
nodes.hint: Fluxsteel with its stagnant flux drawn out. Read lumenash.

pages.t: The bardiche takes trophy heads: a full-strength finishing blow sometimes takes the head of the fallen — a zombie, a skeleton, a creeper, a piglin, a player. It is a crescent of brightsteel on a lumenash haft: slow, and it does not sweep.

The bardiche learns in the hand: every foe it fells adds to its mastery, and with mastery heads fall more often — from one in ten to every second. Mastery lives in the thing itself and goes with it from hand to hand.

nodes.hint: A long axe for the trophy-hunter. Read somebody's head.

pages.t: A spindle carries a skein to a new place — to the workshop, the Conduit, the Flux Workbench. Hold a spindle on a skein: a small one winds in two seconds, a large one in six, and the threads come off onto the spindle. Use a wound spindle on a block face to unwind the skein — native threads stay native. Every rewinding costs an eighth of each thread: it goes to murk.

A greedy skein snaps the thread — feed it first. A turbulent one would burst — calm it with Lattice first. A still skein will not wind: its threads stand still. A skein unwinds no closer than three blocks to another — and closer than four, neighbors merge. A burnt or blown-up spindle snaps its skein: every thread goes to murk.

nodes.hint: A skein is not shut in glass — it is wound, like yarn.

pages.t: Your own workshop wherever it suits you. A dense skein is opened with an Embroidery Hoop — inside it is a Bower, a small world to build in. Its ground, sky and flux are the threads of the skein: a skein of Ember gives warm ground and Ember of the place, a skein of Tide gives water and drizzle. Wind more — the Bower grows; carry the skein on a Spindle — the whole workshop goes with it.

A skein opens once it holds ninety-six shares or more: a medium one three quarters full, or a large one. Hold the hoop on the skein for three seconds — the threads stretch onto it, the hoop goes into the skein and becomes its key. Whoever opened it is the owner. A greedy skein tears the hoop, a turbulent one would burst, a still one does not stretch.

To enter, hold the open skein with an empty hand for two seconds — the threads wrap around you and draw you in. A Loose End hangs from the sky of the Bower: hold it, and you come out where the skein hangs. The owner moves the Loose End with the hoop on a face of the ground. Guests are invited with the hoop on a player; guests enter while the owner is inside.

The side of the Bower follows the greatest winding: ninety-six shares give sixteen blocks, one hundred twenty-eight give twenty-four, a full large skein gives forty-eight. A Bower grows but never shrinks: what you built stays. Each new band of ground takes the nature of the threads at the time — the Bower changes ring by ring, while the sky, the light and the drizzle always follow the threads. Its edge is the Winding: nothing passes through it.

The bed of a Bower comes from its threads: the more shares, the more flux for your devices. The currents of the place are the threads of the skein holding eight shares or more: the Flux Workbench, the Crucible and the Brimming Jug see them. Murk settles here as anywhere: a careless Bower grows murky, and after five minutes of murk its skein does too.

Your workshop will not be lost. Draw the threads below the threshold — the Bower sleeps until you tie more on. Destroy the skein — it furls into a Furled Skein: fire, lava and blasts do not take it, and it never vanishes from the ground; unwind it, and the Bower is back, everything as it was. Whoever was inside comes out where the skein hung. Lost it entirely — call the Bower back with the hoop and Shift on a fresh dense skein of the same leading thread. Only you can erase your Bower: the hoop with Shift on the Loose End — and confirm.

kp: Пяльцы Embroidery Hoop Пяльцы Embroidery Hoop
nodes.hint: A dense skein opens inward — into a workshop that goes wherever you go.

pages.t: A merged skein is bigger: two small skeins merge into a medium one, two medium into a large one — and a large skein grows a bigger Bower, up to forty-eight blocks. The Swift merges a neighbor in a minute, the Skein Bowl keeps a skein apart. Even without them, skeins side by side live with each other: they share threads, merge, cloud and hollow each other.

Neighbors are skeins within seven blocks of each other. Every ten seconds a skein arcs a share of the thread it holds more of to a neighbor — along an arc with a running bead. The threads spread until they even out. The last share of a native thread stays; an opposite Spring never arcs into a skein whose Lattice cannot hold it — turbulence does not spread. Under the Loupe, quiet threads to every neighbor show.

Closer than four blocks, neighbors twine around each other for five minutes — two strands, tighter and brighter — and merge. The one with more shares draws the other in; a hungry greedy skein always does, and the merged skein stays greedy unless it is sated. The absorbed skein brings its threads less an eighth of each, and what does not fit goes to murk. No more than three threads stay native. Murky and lucent cancel each other out — the result is steady.

Every half a minute a murky skein arcs a share of Murk to each neighbor — even to a full one, which then loses a share of its own. When Murk is a sixth of a steady skein, it turns murky in five minutes. A hungry greedy skein draws threads from all its neighbors, and a thin skein beside it turns greedy itself in five minutes. A lucent skein burns Murk away; the Loupe shows how long is left.

The Skein Bowl keeps a skein apart: place it under the skein or beside it, within three blocks. Its skein neither arcs nor takes, never merges, its neighbors' murk and hunger do not reach it, and a turbulent one chafes half as often. With an empty hand switch it to "takes in": the skein draws from its neighbors and gives nothing. Keeping costs two flux every ten seconds, taking in — five; in a drained chunk the bowl holds nothing. While it keeps, a woven sphere rises around the skein, the bowl's eye watches it, and neighbors' arcs strike the sphere and fizzle out; taking in, the sphere warms and lets arcs pass inward.

Place the Swift by the skein that should grow, within three blocks. Its skein draws two shares every ten seconds from each neighbor within seven blocks and merges with the nearest in a minute, without coming closer — and it is always the one that draws the other in. The Swift costs ten flux every ten seconds while it reels and sixteen per merge. It does not reel Murk and leaves a skein under a Skein Bowl alone. While the reel turns, its skein spins up: the threads run faster and faster, at full speed by the merge.

A skein with a Bower shares threads like any other but never merges by itself: only the Swift of the Bower's owner or a guest merges it, and it is the one that draws in — the Bower grows with the new winding. Two skeins with Bowers never merge. A skein cannot be unwound closer than three blocks to another; between three and four they will merge.

kp: Клубочница Skein Bowl Мотовило Swift Мотовило Swift
nodes.hint: Skeins side by side share threads and merge into one. The Swift merges them, the Skein Bowl keeps them apart.

pages.t: Through-Mirrors carry things: what goes into one comes out of the other — in the next room, across the world or in the Nether. They are the mail of a workshop: ore from the mine comes to the chest at home by itself, and what you gather on the road does not fill your inventory. One Confluence gives two mirrors. Hang one and right-click it with the other — the second remembers the first; place the second anywhere — they are a pair.
