Throw a thing into the glass and it goes; a hopper or a pipe feeds the mirror by itself. What arrives goes into the chest, barrel or hopper the pair hangs on (sneak to hang a mirror on one), and if there is none — it comes out of the pair's glass. A send costs the flux of the sender's chunk — five hundredths of a unit per thing (a little over three for a stack), a quarter at the least — and leaves no murk. If the pair's land is not loaded, the things wait in its glass — up to nine stacks — and come out when its land wakes.

A mirror is yours: sneak and right-click it with an empty hand to open it to guests or close it. A broken mirror loses its pair; placed again, it stands alone until it is tuned again. In the Stillness the glass freezes — nothing flows there, save on thawed ground. The Reckoners kept such pairs at their sluices: tally tablets went from weir to weir without a line getting wet.

A Pocket Mirror sends what you hold in your other hand into a Through-Mirror — from anywhere: right-click a mirror with it and it will look into that one. It costs more than mirror to mirror: one unit of the flux of the chunk you stand in, a tenth of a unit per thing, one unit at the least. By Confluence it deepens into the Deep Mirror (the Stillness chapter). Next: "Linked Vessels".

The Ender Mirror is the same thing tuned another way: sneak and right-click an Ender Chest with a Pocket or Deep Mirror, and it will look into your Ender Chest. Then, in hand, it opens it from anywhere — in a mine, on the road, on a far shore: your Ender Chest is the same behind every ender chest anyway, and the things in it are yours. Each opening costs half a unit of the flux of the chunk you stand in (above the bottom of its bed); in the Stillness the glass freezes. Right-click a Through-Mirror with it, and it looks into a mirror again.

kp: Сквозное зеркало Through-Mirror Карманное зеркальце Pocket Mirror Сквозное зеркало Through-Mirror
nodes.hint: A pair of mirrors that carries things anywhere. Read a portal — to the Nether or to the End.

pages.t: A Linked Vessel keeps one level of distillate with its pair, wherever the pair stands: pour into one and it flows into the other until both are even. So the store of a workshop reaches the Confluence altar at the other end of the house, with no siphons through the walls. It is no warehouse: the two hold as much as two plain vessels — the level is shared, not multiplied.

Pair them like Through-Mirrors: right-click a lone vessel with another and place it. One current flows: if the vessels hold different ones, the level stands still, and the Loupe says why. It flows two parts every quarter of a second, each part costs five hundredths of a unit of flux of the giving vessel's land, and only while the land of both is loaded. Siphons, brand, seal and spilling — as with a vessel; a sealed one does not share.

kp: Сообщающийся сосуд Linked Vessel Сообщающийся сосуд Linked Vessel
nodes.hint: Two vessels that share one level of distillate.

pages.t: A Hothouse Lantern makes crops, saplings and berries around it grow faster, day and night: every three seconds it pushes one plant within four blocks a stage on, and its warm light keeps crops from sleeping. Feed it Root distillate from a siphon above: a stage costs half a part.

A Nesting Lantern breeds animals without hand feeding: every ten seconds it brings together an adult pair of one kind within six blocks, for two parts of Fang from a siphon above. It leaves the young, those resting after a litter and the untamed alone.

A farm does not grow without end: a kind that has twelve head in the circle is not bred, and with thirty-two animals around nothing is. The Hothouse Lantern leaves the fluxionist's own crops — Current Crops and Still Rye — alone: they keep their own rules of growth. A broken lantern gives what it holds back to the land as murk.

kp: Тёплый фонарь Hothouse Lantern Гнездовой фонарь Nesting Lantern Тёплый фонарь Hothouse Lantern
nodes.hint: Light can grow and pair. Study Confluence and read seeds or an egg.

pages.t: A Stamp Mill stamps shards of the six primal currents into Current Grit without dropping anvils — and more generously: four pinches a shard instead of three. Three pestles strike in time, one after another, and every third blow crumbles a shard. Shards go in by hand or by a hopper above or at the side; the grit comes out by an empty hand or a hopper below.

Cog distillate turns the cam shaft: a siphon above pours it into the brass cup on the beam, a part per shard. While there is a shard in the trough, Cog in the cup and room in the box, the rune band on the shaft glows and the mill thumps; when one runs out, it stops.

kp: Толчея Stamp Mill Толчея Stamp Mill
nodes.hint: Grit can be stamped in time. Read a primal current shard.

pages.t: A Biome Converter grows a new place around itself. Feed it distillate and the land's flux, and everything within 128 blocks of its tower slowly becomes the chosen biome: other ground and grass, other trees and flowers, other creatures, its own color of water and sky. The growth spreads in a circle from the heart with a soft edge; where the place has grown it is real — F3 shows it, and its creatures are born there.

Build a 3×3 tower four blocks tall and set the heart — the Place Seed — in the middle of the chamber's lower tier, niche toward you. Sprinkle Quickdust on the built tower: it folds into one device — a greenhouse of a place with a glass chamber and an opaline druse on its crown; only a folded tower grows. Reach through the niche or click any part with an empty hand to open the window: the places it can grow, the feed of the chosen one, and the course. Break any part and the tower turns back into blocks, each returned as it was laid.

The feed is Shift and two currents of the new place that the tower's place lacks: the window names them with runes. The heart draws them itself from vessels and Gyres within six blocks, or by a siphon from above through the crown; the flux comes from the land under the tower, never below the riverbed's bottom. What is missing, the window and the Loupe tell in a line.

Numbers. A dose of each feed current grows 8 cells of the place (128 blocks²); a cell costs another quarter of a flux; the place grows no faster than one and a half cells a second. The full circle is about half an hour of fed work and about three hundred doses of each current.

What changes and what does not. Old trees dissolve into flux without a splinter, and trees of the new place take their spot; so do grass and flowers. The new place covers the whole circle — under the tower and under buildings too. Buildings are left alone: a column whose top is not a natural block stays as it was, while the ground right next to it changes; crops and saplings stay, and so does a tree that touches a building; claims hold. It grows only in the Overworld. Break the heart and the growth stands, what has grown stays. Restore drives the growth back to the heart on Shift alone: the native ground, trees and flowers rise again. Two Converters never quarrel: a cell belongs to the one that grew it first.

Everything in the world is frozen flow, and a place is the slowest of all. The Reckoners measured it without touching; the fluxionist who grew the first islet in a glass chamber understood that a place can be retuned like a string. Shift blurs the land's old current, the currents of the new place give it another — and everything that grows and lives on it grows anew.

kp: Преобразователь биома Biome Converter Преобразователь биома Biome Converter
nodes.hint: A place can be grown anew. Study the Wellspring and Confluence and read the grass under your feet.

pages.t: The Shard Satchel spares you the fuss with the sockets of the Wheel: carry your shards with you, and a Flux Workbench whose socket is empty takes the shard straight from the satchel in your inventory — a little satchel shows by that socket in the window. The workbench spends what lies in its sockets first, then the satchel.

Six pockets — one for each Source and Pole, up to 128 shards in each: the satchel is not bottomless. Use it in hand and every such shard in your inventory goes in. In the inventory it works like a bundle: shards onto the satchel go into a pocket; a right click takes out a stack of the fullest one.

kp: Сума осколков Shard Satchel Сума осколков Shard Satchel
nodes.hint: A satchel the Flux Workbench takes its shards from.

pages.t: A glyph is a current cast in stone. Three glyphs in a current circle make the circle work: keep monsters out, heal, keep dropped things, smelt, call a comparator or take you to another circle — and thirteen more rites in their own entries, from the weather and ores to bringing your things back.
1. Cut glyph blanks from flowstone on a stonecutter — four from a block.
2. Gather 4 parts of the current you need in a Crucible.
3. Drop the blank into the Crucible last — the glyph of that current floats up.
What circles of three glyphs do:
Ward, Lattice, Gleam — a ward circle: monsters do not come into the circle.
Bloom, Soul, Tide — a healing circle: heals people, animals and villagers in the circle.
Three Echoes — a watch circle: a comparator by the slab reads how many living things are in the circle.
Three Stills — a still circle: things dropped in the circle do not vanish.
Alloy and two Embers — a smelting circle: smelts things thrown into it without coal, but leaves murk.
Shift, Drift, Bind — a Through-Circle: takes you to its paired circle (its own entry).

A circle of glyphs alone works a block farther. Rites wake only to glyphs: shards and vials are good only for the field. Every deed takes the flux of its chunk, and a redstone signal on the slab puts any circle to sleep — that is how a lever turns a rite off.

A still circle keeps up to sixty-four things; it does not touch what is kept forever already. A smelting circle smelts by furnace recipes, one thing at a time in its furnace time, with experience; each thing costs two flux of the land and a little murk — heat without a forge is rougher than a Flux Forge — and what came out is not smelted a second time.

The Reckoners' type foundries cast letters for their tally boards; a fluxionist casts them from distillate: the blank sinks in the Crucible and rises as the sign of a current, and its ink no longer washes off.

kp: Заготовка литеры Glyph Blank Литера течения Current Glyph Заготовка литеры Glyph Blank
nodes.hint: A current can be cast in stone. Read a distillate vial.

pages.t: Two circles — an entrance and an exit: stand on one, crouch, and you are on the other, wherever it is. Great circles (5 × 5) lead even to the Nether and the End.
1. Lay nine flowstone bottom slabs as a 3 × 3 square and run a ruling pen over the middle one — that is a circle (the entry "Current Circles"). To step to another world, lay twenty-five, 5 × 5.
2. Set Shift, Drift and Bind glyphs in its three sockets, one each (the Crucible casts them — the entry "Current Glyphs").
3. Where you want to arrive, draw a second circle like it and set Shift and Drift in it.
4. Right-click the first circle with one more Bind glyph — it remembers that circle. Set it in the third socket of the second circle — the circles are paired.
5. Stand on either one and crouch: a second and a half later you are on the other.
The cost is the flux of the land you leave: 4 and 1 more for every 100 blocks, 16 at most; 24 between worlds.
After a step the circle rests for 5 seconds.

A small circle (3 × 3) leads within its own world. Between worlds — the Overworld, the Nether and the End — only great circles (5 × 5) lead, at both ends. Circles do not lead in the Stillness, the Lees or the Quickstream: they have their own ways.
Your pets standing on the circle come with you. A circle does not carry things or other creatures — Through-Mirrors are for things.
Someone else's circle is closed. The owner is the one who set the last glyph: crouching, they right-click the circle with any glyph to open it to guests.
If the far circle is erased, undone or blocked, you stay where you are, and no flux is spent.

The Reckoners walked between their sluices like this: two circles on two weirs, and the keeper stepped over the river without wetting his feet. A circle does not hold the land on the other side — it comes for the moment of the step and falls asleep again.

nodes.hint: A pair of circles that carries you yourself. Read a Through-Mirror.

pages.t: Four circles for the workshop: they age the stone and copper of a building, dye wool, glass and concrete right in the wall, move enchantments from a thing onto a book and make furnaces work twice as fast.
Each is three glyphs in a current circle (the entry "Current Glyphs").
A circle of years ages the building around it: stone bricks and cobblestone grow moss and crack, copper turns green with patina — no moss in your inventory and no years of waiting.
Glyphs: Tempo, Fray, Strata. Any circle; a great one reaches farther.
Two blocks every 2 seconds, 0.15 flux a block. It leaves waxed copper, wood and soil alone.
A painting circle dyes the building with a dye thrown into it: wool and carpets, terracotta, glass and panes, concrete and concrete powder — right where they stand, and the sheep in the circle.
Glyphs: Prism, Shift, Craft. Throw a dye into the circle — one per 8 blocks, as at a crafting table.
Two blocks a second, 0.05 flux a block; up to six blocks above the circle. It does not dye beds, banners or shulker boxes.
A disenchanting circle moves an enchantment from a thing onto a book: a sword with Mending from a chest gives it to a book, and a book with three enchantments splits into books of one each.
Glyphs: Weave, Shift, Mind. Throw an enchanted thing and plain books into the circle — a book per enchantment.
An enchantment every 3 seconds, 2 flux per level and a little murk. Curses stay on the thing.
A hastening circle hurries furnaces: a furnace, blast furnace, smoker, brewing stand or campfire in the circle works twice as fast.
Glyphs: Tempo, Spark, Cog. A small circle hurries the two nearest, a great one four.
0.2 flux a second per furnace; fuel burns as fast too. It does not hurry spawners, beacons or the devices of flux.

nodes.hint: Circles that age, dye, lift enchantments and hurry furnaces. Read an enchanted book.

pages.t: Three circles for the farm: they pair animals up without feed, lure the herds around into your pen and call an animal that lives in this place.
A breeding circle: grown animals of one kind in the circle have young without feed — a pair every 5 seconds.
Glyphs: Bloom, Bloom, Fang. Keep the animals in the circle — with a pen or on a lead.
1 flux a pair — while the circle holds fewer than eight of the kind (twelve for a great one).
A luring circle calls the animals around: they walk to it on their own — up to four at a time, from 16 blocks past its edge (24 for a great one).
Glyphs: Want, Fang, Echo.
0.05 flux an animal. It does not call tamed, named or leashed ones: you cannot steal someone's herd. Nor does it lure an animal away from another luring circle.
A calling circle brings onto it an animal that lives in this place: on plains a cow, a sheep or a pig, in a place grown by the Converter — its animals.
Glyphs: Bloom, Echo, Halo. A great circle only (5 × 5). Stand on it and crouch.

10 flux and half a murk an animal, then the circle rests 30 seconds; with eight animals within 16 blocks it does not call, and by a Totem of Tally whose count is full no animal comes. It never calls monsters or water creatures.

nodes.hint: Circles for animals: breeding, luring and calling. Read a cow, a sheep or a pig.

pages.t: Four circles for earth and sky: they show the ores under them, lift you out of a mine to the surface, dry out water and lava and change the weather.
A dowsing circle listens to the ground: crouch on it, and the ore veins under it light up as signs through the stone for 30 seconds, in the color of their ore.
Glyphs: Echo, Strata, Want. A small circle hears 32 blocks down, a great one down to the bottom of the world.
4 flux (8 for a great one), then the circle rests 10 seconds. Only the one who crouched sees the signs; ores of other mods show too.
A rising circle lifts you out of a mine: crouch, and you stand on the ground straight above the circle, under the open sky.
Glyphs: Wing, Gale, Gleam. A small circle lifts up to 64 blocks, a great one from any depth.
2 flux and 1 more for every 16 blocks, 12 at most; a 5 second rest. It does not lift in the Nether and never sets you on lava or into a wall.
A draining circle: water and lava in and under it go up as steam, and waterlogged blocks dry — a pit on a pond floor, a dry way past lava.
Glyphs: Hollow, Ember, Gale. From three blocks above the circle down to 8 below it (16 for a great one).
Up to 8 places a quarter second, 0.03 flux a place, lava twice that. The sea flows back: the circle drinks flux as long as it works.
A weather circle changes the weather: crouch, and a clear sky clouds over with rain, rain turns to a thunderstorm, a thunderstorm clears.
Glyphs: Gale, Tide, Spark. A great circle only (5 × 5), and only where there is weather.
20 flux and 1 murk. The weather is the same for the whole server, so after a rite the sky is left alone for 2 minutes.

kp: Rites of Earth and Sky Обряды земли и неба
nodes.hint: Circles that hear ores, lift you out of a mine, dry things out and call the weather. Read an ore.

pages.t: Two circles that remember: one puts back what was broken in a building, the other brings back your things if you die far from home.

A memory circle guards a building: crouch on it, and it remembers the blocks around; if a creeper blows up the wall or someone breaks a window, the circle puts them back, taking blocks from a chest by the circle.
Glyphs: Mind, Still, Lattice. The chest goes under any slab of the circle or right against its edge.

2 flux to remember, 0.3 a block, a block a second (two for a great one); from the block under the circle to six above it. It never places chests, doors or beds, and never breaks a block someone set in a gap. Rebuilding? Put the circle to sleep with a lever or crouch on it again.
A recall circle: die anywhere, and the things in your inventory and what you wear do not fall where you died — they wait at this circle and come out of the ink when you walk up.
Glyphs: Soul, Bind, Drift. A great circle only (5 × 5). Stand on it and crouch — it remembers you.
6 flux to bind, the things come free. You are bound to one circle; an erased circle drops the waiting things where it was. Experience and things with the Curse of Vanishing do not come back.

nodes.hint: Circles that remember a building and you. Read a recovery compass or a lodestone.

pages.t: A totem lays a law on a place: in its circle something never happens — a creeper does not explode, fire does not spread, an enderman does not teleport — or something always does: a sprout grows even in the dark. Sixteen totems — sixteen laws.
1. Make a Totem Blank on the Flux Workbench.
2. Gather 8 parts of the totem's current and 4 of Lattice in a Crucible.
3. Drop the blank in last — the totem of that current floats up.
4. Set the totem down: its law holds in a circle of 8 blocks.
You can always see where a law ends:
look at a totem with the Loupe in hand — its circle shows on the ground;
right-click a totem with an empty hand — the circle stays until you click again;
hold a totem — you see its circle where it would stand and the faint circles of all totems nearby.
Crouching with an empty hand, the owner changes the radius: 4, 6 or 8 blocks. A Gauge Crown on top adds 12 and 16, rims on the crown add 24 and 32.
A redstone signal puts a totem to sleep — that is how a lever switches a law off.
A law over a whole homestead — rims on the crown. A Far Rim on a totem wearing a Gauge Crown raises its radius limit to 24 blocks, a Horizon Rim on top of it — to 32.
Click a rim onto your totem: the Far Rim first, then the Horizon Rim. A broken totem drops its crown and rims, each once.
A wide law costs upkeep on top of the price of events: 3 flux a minute at 24 blocks, 7 at 32.

A totem pays with the flux of its chunk for every event it holds; laws that hold all the time pay a little every second. It leaves no murk. When the land has less than one flux above the riverbed floor, the totem falls asleep: its rune goes dark and the Loupe says "Dry". Six totems in one drained chunk will sleep — set them by a river and a willow or spread them over chunks.

The Reckoners wrote the rules of places — where a current should stand, where it should flow — and carved them on posts. A post held one current on a tether. The Order of the Still Hour decided that holding the whole world was better — and so the Great Stilling came. A totem is the honest measure of the same thought: one current, a small circle, and only while the land pays.

kp: Заготовка тотема Totem Blank Мерный венец Gauge Crown Дальний обод Far Rim Обод окоёма Horizon Rim Заготовка тотема Totem Blank
nodes.hint: A carved post that lays a law on a place. Read a Boundary Stone.

pages.t: Five totems keep a house and a workshop safe:
Totem of Calm — creepers and TNT do not explode.
Totem of the Hearth — fire does not spread or eat the house.
Totem of Order — creatures do not carry blocks off or trample the beds.
Totem of Clear Skies — no rain, no snow, no lightning.
Totem of Thistledown — falls do not hurt.

In the circle of a Totem of Calm creepers do not explode: a creeper hisses, swells — and halfway the fuse fizzles out. TNT, ghast fireballs, beds and respawn anchors in the wrong world, and lens and weave blasts do not explode there either.

The creeper tries again — and fizzles again. Wind charges and breezes are a push, not a blast: the totem does not hold them, nor the blasts of bosses and guardians. TNT fizzles and is gone — the block does not come back.
Cost: 1 flux per blast.
A Totem of the Hearth keeps a wooden house safe: in its circle fire does not spread or eat blocks, and lava and lightning set nothing alight.

Fire away from a hearth goes out at once, hissing. Fire on a hearth — on netherrack, magma blocks, soul soil or soul sand — keeps burning but does not spread. Campfires, torches and furnaces burn as before.
Cost: 0.05 flux per fire put out.

A Totem of Order keeps creatures from wrecking your place: endermen do not carry blocks off or set them down, zombies do not break doors or crush turtle eggs, ravagers do not break leaves and crops, silverfish do not hide in stone, and rabbits and foxes do not eat the beds.
No one tramples the farmland in its circle — not even you. Farmer villagers, allays, snow golems and sheep on the grass do their thing: that is work, not wrecking.
Cost: 0.1 flux per thing held.
A Totem of Clear Skies keeps the weather off: over its circle no rain or snow falls and no lightning strikes. Endermen by the house stay dry, snow does not pile on the build, ice does not form.
Its column of law reaches the sky. Inside it is dry, and you hear the rain beyond the edge. Farmland by water stays wet as before, and a burning creature is not put out by rain.
Cost: 0.02 flux per second while the weather is bad.
In the circle of a Totem of Thistledown no fall hurts — not you, not animals, not monsters. Set it at the bottom of a shaft, where you land with wings, and in a pen animals fall into.
Hitting a wall on wings is not a fall: the totem does not hold it.
Cost: 0.05 flux and 0.02 more for every point of damage there would have been.

Тотем спокойствия Totem of Calm Тотем очага Totem of the Hearth Тотем уклада Totem of Order Тотем ясного неба Totem of Clear Skies Тотем пушинки Totem of Thistledown Тотем спокойствия Totem of Calm
nodes.hint: A law for the house: no blast, no fire, no wrecking. Read a creeper.

pages.t: Five totems keep a yard and a farm:
Totem of the Fold — animals do not wander off or vanish.
Totem of Concord — no one starts a fight.
Totem of Tally — no more creatures than the limit.
Totem of the Sprout — crops grow even in the dark.
Totem of Clean Ground — mire does not creep onto the garden.
A Totem of the Fold is a pasture without a fence: creatures in its circle do not step out and do not vanish, even a wandering trader.

You can lead an animal out on a lead, ride it or carry it in a cart. Monsters do not leave either, but they vanish as usual. Break the totem or put it to sleep, and three seconds later everyone is free.
Cost: 0.002 flux per creature every 2 seconds.

A Totem of Concord keeps the peace: in its circle endermen, bees, wolves, polar bears, zombified piglins and iron golems do not turn on you, piglins do not mind opened chests and mined gold, foxes and wolves leave the livestock alone, and players cannot hurt each other.
Anger waits beyond the edge: step out and it comes back. The totem does not hold the born malice of monsters — a ward circle and a Totem of Vigil are for that.
Cost: 0.2 flux per quarrel; a player's blow at a player costs nothing.

A Totem of Tally keeps a farm from choking the world: no more creatures live in its circle than three per block of radius — 24 at radius 8. Past that nothing is born: not from breeding, eggs, monster spawners or by itself.
The totem counts every 5 seconds; the Loupe shows how many creatures are in the circle and how many may be. Breeding past the limit gives no young — the love simply passes.
Cost: 0.1 flux per birth held.
A Totem of the Sprout makes a farm underground: crops, saplings, sweet berries and pumpkin and melon stems in its circle grow in darkness as they do in sunlight and do not wither without light.
They do not grow faster: a nourishing circle hurries growth. Where a Totem of Constancy stands nearby, nothing grows.
Cost: 0.02 flux per growth in the dark.

A Totem of Clean Ground holds the mire at the edge: it does not spread onto blocks in its circle even in a murky chunk — the garden and the pond by a dirty workshop stay clean while you set up a Purifier.
The totem does not clean the murk, and mire already in the circle rolls back by itself once the murk is gone.
Cost: 0.05 flux per thing held.

kp: Totems of the Yard Тотемы двора
Тотем околицы Totem of the Fold Тотем лада Totem of Concord Тотем счёта Totem of Tally Тотем ростка Totem of the Sprout Тотем чистой земли Totem of Clean Ground Тотем околицы Totem of the Fold
nodes.hint: A law for the farm: the herd, peace, measure, growth. Read a sheep.

pages.t: Five totems guard the approaches:
Totem of Vigil — night visitors do not come.
Totem of Keen Sight — monsters show through walls.
Totem of the Bulwark — shots from outside stop at the edge.
Totem of Silence — sculk and the warden hear nothing.
Totem of Mooring — nothing teleports.

A Totem of Vigil turns night visitors away: phantoms do not come for those in its circle, patrols do not find them, a raid does not start in the village, monster spawners stand still, and monsters are not born in the circle even in the dark.
The totem does not drive away those who came from outside — that is a ward circle's work. It does not hold trial spawners or cult raids: they have their own answer.
Cost: 0.5 flux per phantom or patrol, 2 per raid, 0.1 per spawner round, 0.005 per monster that did not appear.
A Totem of Keen Sight shows what lurks: monsters in its circle glow with an outline through walls for everyone within 32 blocks of the totem — the creeper behind the wall, the cave under the house.
The outline is the totem's color, pink like Sense.
Cost: 0.01 flux per monster in the circle every 5 seconds.
A Totem of the Bulwark is a shield against archers: arrows, fireballs, potions and snowballs shot from outside stop at the edge of its circle. From inside you shoot out as usual — a loophole.
Arrows and tridents drop at the edge, the rest fades in a puff. Shots of bosses and guardians pass.
Cost: 0.1 flux per shot stopped.
A Totem of Silence muffles the vibrations of its circle: sculk sensors, sculk shriekers and the warden hear neither steps nor chests nor blasts inside. Take it into an ancient city.
Players still hear everything. The warden still smells with its nose — do not come close.
Cost: 0.005 flux per vibration, at most twice a second.
A Totem of Mooring holds every jump in place: in its circle endermen and shulkers cannot teleport — they stay and fight — and chorus fruit and ender pearls carry no one in or out.
A pearl landing in the circle fades. A fluxionist's own ways — Through-Circles, mirrors, the Sluice Arch — go along the riverbed, not by a jump, and work as before.
Cost: 0.3 flux per jump, 0.5 per pearl.

kp: Totems of the Watch Тотемы заставы
Тотем бдения Totem of Vigil Тотем зоркости Totem of Keen Sight Тотем заслона Totem of the Bulwark Тотем безмолвия Totem of Silence Тотем причала Totem of Mooring Тотем бдения Totem of Vigil
nodes.hint: A law for defense: no visitor, no shot, no jump. Read an enderman.

pages.t: A Totem of Constancy keeps a place as it was built: in its circle nothing changes by itself — copper does not weather, ice and snow do not melt, leaves do not fall, grass does not creep, mire does not grow, crops, saplings and young animals do not grow.
By hand everything changes as before: build, break, plant and reap. Next to a Totem of the Sprout, constancy is stronger.
Cost: 0.02 flux per second.

kp: Тотем постоянства Totem of Constancy Тотем постоянства Totem of Constancy
nodes.hint: A place where nothing changes by itself. Read a Still Grain.

pages.t: A Memory Obelisk keeps your experience safe to the last point: put it into the stone and it is not lost when you die, nor spent on the steep prices of high levels. And while you are within eight blocks of the obelisk, the anvil, the enchanting table and the Reckoning Desk take their price from it, at the lowest price: your own levels stay with you.

Use the obelisk with an empty hand and its window opens. Put in a level or all of it, take out a level or all, or stand on the level you need — the obelisk puts in the surplus or makes up the lack itself. Glass Bottles fill into Bottles o' Enchanting: each costs seven points and, broken, gives exactly seven, with no luck either way. A Glass Bottle in hand on the obelisk fills one.

Prices in levels are cheaper low down: five levels from the fifth cost 55 points, from the fortieth — 875. The obelisk pays as if you stood on the lowest level that allows the price: a five-level repair at the anvil costs 55 points, the thirtieth-level line of the table — 306. That is what a careful crafter would do by hand, only without the fuss and without loss. If the obelisk lacks it, you pay yourself, as usual.

The obelisk holds a hundred levels — 30,970 points. Its owner is whoever set it down: they decide who else may use it — nobody, the trusted from a list, or anyone — and whether it pays for work nearby. Broken by hand, the obelisk carries its experience along; someone else's personal one does not yield to a pickaxe, and explosions do not take it. A comparator reads how full it is.

The Reckoners measured flux to the last part. Memory — the experience of the living — they took for the same flux, only set in whoever lived it, and they learned to lay it in stone like water behind a weir. The runes in the obelisk's groove fill with its pale gold from the bottom up: as much light, as much memory.

kp: Обелиск памяти Memory Obelisk Обелиск памяти Memory Obelisk
nodes.hint: A bank of experience that pays for you. Read a Bottle o' Enchanting or an enchanting table.

pages.t: When you cannot get a hopper to a furnace, chest or machine — a wall is in the way, neighbors took every side — set a Stand-in where there is room. Its faces act as the faces of another block up to eight blocks away: a hopper, pipe or Molder at the cabinet fills and empties that block as if it stood right against it.

Sneak-click a block with the Stand-in — it remembers the block and the face. Place it: each face of the cabinet continues the same face of the target — the top of a furnace takes ore, a side takes fuel, the bottom gives the result. Sneak-click a face of a placed one with a Stand-in that remembers something — that face now leads to the new block: one cabinet can serve up to six neighbors. Empty hand on a face tells where it leads; sneaking, it lets go.

It carries items, fluids and other mods' energy — a Flux Mill that pushes energy into the cabinet pushes it into the machine behind. It never carries distillate: that flows down the slope through siphons. The target must be in the same world, within eight blocks and loaded; a Stand-in never continues another Stand-in. A thread of flux runs from each linked face to its target — brighter with the Loupe or the Diviner's Spectacles; break the target and the thread snaps.

nodes.hint: A face can belong to another block. Read a hopper.

pages.t: A pair of Ferrystones swaps two places: on a redstone pulse everything in the three-by-three-by-three cube above one slab — blocks with their contents and creatures — trades places with everything above the other. A lift between floors, a hidden room, a workshop rolled in and out, a store you swap in.

Set the slab into the floor: the cube is above it, the slab is the middle of its floor. One Confluence gives two slabs; click a placed one with the other — it remembers it, and once placed they are a pair. A pulse at either slab swaps, no more than once every two seconds. Whoever stands on the slab and in the cube travels with it. The owner is whoever placed it; sneaking with an empty hand, they open it to guests.

Only within one world, and only while both ends are loaded. Each slab pays its own chunk's flux: a tenth for every block of its cube, four times that for a block with contents; no murk. Bedrock and anything unbreakable, spawners, portals, the mod's place-bound blocks and someone else's land do not travel; a cube edge must not cut a door, bed or chest in half. In the Stillness the slabs freeze.

nodes.hint: Two places can trade. Study the Reckoner locks and read their stone.

pages.t: A Canopy is a one-way floor: flux cloth stretched in a frame. Whoever stands on it — player, animal, dropped item — is held; from below and from the side you pass through and jump up onto it; sneak, and you drop through. Cover shafts with it, lay floors over farms (animals stay, you go down) and make steps you jump onto from below.
It is not a lift: a Driftway carries riders through its own landings, and an Updraft's stream stops at a Canopy as at a floor. The membrane glows with Halo and casts no shadow.

nodes.hint: A floor can let you through one way. Read scaffolding.

pages.t: A secret passage without doors: a wall of Seeping Masonry turns to water at its owner's word. Right-click it with a Conduit or give it a redstone pulse — the whole joined masonry, up to the sixty-four nearest blocks, weeps into standing flux water you walk and swim through. Once more — stone again.

The masonry's water does not flow anywhere and no bucket takes it; you cannot breathe in it, as in any water. It never sets on the living: whoever is inside is pushed out to free space, and if there is nowhere to go that block stays water. The masonry does not carry a redstone signal.

kp: Проницаемая кладка Seeping Masonry Проницаемая кладка Seeping Masonry
nodes.hint: Stone can turn to water. Read Flowstone Bricks.

pages.t: The Lined Satchel is 54 slots that are always with you — on a trek, in a mine, on a building site. Whatever doesn't fit in your inventory slips into it by itself, and the workshop takes from it as from your hands: the lens wheel sees the lenses in it, the Flux Workbench pays with its shards, the Strata Spade and the Flux Trowel lay its blocks.

Open the satchel with its key («Open Lined Satchel» in Controls) or use it in hand; the same key closes the window. With a slot mod it is worn in the back slot; without one it works from the inventory, and the first one counts. The window has two buttons: «Stack and sort» and pickup — turn pickup off if the satchel should only hold what you put in yourself.

The satchel goes into no satchel, shulker box or bundle, and shulker boxes and bundles don't go into it. Its things live in the satchel itself: it carries them into a chest, onto the ground and through death, and if it burns or blows up it drops everything it held. While its window is open, its slot in your inventory is strapped shut.

The lining is flux cloth quilted to the pattern of a skein's inner side. In a skein the same pattern folds a whole Bower; in a satchel it folds only a span, but a span is enough for the inside to be larger than the outside. Lay your hand on the lining: it is faintly warm and draws you in, like water under a jetty.

kp: Сума с подкладом Lined Satchel Сума с подкладом Lined Satchel
nodes.hint: 54 more slots on your back. Read leather or a chest.

pages.t: The Bundling Cord is for when a chest, a furnace mid-smelt or a workshop device has to move without being taken apart: use it on a block and the block is tied into a Bale with everything in it and its settings. Use the Bale where it should stand and the block stands as it was, turned to face where you look.

A Bale is heavy: while you carry it you walk slower and cannot carry a second one. It goes into no chest, satchel, shulker box or bundle, hoppers don't pull it in, and on the ground it doesn't vanish. A double chest, a bed and a door are tied whole.

A knot costs the chunk's flux — 0.5, a block with contents 2; the cord holds 48 knots and is mended with string on an anvil. Monster and trial spawners stay where they were found; bedrock, portals and frames, mirrors, circles, skeins and totems cannot be tied, nor can anything where you may not build.

kp: Увязка Bundling Cord Увязка Bundling Cord
nodes.hint: Moves a chest with its things whole. Read a lead.

pages.t: A Driftway is a fast lift for any number of floors in one shaft: from the cellar to the tower, a hundred blocks in two seconds, with no ladders and no fall damage. Set a Driftway Landing into the floor of each story — one above another in one column — and leave the shaft between them open: Drift will flow along it.

Stand on a Landing. Jump — the next floor up; sneak — the next floor down. Use the Landing with an empty hand and a sheet of all the floors of the shaft opens: click a floor to ride straight there, passing through the other Landings. Drift sets you down facing the Landing's exit — the side it was placed from. A name tag names the floor; a Landing renamed on an anvil goes down already named.

Drift takes the flux of the ground under the Landing: one for a ride and one more for every 64 blocks of the way; when the ground is dry, the Driftway stands still. The shaft is one column: a block with a shape in it splits the shaft in two, lava and fire close the way, and you cannot stand on a Landing with less than two empty blocks above it. A lone Landing does not glow — you can see it has no pair. Everyone rides at once, each where they chose.

River towns had a steep road from the landing up to the town: goods were hauled up it from the barges. A fluxionist's Driftway goes straight up, and Drift itself does the hauling — Gale and Tide at once, a wind that flows like water. A Landing is a slab of deepslate with an opal eye in a bronze ring: Drift flows through the eye, and to the one riding, the slab is not a floor but a veil.

kp: Пристань взвоза Driftway Landing Пристань взвоза Driftway Landing
nodes.hint: A fast lift for many floors in one shaft. Discover Drift, the current of motion.

pages.t: Flux wakes more than devices. Living decor glows, moves and breathes by itself: a ball of thread winds in a spindle, a current's flame burns without a blaze, a floatbell pulses in the water, a glint flutters in a cage, drops run down a curtain's threads, a pendulum swings for ever. All of it is made on the Flux Workbench for a pinch of flux.

A piece's color is a current. Click it with a distillate vial: the vial loses one part, the piece flares and takes any of the 42 currents. A broken piece keeps its color — that is how rows of different currents are gathered.
Thread Lamp — the main lamp of a house: a little ball of glowing thread winds itself in a spindle — five loops turn each about its own axis around a warm heart. Light 14.
Stands on the floor or hangs from the ceiling, like a lantern.
Current Brazier — a bright fire without a blaze: a flame of its current in stepped tongues in a bronze bowl, embers rising. It sets nothing alight. Light 13.
Goes on the floor; not under water. It crackles softly.
Floatbell — a living light in the air and under water: a bell of light pulses, its tendrils trail behind, and it drifts slowly in its block. Light 10.
Needs no support — place it anywhere, it stays in water: a lamp for ponds and aquariums. Breaks at a touch.
Glint Cage — a home for a glint: click a bottled glint on the cage and it flutters inside, now and then perching. Light 12, the color of the glint's current.
An empty bottle takes the glint back; a broken cage lets it go. Stands or hangs like a lantern. A vial drop does not recolor the cage: the color is the glint's.
Bead Curtain — for doorways and windows: threads with beads where drops of the current's light run down. Light 5.
Place blocks one under another — the curtain grows down as one sheet, a drop runs through every block. You walk through it — the threads part. A vial drop colors the whole column.
Tempo Pendulum — for tall halls: it swings for ever, its swing plane slowly turning — a full circle in six minutes; the bob is a ball of light with a fading trail. Light 9.
Hangs from the ceiling, one and a half blocks down.

Нитяной фонарь Thread Lamp Жаровня течения Current Brazier Плывун Floatbell Клетка огонька Glint Cage Капельный занавес Bead Curtain Маятник Темпа Tempo Pendulum Нитяной фонарь Thread Lamp

pages.t: A flux-worker's curios — for a table, a shelf and a study: the Wheel of Currents in miniature, a clock with flux instead of sand, a prism that splits light into the Sources, a book that turns its own pages, a whirlwind in a jar and stones floating over a plinth.

A piece's color is a current. Click it with a distillate vial: the vial loses one part, the piece flares and takes any of the 42 currents. A broken piece keeps its color — that is how rows of different currents are gathered.

Wheel Orrery — the Wheel of Currents in miniature: the four Sources circle the axle in Wheel order, the Poles slide along it toward each other, a hoop of the other currents turns the other way, and the Wheel's heart, a ball of light, glows above. Light 7.
Goes on a table or the floor. A vial drop colors the Wheel's heart.
Current Hourglass — a clock of the flux: glowing grains of its current pour in a thin stream — the top heap melts, the bottom one grows; after a minute the glass turns over by itself. Light 6.
Faces the one who placed it. Clinks softly as it turns.

Glimmer Prism — colored light for a hall: a cut opaline turns over a tripod, and its four glimmers — in the colors of the Sources — drift as spots over the walls, floor and ceiling up to 8 blocks around. Light 7.
The prism keeps its own colors: a drop does not recolor it.
Leafing Lectern — for a library or a study: the pages turn by themselves, lines appear in the ink of its current and signs rise above the book. Light 6.
Faces the one who placed it. The page rustles as it turns.
Whirl Jar — a curio for a shelf: a tiny whirlwind of its current spins in a glass jar. Light 6.
A row of jars of different currents makes a cabinet of curiosities.
Floating Runestones — for shrines and gardens: three little stones with glowing signs float over a plinth and circle slowly, each tied to it by a thread of the current. Light 7.
Goes on the floor.

kp: Living Decor: Curios Живой декор: диковины

nodes.hint: Things for a table and a shelf. Read an orb.

pages.t: For a yard, a garden and roofs: a fountain where arcs of a current spring, chimes of opaline, a pennant with a workshop's rune and a weathervane that catches the wind of the whole land.

A piece's color is a current. Click it with a distillate vial: the vial loses one part, the piece flares and takes any of the 42 currents. A broken piece keeps its color — that is how rows of different currents are gathered.
Current Fountain — for a yard, a hall or a garden: four arcs of the current spring from the spout and fall into a flowstone basin; rings spread over the glowing surface. Light 9.
Goes on the floor. It babbles softly.
Opaline Chimes — a hanging piece: opaline shards on twine turn and sway, and a face that turns to you flashes with opaline's play of colors. Light 4.
Hangs from a ceiling, a fence or a chain. Chimes now and then. Keeps its own colors.
Current Pennant — a sign for a workshop or a house: a pennant with the rune of its current — the same as in the Codex — waves on the wall. Light 3.
Hangs on a wall and reaches into the block below. A vial drop changes both the color and the rune.
Weathervane — for roofs: the arrow with a sail of woven light turns with the wind — the wind is the same for the whole land, and the weathervanes on the roofs turn together.
Goes on top of a block or a fence post.

kp: Living Decor: Yard and Garden Живой декор: двор и сад
Струйный фонтан Current Fountain Опаловые подвески Opaline Chimes Струйный вымпел Current Pennant Флюгер Weathervane Струйный фонтан Current Fountain
nodes.hint: A yard that breathes flux. Read flowstone.

pages.t: A trim gives armor a look, not protection: a smithing table lays the pattern of a smithing template on a piece of armor in the color of a material — an ingot or a crystal. The pattern goes onto the game's armor and the mod's alike: on each set it follows the set's own model, where the game's armor would carry the same pattern (on the cuirass, the shoulders, the belt, the boots). The template is used up.

Four Fluxion templates lie where their patterns were born. Rill — streams of a current running from a spring on the crown — in Reckoner Locks. Spoke — the Wheel of Currents on the chest and a notched rim — in the vaults of the Meanders. Whorl — a spiral and thread wound around the shoulders and shins — in the workshops of Fluxionist's Homesteads. Hoarfrost — frost ferns and a rim of ice — in the treasury of the City of Midstep in the Stillness.

A Flux Workbench copies a template: the template itself, three diamonds, four opaline and the stone or cloth of its place give two templates — for the flux of the place and its Source. Opaline holds the drawing while the flux carries it onto the new blank.

nodes.hint: A pattern and a color on any armor, from a smithing table; four Fluxion templates and their copies.

pages.t: The Threadwood is a garden of skeins and yarn. A skein in the wood winds its native thread twice: a second share for the same work, always. Fray flows here by itself — the Flux Workbench asks for no Fray shards. And only here is yarn gathered: Glowsilk from cocoons, Current Hanks and Tangled Thread (now and then the Snagling Peddler brings a hank or two). A hank carries Shift — the Converter's feed, so the wood feeds the growth of the next place.

How to gather. Shears on a Glow Cocoon that has silk (it is fluffy and sparks more often): two Glowsilk, the cocoon stays and glows, and its silk grows back in about half an hour — only in the wood. A Reeler drops a Current Hank every 5–10 minutes; don't hit it — it answers with its reel. At night under the canopy Tangles drop Tangled Thread. All three are woven into Weavecloth.

The Silk Spindle is a Spindle with Weavecloth on a crafting table; a wound skein passes to it whole. It winds twice as fast and carries a skein with no loss: a plain Spindle loses an eighth of the threads to murk with every rewinding.

The Tow Sash is a belt of thrift: flux crafting and casting take 10% less flux, and at a Confluence it now and then spares a side plinth's thing. It grows with the flux you spend — up to 14%. It is fused on an Opaline Belt with Weavecloth, a Current Hank and Glowsilk.

What it is grown with: Shift, Weave and Gloom. Spinner Elms stand close, their flat crowns join and close the sky; Current Threads hang from beneath, cocoons glow on the trunks, and underfoot lie near-black Tow Turf, Teasel, Cottongrass and Threadcap. The riverbed is 120. Skeins wind themselves in the wood more often than in the forests of the world.
Where Weave thickens, the trees spin it like a spinner spins tow, and a snapped thread does not fall — it curls into a Tangle. The currents of the place are Weave, Shift, Gloom, Soul and Halo.

kp: Чарное сукно Weavecloth Шёлковое веретено Silk Spindle Кудельный кушак Tow Sash Светошёлк Glowsilk
nodes.hint: A place where skeins wind twice as fast and Glowsilk is sheared from cocoons. The Biome Converter grows it.

pages.t: The Halo Meadow is a quiet, clean place for a home and a workshop. No monsters appear on it at night, phantoms do not swoop on whoever stands on it, no raider patrols walk it and no raids begin. The murk of its chunks burns away by itself — 0.1 a second, like five lumenash trees: a workshop never grows murky, and the mire, with nothing to live on, recedes.

The riverbed is 140, the highest in the overworld: a workshop's flux refills fastest of all. Lattice flows here by itself (elsewhere in the overworld only in snow), and the skeins of the meadow are born lucent. The deep caves under the meadow stay as they were — and so do their creatures.

What to gather. Pearlberries ripen only on the meadow: you can carry a bush away, but without the meadow it bears nothing. A berry is Halo for the Crucible and food with a short Regeneration. Ringhorns shed velvet from their antlers every 5–10 minutes, Lumen Larks drop feathers in flight: a herd and a flock nearby give them without end. The Ringbloom gives the Crucible Halo and Gleam.

The Halo Wreath is for whoever fuses a lot: worn by the one who starts a Confluence, it gives twin yield 4% (now and then what comes out comes out twice) and calm +4. It is fused on Goldspire with two velvets, two feathers, a Pearlberry and opaline.

What it is grown with: Shift, Halo and Gleam. Halo Lindens stand far apart, their leaves ring an empty middle, and the inner rim of the ring glows. The meadow sways with Goldspire, Ringblooms nod in the grass, warm motes rise above it; Ringhorns graze — don't provoke them — and Lumen Larks sing overhead.
Where the world's flux is clean and high, it does not hide in things. The Reckoners called such meadows quiet. The currents of the place are Halo, Gleam, Ward and Sense.

kp: Ореольный венок Halo Wreath Перламутровая ягода Pearlberry
nodes.hint: A quiet place for a home: no monsters, no phantoms, and murk burns away by itself. The Biome Converter grows it.

pages.t: The Simmering Dell is an alchemist's home. A Crucible in the dell brews gently: a clash of opposite Springs carries off half as much, and the murk of the Crucible and the Brewing Tower is halved (with the thrower's Patience, even less). All four Springs flow here by themselves: the Flux Workbench asks for no Gale, Ember, Strata or Tide shards. The riverbed is 100.

What to gather. Bottle Gourds hang under the leaves of Gourdwoods and ripen only in the dell; pick a ripe one by hand, and a new one sets on the stem. A gourd holds Brew 4 and Bloom 2 — Brew from a tree, and every potion of the Crucible needs Brew 2. Sinterstone at the warm springs is heat without fire: a Crucible on it simmers over gentle heat anywhere. Brew Newts drop a Newt Eye — Brew and Tempo.

The Gourd Flask holds three sips of one potion in one slot. Throw it into a Crucible instead of a bottle: it takes a sip of the same brew and floats out — up to three sips of the same potion. It is drunk a sip at a time, and when empty it stays a flask. Its body is a Dried Gourd: a Bottle Gourd in a furnace, smoker or on a campfire.
The Dried Gourd is the first step to a flask; on the Flux Workbench a speculum nugget stopper, two strings for a strap and a Newt Eye are added to it.

What it is grown with: Shift, Brew and Bloom. Warm springs rise in the hollows — pools of turquoise water in a ring of sinter, bubbles rising from the bottom, steam over the surface; Steamreed smokes at the water, Bubblewort glows in it, Simmerbloom blooms on the moss. Baskers sit in the warm water and Brew Newts live by the springs — a provoked newt spits heat.
Where Brew flows, the land brews by itself, and the gourds swell with the sap of currents like vials on an alchemist's shelf. The currents of the place are Brew, Bloom, Alloy, Tide and Venom.

kp: Фляга-горлянка Gourd Flask Сушёная горлянка Dried Gourd Горлянка Bottle Gourd
nodes.hint: An alchemist's home: the Crucible makes half the murk, and Brew grows on trees. The Biome Converter grows it.

pages.t: A Guiding Glint is the light of a journey: with it you need not set a torch at every turn of a cave. Light it with a right-click and carry it anywhere in your inventory: wherever it is dark, it leaves little lights at your feet — a trail of light follows you, easy to walk back by. The lights do not stay: each goes out by itself after two minutes, and the cave is as dark as it was.

The glint sows a light only where it is darker than seven at your feet (not in light and not under a daytime sky), no more than twice a second and no closer than four blocks to its own light: the light of the last one spaces them by itself. Up to twelve burn at once; the thirteenth puts out the oldest. A light is one unit of charge: a full glint holds 64; fill it at a Charging Basin, and a Flux Locket tops it up on the road. The lights take the current of the glint from the bottle: Ember is warm, Tide is blue.

The glint in the cage is no prisoner: it follows its keeper because the keeper carries its home. You can see it over your shoulder — it circles like a firefly by a lantern, only now the lantern is you.

kp: Провожатый огонёк Guiding Glint Провожатый огонёк Guiding Glint
nodes.hint: A glint that lights the road and puts its own lights out.

pages.t: A Sky Cork is the way up when the way back is lost: from a deep cave, a mine or a pit it carries you straight up to the first place under the open sky above you, like a cork from the bottom. Hold right-click for a second and a half and stand still while bubbles of light rise around you; step away and the cork settles back, whole. An opened cork is used up.

The cork lifts you only up, in the same column you stand in — onto the ground, a treetop or the surface of water — and never with a random jump aside. Where there is no sky — in the Nether, the Lees, the Stillness, a Bower under its winding and the Meanders — it will not open; nor will it where fire, lava or no room to stand waits above. A line will tell you why.

kp: Небесная пробка Sky Cork Небесная пробка Sky Cork
nodes.hint: A cork that rises to the sky and takes you with it.

pages.t: The Conduit is the fluxionist's weapon and tool: it strikes with the land's flux, heals, mines, relays blocks and sets traps — which of these, the lens in its socket decides. It is a leather bracer over fluxsteel ribs, a flux coil winding along it, and on the back of the hand a socket with a lens. The flux of the chunk you stand in runs through your arm and the coil and leaves the lens as a deed.

A lens is an opaline disc with facets, and its cut decides what it does. The first lens is cut from a small blank on the Lens Grinder (the next entry, "Lenses"); slot it in by clicking the lens onto the Conduit in your inventory, then right-click to cast. A cast draws flux from the chunk — one flux for every four facets of the lens. To swap lenses on the move, hold …: the lens wheel of your inventory and cases rises around the crosshair; let go, and the one you point at slots in.

Where flux is plentiful, the lens strikes at full force; in a dry place, weaker. Below the bed floor nothing can draw flux: there the lens only hisses and scorches the bed with a pinch of murk. A small blank is rough — every fourth cast leaves murk. Work by a river and watch the flux with the Loupe.

kp: Проводник Conduit Малая заготовка линзы Small Lens Blank Проводник Conduit
nodes.hint: A bracer to pour flux through. Read the air by a river with the Loupe — flux is liveliest there.

pages.t: The Lens Grinder cuts lenses for the Conduit: you build from nodes what the lens will do and how. A pinch of quickdust on a grindstone — and the stone of the wheel clouds with opal, the posts darken, the axle turns to brass, and a ring of runes surfaces on the wheel. This is the Lens Grinder. Lay a lens blank on its wheel by clicking the blank onto it, and open it with an empty hand.

A lens is assembled from nodes. The carrier is how the action flies: Palm, Jet, Droplet, Mist, Pool. The action is what it does: a small blank holds one or two, a Lens Blank three with two carriers in a conjunction, a great one four with up to three. Cuts are how it multiplies and repeats. Every node takes facets of the blank; a node's levels — reach, spread, force — take more.

The wheel cuts slowly and draws the flux of the chunk — two flux for every facet; at the bed floor it stops and waits. A cut must be watered: every level of a node asks for a shard of the Spring or Pole its current flows from; Palm is free. The first nodes — Palm and Scorch — are known to anyone who has studied the Conduit; the entries of this chapter open the rest.

nodes.hint: The Lens Grinder, where lenses are cut. Read fire with the Loupe.

pages.t: A conjunction is two or three carriers of one lens woven into a new path for the action: a trap that digs the layer beneath it, a skipping droplet, a cloud on wings. A Lens Blank holds two carriers, a great blank three. Carriers that do not weave together the Grinder wheel will not cut. The actions stay the lens's own: the conjunction only decides how and where they fly.

Seam Snare (Pool, Survey): whoever steps in — you too — sets the action across the layer beneath, and the trap sinks a layer. Furrow (Jet, Survey): the jet runs straight through blocks of one kind, head-high. Lode Moths (Survey, Courier Moth) fly the lode, and the spoils fall by you. Puffball (Droplet, Mist): the droplet bursts into a cloud.

Skipstone (Jet, Droplet) bounces off blocks, creatures and water. Stalking Mist (Mist, Courier Moth) drifts after a foe. Lookout Moth (Pool, Courier Moth) sits and waits for one. Tripline (Jet, Pool) is a thread that snaps on whoever crosses it. Kin Ring (Palm, Pool) walks with you and strikes foes inside.

Three carriers: Downpour (Jet, Mist, Droplet) — a cloud that drops droplets on foes; Watchfire (Pool, Courier Moth, Jet) — a moth that keeps watch and strikes with a jet. A conjunction costs some flux above the lens's price, its cooldown is never shorter than its own, and one fluxionist keeps one to three of each trap, cloud and watcher: the extra ones fade.

kp: Большая заготовка линзы Great Lens Blank
nodes.hint: Two or three carriers of one lens fly one new way.

pages.t: A case carries twelve lenses on your belt, and the lens wheel sees them there too: swap lenses without opening your inventory — hold …. Twelve pockets of soft leather: click a lens onto the case and it slips into a pocket; right-click brings the last one out. Next: "Lens Blank".

kp: Футляр для линз Lens Case Футляр для линз Lens Case
nodes.hint: A pouch for lenses at your belt.

pages.t: Three actions against whatever is in the way: Gust knocks back and puts out fire, Crack splits blocks, Chill slows and bridges water. Gust is Gale on a lens: a blow of wind knocks back, blows grass away and puts out fire. Crack is Strata: it splits soft blocks, and they fall as items rather than vanish; with force, in a cross and then a square.
Chill is Rime: cold strikes and slows, and over water it lays a bridge of ice that melts on its own. It puts out fire. Next: "Offload".

nodes.hint: Wind, stone and cold on a lens. Reveal Gale, Strata and Rime.

pages.t: Offload cleans a workshop of murk: it carries murk from the chunk you stand in to the chunk it hits. And it strikes past armor with stagnant flux. Remember: murk does not vanish, it only settles in other land. Next: "Mend", "Excavate", "Blight" and "Swap".

nodes.hint: A lens that carries murk away. Reveal Murk.

pages.t: Mend heals you and your own and makes crops grow. It is Bloom on a lens: it closes the wounds of the living, and wounds the undead, who have no life. On the ground it makes crops and grass grow; a Palm cast into empty air heals you yourself.

nodes.hint: A lens that heals. Reveal Bloom.

pages.t: Excavate mines blocks from afar, like a pickaxe. It is Fray on a lens: a block crumbles and drops as an item. The higher the force, the harder the stone it takes; where you may not break, it stays silent. Next: "Washout" and "The Dredge".

nodes.hint: A lens that pries blocks loose. Read a pickaxe or an enchanted book with the Loupe.

pages.t: Droplet carries the action far, as a shot. It is Drift on a lens: the action flies as a bright droplet with a tail and strikes wherever it lands. A droplet's levels are speed. It sinks a little toward the ground: aim with that in mind. Next: "Jet", "Pool", "Stall" and "Survey".

nodes.hint: A carrier that flies. Read an arrow, a snowball or a fire charge with the Loupe.

pages.t: Jet strikes at once and true, with no flight. It is Tide on a lens: the action strikes in a jet of 16, 24 or 32 blocks, and you see the whole of it. Underwater the jet reaches twice as far — Tide is at home there. Next: "Spray".

nodes.hint: An instant beam of flux. Reveal Spark.

pages.t: Spray strikes many at once: it splits the action into three, four or five rays in a fan. Each ray is weaker than a single one, but together they hit harder and catch many. One Spray per lens. Next: "Reverb" and "Branch and Fork".

nodes.hint: A cut that fans the action out.

pages.t: Reverb gives a second strike for free: a second after the cast the lens strikes again — from the same place in the same direction, at half force, drawing no flux. A Mist's reverb is a second cloud, a Pool's a second trap. Next: "Prism Rod".

nodes.hint: A cut that repeats the cast. Reveal Echo.

pages.t: A Pool is a trap: set it in a foe's path. It settles on the ground as a sealed circle and arms itself a second later. Whoever steps in, the lens's action strikes everyone inside, and the pool goes out. On water it spreads half again as wide. A lens keeps no more than four pools at once. Next: "Mist" and "Courier Moth".

nodes.hint: A trap made of flux. Reveal Bind.

pages.t: Mist strikes many and for long: a cloud rises where you look and for several seconds breathes the lens's action on everyone inside except yourself. It is half as strong as a jet; a river's current carries it downstream.

nodes.hint: A cloud of action. Read dragon's breath, a lingering potion or a brewing stand with the Loupe.

pages.t: Stall slows a foe and its shots. It is Tempo on a lens: the target's time thickens — it barely steps, strikes and digs slowly; a flying projectile hangs in the air for a moment. The Reckoners measured Tempo with clocks — a lens simply stops it.

nodes.hint: A lens that slows time. Reveal Tempo.

pages.t: Blight weakens a foe rather than killing: it takes strength away. It is Venom on a lens. First poison; with force, weakness too; at the third level, slowness and hunger. The undead take no poison, only the weakening. On stone and earth Blight does nothing.

nodes.hint: Venom and a chain of weaknesses. Reveal Venom.

pages.t: Swap relays blocks from afar: the block it hits gives way to another. It is Shift on a lens. Your off hand decides which: hold a block in it. If there is none, the lens takes the block from the slot right of the Conduit. The old one drops as an item; the new one comes out of your inventory.

Swap leaves chests, furnaces and anything holding something alone, and stone harder than an iron pickaxe takes. With Survey it trades a whole layer — that is how floors and walls are relaid. Next: "Survey" and "Washout".

nodes.hint: A block is traded for another. Reveal Shift.

pages.t: Survey strikes not a block but a layer: that is how an ore vein is taken, a floor relaid and a wall opened. It is Craft on a lens: the action falls on every block of the same kind as the one you look at, joined to it across the face you struck. Its levels are spread: three, five, seven blocks across. You see the frame of what is marked.

Survey with Excavate lifts a layer of ore or earth; with Swap it relays a floor; with Washout it opens a whole wall. With Branch it takes the layer behind as well. On a creature, Survey strikes like a Palm. Next: "Carrier Conjunctions".

nodes.hint: A carrier that takes a whole layer. Reveal Craft.

pages.t: Washout opens a passage through stone — for a while, with no pickaxe and no trace, and underwater it leads you dry. It is Hollow on a lens: the blocks along the strike step away, and a passage as tall as a person opens in the stone — three, five or seven blocks deep. After twelve to twenty seconds it closes from the mouth inward: everything that was there comes back.

Water does not flow into a washout — it stands around the passage as walls, and so you can walk dry under water. The passage waits until you step out of it. Washout does not go through chests, doors, torches or anything unbreakable.

nodes.hint: A passage through stone for a while. Reveal Hollow.

pages.t: Two facets to reach more targets. Branch sends the cast out as two branches side by side, half a block apart: two jets, two droplets, two clouds. Fork branches the action at the target: on a hit it leaps to the nearest other target — up to six blocks away. Each branch strikes at seven tenths of the force.
One Branch and one Fork per lens, but they can stand together. Fork branches from a pool and a mist too, to whoever stands outside the circle. With Mend, Fork carries the healing to your own.

kp: Branch and Fork Рукав и развилка
nodes.hint: Two cuts that branch a cast.

pages.t: The Courier Moth delivers the action by itself: it flies to the target or seeks a foe nearby — no aiming needed. It is Wing on a lens: a moth of light flies out of the Conduit, its wings the color of the action, and delivers it three times, falling back and coming in again. It does not bite on its own and fades after fifteen seconds.

A Courier Moth with Mend heals you and your own. With nothing to do it flies to the light — it circles the brightest fire nearby. A Courier Moth node is watered with an ember moth's wing: watch the ember moth to learn how things fly to the light.

The ember moth is a Nether moth of soot and ember: it flies to any light and settles on lanterns to warm the coal in its belly. Struck, it sheds sparks; water puts it out for good. Its wing remembers the way to the light — that is why a Courier Moth node is watered with an ember moth's wing.

nodes.hint: A ghostly moth carries the action to its target. Read an ember moth with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Lens Blank is the second step of lenses: it takes a lens with two carriers woven into a conjunction and three actions. A trap that digs the layer beneath it, a furrow through stone, lode moths, a skipping droplet, a cloud on wings — all of these are within its reach; only a great blank holds three-carrier conjunctions.

It is grown by Confluence: a small blank in the middle, two opaline, two speculum sheets and an amethyst shard on the plinths; Prism, Lattice and Weave, a mid Confluence. A cut small lens in the middle grows together with its cut — no need to cut it again.

Twenty facets against a small blank's twelve. The bronze rim holds the glass steadier: the lens leaves murk only every sixteenth cast, and its cooldown grows a quarter slower with facets. The cast costs the same — one flux for four facets — plus the conjunction's share. Next: "Fluxsteel Conduit".

kp: Заготовка линзы Lens Blank Заготовка линзы Lens Blank
nodes.hint: A lens with two carriers in a conjunction and three actions — and murk only once in sixteen casts. Read amethyst with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Still Conduit casts at full strength anywhere and never touches the land's flux: each cast pays from the store in its vial — forty flux. It is the only Conduit that works in the Stillness, where the world's flux is zero and every other Conduit only fizzles. A dry place does not weaken its lens and no rough draw makes murk; a cheap blank still does, as always. Refill the empty vial in a Charging Basin or with a Flux Locket.
A Conduit is reforged at the Flux Workbench: two stillmetal plates, a vial for the store and an ingot to seal it. The lens, the Niello Inlay and the Survey reach carry over into the new bracer.

kp: Стылый проводник Still Conduit Стылый проводник Still Conduit
nodes.hint: A Conduit that carries its own flux. Study the Conduit and Stillmetal.

pages.t: The Flux Locket charges your things on the move — Waders, the Charm, belts, the Grapnel — with no Charging Basin. It is a brass reliquary with flux turning behind its window: it drinks from the land, but only while you stand by water or in a chunk where flux is above its bed. In a dry, drained place the locket stays silent.

kp: Ладанка тока Flux Locket Ладанка тока Flux Locket
nodes.hint: A Charging Basin you wear — but only by water. Study the Charging Basin and the Confluence.

pages.t: The Prism Rod is a beam weapon that grows stronger with every reflection: by mirrors and water it hits hardest. The Prism beam on its own is plain light, but it glances off glass, opaline, ice and still water, and every reflection makes it stronger. Reverb teaches that flux reflects; fluxionists built halls of mirrors by their doors on purpose.

A shot costs a charge of Prism. To fill it, sneak with a Prism distillate vial in the other hand: one part of the vial, one shot. Or lay the rod in a Charging Basin and run a siphon into its side from a vessel of Prism: the rod fills by itself. With mastery the beam reflects more, strikes harder and at last passes through foes.

kp: Призменный жезл Prism Rod Призменный жезл Prism Rod
nodes.hint: A beam that grows stronger off every mirror. Study Reverb and Brightsteel.

pages.t: A Fluxsteel Conduit drinks flux not from your own chunk but from the nine around it — more from the fuller ones, like a Catchment: in a dry spot amid full land a cast strikes at full strength, and a great lens does not scrape your chunk to the bottom. It is fused from a Conduit: the lens and the inlay move into the new bracer by themselves.
Lenses, the wheel, cooldowns and the murk of cheap lenses work as with the Conduit. It does not help thin land: if all nine chunks are drained, a cast weakens as in the hand of a plain Conduit.

kp: Флюкс-стальной проводник Fluxsteel Conduit Флюкс-стальной проводник Fluxsteel Conduit
nodes.hint: A hand can drink from the whole neighborhood. Study the Lens Blank and the Catchment.

pages.t: A tracery is a spell no node of the Lens Grinder makes: lightning that leaps between foes; two strikes at two targets from one lens; a strike that repeats from a rune in the air. You draw it yourself — on a board, with springs, channels and mouths — and the Pantograph cuts the drawing into the opal of a blank. A pinch of quickdust on a cartography table wakes it as a Pantograph. Lay a lens blank in the clamp and open it with an empty hand.

A spring is a current shard: a stream of strength one flows out of it. You lead a channel with the mouse from a cell to its neighbors, like the pen on a riverbed puzzle. A mouth is where the stream leaves as a strike; its kind is a carrier — Jet, Palm, Droplet and the others you have studied. The current that arrives decides what the strike does.

The shape decides. Two channels that merge add their currents on the Wheel: Ember and Gale make Spark, and the Jet strikes with an Arc. A fork splits the stream evenly, and its mouths strike different targets. Opposite Springs — Tide and Ember, Strata and Gale — clash outside a basin: the strike hits with both actions, harder and two blocks around, but it murks. A basin merges them in peace. A curl — a ring of channel — repeats the strike; a lull delays it, and it comes later from a rune where you cast.

The current at the mouth is the action. Gale pushes, Ember burns, Strata cracks, Fray excavates; Tide is Douse: it puts out fire and wets; Lattice is Brace: steadiness for friends, sluggishness for foes; Spark is an Arc, Blast a Burst, Drift a Haul that drags the target to you. Rime, Bloom, Tempo, Murk, Venom, Shift and Hollow do what their nodes do. Other currents fall apart into the actions of their forebears: Alloy is Crack and Scorch.

A tracery costs more than a cut: a channel is half a facet per segment, marks and mouths have their own facets; a cast costs facets / 4 flux and one more per clash. The strength of a tracery is the sum of the strikes of one cast: up to 3 on a small blank, 5 on a Lens Blank, 8 on a great one; facets — 18, 30 and 54. The cutter drinks the flux of the chunk, facets × 2, and asks a shard for every mark. To recut a lens is to pay again. The Pantograph does not take a ground lens, the Lens Grinder does not take a tracery.

The patterns in the Pantograph window are where to begin: «Arc» (Ember and Gale merge), «Twin Fire» (a fork at two targets), «The Curl», «Steam» (a clash), «Delayed Blow». A click lays a pattern on the board — then change it yourself.

You can keep a tracery and give it away: «Make a tracing» above the board lays the drawing on a sheet of paper — the tracing shows in the list under the cutters at any Pantograph, and a friend on the server cuts it at his own. Above the sheet are the name of the tracery (seen on the lens, in the lens wheel and in the Conduit line) and a drop of ink: gold for free or a dye from your inventory. Changing only the name or ink costs no shards and no cutting. The drawing turns and mirrors with the buttons above the board and shifts with the arrow keys; «Trial» on the sheet shows in a small scene whom the tracery strikes and when.

nodes.hint: A table where you cut a spell of your own into a lens blank. Read a cartography table with the Loupe.

pages.t: One lens, different spells: a Switch asks at the moment of the cast and leads the stream straight on if yes, aside if no. Is the target undead, burning, wet, a friend; is the flux of the place full, is it dark, are you sneaking. At the undead — life, at the living — fire; Brace for friends, an Arc for foes. Switches are cut on a Lens Blank and a great one.

A Surge gathers casts: the stream goes on every second, third or fourth cast — that many times stronger; the count lives in the lens itself. A Scent remembers a target: a cast marks the one you look at, and the mouths behind the Scent fly to it for thirty seconds wherever you look. A spring can be a vial too: a full vial of distillate gives a stream of any current.
Up to four switches on a board, up to four surges. A switch is 2 facets, a surge and a scent 2 each; the price is a shard of Lattice, Fray and Gale. Patterns: «Healer», «Thunder Bank», «Hunter».

kp: Switches and Memory Стрелки и память
nodes.hint: A tracery that asks and remembers. Read a comparator.

pages.t: A cameo is a ready piece of tracery you set into another: draw «two Jets» once and set them into any tracery with one socket. A cameo is cut on a small blank: instead of springs it has an Inlet — the stream of the bigger board comes in here — and, if needed, an Outlet, where the stream goes back out.

A cameo socket is set on a Lens Blank (one) and a great blank (two); the mouse wheel over the socket picks a cameo from your inventory. The Pantograph copies the pattern, the cameo stays with you; its marks are paid again, its mouths and strength count in the bigger tracery. There is no cameo inside a cameo. Pattern — «Chain».

kp: Малая заготовка линзы Small Lens Blank
nodes.hint: A small tracery set into a bigger one.

pages.t: A shape is not what a strike does but how it lands: a fan into a crowd, a wall across a passage, through a rank, a ricochet round a corner, a chain from foe to foe. A shape mark goes on a channel — every mouth downstream takes it. Spray is a fan of 3 or 5 rays, or even a ring of eight strikes around you. Ridge is three strikes side by side across your gaze.

Range raises the carrier a level: the Jet reaches further, Mist and Pool spread wider, the Droplet flies faster. A Rosary repeats the strike ×2, ×3, ×4 — a burst without a ring on the board. Ricochet bounces the Jet off a block once or twice. Pierce carries the Jet through its target into 1–3 more behind. Leap takes the action down a chain of targets — kind ones to friends.

Numbers: a Ridge is 2 facets, each strike ×0.55; a Spray ring — ×0.35 a strike, only the Jet, Palm and Droplet; Ricochet and Pierce — only the Jet, ×0.8 and ×0.7; Leap — ×0.7 a link; a Rosary — a quarter second between strikes, counted in the repeats of the blank. Patterns: «Fire Ridge», «Burst Ring», «Ricochet», «Rosary», «Piercer», «Frost Chain».

kp: Shape of the Strike Форма удара
nodes.hint: How a strike lands in the world: a fan, a wall, through, a ricochet, a chain. Read a spyglass with the Loupe.

pages.t: Fifteen compound currents that used to fall apart into the deeds of their forebears now do their own at a mouth: Gleam dazzles a foe, Soul drains its life into you, Mind beguiles a monster into attacking its neighbor, Cog opens doors and presses buttons from afar. You get such currents by merging on the Wheel or from a vial of distillate on a Lens Blank.

For a foe: Dazzle (Gleam), Drain (Soul), Beguile (Mind), Uplift (Wing) — into the air, Entangle (Bind) — rooted, Rend (Fang) — the more wounded, the harder, Wilt (Ash), Eclipse (Gloom) — darkness, and the monster loses you. For a friend: Uplift — a soft fall, Eclipse — invisibility, Bulwark (Ward) — golden hearts, Dispel (Balance) strips the bad.

Around the hit: Reveal (Sense) — every creature glows, Rally (Kin) — speed and strength for friends, Grace (Halo) — heals friends, Beckon (Want) — things and experience fly to you. On a block: Hinge (Cog) — doors, trapdoors, gates, buttons, levers. Patterns: «Flock Healer», «Shadow».

kp: Voices of the Mouth Устья течений
nodes.hint: Compound currents have deeds of their own at a mouth. Read a distillate vial with the Loupe.

pages.t: A Target picks the target for the mouths behind it: yourself — healing and wards, the nearest foe — the strike finds it without your gaze, under your feet, behind — at whoever chases you, the avenger — whoever hurt you in 10 seconds, the most wounded friend. A Latch charges a strike in advance: it waits at your side for an event and strikes then.

Latch events: you are hurt — at whoever hurt you; you hit — at the one you hit; you kill — at the nearest other foe; you land from a height — under your feet; a foe comes near — at it; you break a block — into that block. It waits 15 seconds on a Lens Blank and 30 on a great one; you hold up to four latches, and the Conduit line says how long they wait. A Target behind a Latch outranks the event: «hurt → yourself» is a heal at the moment of the blow.

The Switch learns new questions: about the target — is it near, in a crowd, airborne, armored; about you — night, storm, in water, falling, sprinting, looking down or up. Patterns: «Avenger», «Homing», «Shockwave», «Vein Digger».

kp: Target and Latch Прицел и Взвод
nodes.hint: A tracery that strikes not where you look and not when you cast. Read a tripwire hook with the Loupe.

pages.t: A Pond hoards strikes, a Ladle spends them when needed: in a quiet moment the stream goes into the Pond as a charge, in a fight the Ladle draws it and adds a strike.
