A Lockgate lets the stream on only if both channels arrive — with switches that is «and»: Rend only if the target is a foe and wounded. An Overflow splits strength unevenly.

One Pond per tracery, up to 4 charges (6 on a great blank); the charges live in the lens. A Ladle is a spring of the Pond's current, strength 1: an empty Pond silences the Ladle and all it flows into. The Switch asks «Pond holds», «Alternate» — every second cast — and «Chance». An Overflow lets no more than strength 1 or 2 straight on, the rest aside. Patterns: «Reserve», «Finisher».

kp: Pond and Lockgate Копань и Створ
nodes.hint: A tracery with memory and logic: hoard, spend, ask «and». Read a repeater with the Loupe.

pages.t: Bindings fit your Conduit to you and to the place. There are two slots: a cuff at the wrist changes every cast — cheaper, faster or steadier near the bottom of the bed; an insert in the bed gives a native current, and its casts are cheaper where it flows. Set them at the Flux Workbench: any Conduit with a cuff or an insert below it; the old one comes back into the grid. The binding shows on the bracer and moves to a new bracer along with the lens.

Cuffs are forged from the Copper Cuff, which changes nothing by itself. Gold: casts 10% cheaper. Bronze: cooldown 15% shorter. Fluxsteel: 15% cheaper and murk half as often. Still: casts do not weaken near the bottom of the bed. A cuff's thrift adds to your fluxionist garb and Will, but a cast never costs less than half.

An insert is the substance of a Spring or a Pole: Ember — a blaze rod, Gale — a breeze rod, Tide — a prismarine shard, Strata — obsidian, Lattice — nether quartz, Fray — a bone. A native cast is one whose main action (the first in the lens's name) is the insert's current or made of it: Chill is native to both Tide and Lattice. It takes a quarter less flux from the land; where the insert's Spring flows in the place — as at the Flux Workbench — it also murks half as often; where the opposite flows (Ember — Tide, Strata — Gale, Lattice — Fray) and its own does not, a quarter more. Other casts are left as they are.

An insert holds 8 flux of its own. It fills one at a time every five seconds from the chunk's flux while you hold the Conduit where the insert's Spring flows and the chunk is at least half full. In a dry chunk the store covers a cast's shortfall — after a skein and before a Belt Reliquary. Pantograph traceries and the Wheel Conduit pay by the same rules; a tracery's main action is that of its first strike.

kp: Проводник Conduit Медный обшлаг Copper Cuff Вставка Жара Ember Insert Золотой обшлаг Gold Cuff
nodes.hint: Metal at the wrist and a substance in the bed. Read a blaze rod, a breeze rod or a prismarine shard.

pages.t: Confluence gives things what neither the Crucible nor a workbench can: weavings in tools and armor, exact enchantments, the power of trinkets and the strongest things of fluxion. The Crucible dissolves things, the Workbench puts them together, and the Confluence pours currents into the thing itself. The Confluence Heart hangs two blocks above the central plinth; the thing on the central plinth is the one that changes.

Side plinths stand around it, up to sixteen within eight blocks: one thing on each, to flow into the central one. Set them in an even ring — two rings of eight, near and far: streams heaped on one side churn, and so do streams that cross from above.

Four columns stand two blocks from the central plinth on each side — by them the Heart knows its altar. Once it is built, throw a pinch of quickdust on the Heart: it wakes, and golden veins run along the floor from the columns and plinths to the center.
The whole altar is on the diagram: drag it with the mouse and look at it layer by layer. "Place ghost" sets it in the world where you look — build along it.

Lay out the things and look at the Heart with the Loupe or the Diviner's Spectacles: it tells you what will come out, how much distillate it needs and whether there is enough calm. The Confluence draws distillate from vessels within twelve blocks, two parts a second; touch the Heart with the Conduit, and the things leave for it one by one.

Calm is the Heart's store of steadiness: once awake, it gathers up to thirty. During a Confluence the streams take it away — rough ones more (Fray, Murk, Blast), quiet ones less (Lattice, Still). Below zero come eddies: a thing is knocked off, a stream lashes out, distillate flows back. The Heart shows how much calm the Confluence needs and how much the altar gives.

Confluences are simple, mid or great. A bare altar holds a simple one with room to spare. A mid one takes eight calm to begin and weighs more with every part — it needs weirs or calm stones. A great one takes twenty-four and churns — it needs a well-built altar. Every weaving on top of earlier ones is a tier higher.

A Confluence always ends. You can stop it yourself: sneak and press the Heart twice with an empty hand. If the Heart waits a minute for distillate or for a knocked-off thing, the Confluence fades; if calm falls to minus forty, it collapses. However it ends, the gathered distillate spills as murk and the things already taken are lost. Make an inscription your first Confluence (the entry "Inscription"): Sharpness on a sword from two flints and an iron ingot is simple, and a bare altar holds it any day or night; it takes two parts each of Bane, Edge and Lattice distillate.

kp: Сердце слияния Confluence Heart Постамент Plinth Опора слияния Confluence Column Сердце слияния Confluence Heart
nodes.hint: Pouring currents into a thing on an altar — if you can hold it steady. Discover Halo and Weave: Halo flows in current shards, Weave in quickdust, fluxsteel and enchanted books.

pages.t: Weirs keep a Confluence steady: without them a mid or great Confluence breaks into eddies. A weir calms one stream — the one it stands beside: set it within a block of the line between a side plinth and the center. The first weir on a stream calms 0.8 a second, the second half that, a third nothing. Set it by the stream with a rough thing — a turquoise thread will run to it.

A flume is a channel in the floor. Lay a line of flumes from a weir to a side plinth: if an eddy would knock that plinth's thing off, the weir holds it — once per Confluence. Light runs along connected flumes.
Float lanterns by a stream calm it too, and a lantern of its current's color twice as much. Next: "Rapids and Reach" and "Calm Stones".

kp: Запруда Weir Лоток Flume Запруда Weir
nodes.hint: How to hold a Confluence steady. See an eddy with your own eyes.

pages.t: Stones under the columns tune the course of a Confluence: rapids hurry the distillate, a reach spares it and calms the altar. A rapids stone goes under a column: distillate flows faster — three parts a second with four stones — but the streams churn harder.

A reach stone is the opposite: distillate flows slower, down to one part a second, but less of it is needed, up to a fifteenth less, and the altar is calmer. Stones of different kinds cancel each other.

kp: Rapids and Reach Стремнина и плёс
Камень стремнины Rapids Stone Камень плёса Reach Stone Камень стремнины Rapids Stone
nodes.hint: Stones under the columns change the pace of a Confluence.

pages.t: Reckoner plinths and columns make an altar calmer and thriftier: their streams run more evenly, and less distillate is spent. The Reckoners measured the Confluence too. The stream from a plinth of their stone runs to the Heart a quarter calmer than usual: the measuring frame above the bowl holds the thing like a gauge.
Reckoner Columns gather the flux with care: set all four, and every Confluence takes a tenth less distillate. With reach stones the savings add up. Mixed columns count as ordinary ones.

kp: Постамент Исчислителей Reckoner Plinth Опора Исчислителей Reckoner Column Постамент Исчислителей Reckoner Plinth
nodes.hint: Read a Reckoner stone: their masons cut altar parts too.

pages.t: A floor of backwater flagstone gives the Heart a store of calm — and a great Confluence stops breaking. The Reckoners' weir keepers paved the beds by their sluices with flagstones over which water stood still, as in a backwater. An altar floor of such flagstone — at the level of the plinths or below, within eight blocks — raises the Heart's calm: the first flags give the most, up to +30.

Calm steles stand along old weirs. By an altar a stele calms 0.3 a second of a Confluence, each next a little less; eight count. While the Heart is awake their runes glow and a thread runs from each to the center.
A weirkeeper figurine — a clay keeper holding a float — was left by a sluice as a vow: hold the water level. By an altar it calms 0.4 a second and adds 5 to the Heart's calm; the four nearest count.

A Lees Shell with a ripe pearl is a calm stone from the bottom of the Lees: by an altar it calms 0.4 a second and adds 8 to the Heart's calm — more than a figurine. Shells stand in for figurines: the four nearest of both together count, and the fittings' common calm limit stays. The Heart ignores a shell without a pearl; take one with Silk Touch and the pearl stays in it. Next: "Altar Fittings".

kp: Плитняк заводи Backwater Flagstone Стела покоя Calm Stele Фигурка запрудника Weirkeeper Figurine Стела покоя Calm Stele
nodes.hint: The Reckoners' weir keepers knew how to hold water level. Study Weirs.

pages.t: Altar fittings make a Confluence stronger: more calm, less distillate, twin yield, fewer eddies, softer failure. Two give boons to a Confluence: the gear of whoever started it and the fittings of the altar. There are ten boons: calm and calm a second, distillate thrift, twin yield, fewer eddies, softer failure, draw reach, swifter distillate, sparing a thing and a lighter mid and great Confluence. Each source has its limit and the sum a common one: gear helps, but the strength is in the building.

Gear counts only for the one who started and only while they stay within sixteen blocks of the Heart: step away and its boons stop, come back and they count again. A crowd in armor nearby does not help. A thing's tooltip says what it gives; the Heart in the Loupe shows the altar's and the gear's boons apart.

A twin yield falls only to a steady Confluence — without a single eddy — and only to a thing that stacks: gear, weavings and one-of-a-kind things are never doubled. The backwater basin is still water in stone: it adds to the Heart's calm.
The flux censer is a wisp of smoke over the altar: it calms a little every second of a Confluence, and eddies come more rarely.
Speculum mirrors work in pairs: two facing each other across the middle of the altar, both turned to it. The thing is reflected — and sometimes comes out twofold.
Rune pillars also work in pairs, facing each other across the middle: their runes hold the water level, and eddies are rarer and milder.
The sluice bell rings when a Confluence fails: less murk spills, and the Heart loses less calm.
The opaline druse draws distillate from afar: vessels can stand further away, and it flows a little faster.
A Reckoner's reliquary keeps a measuring bone: sometimes a thing from a side plinth comes back to it instead of flowing into the Heart, and a little less distillate is needed.
Current banners work in a set of four, in a pinwheel around the middle at one height: a mid or great Confluence is lighter to begin and with every part.
All the fittings are on the altar diagram, as optional parts. The Loupe on any fitting tells you whether it counts and what it lacks.

kp: Чаша заводи Backwater Basin Курильница тока Flux Censer Бронзовое зеркало Speculum Mirror Рунный столп Rune Pillar Колокол шлюза Sluice Bell Опаловая друза Opaline Druse Ковчег Исчислителя Reckoner's Reliquary Хоругвь течений Current Banner Бронзовое зеркало Speculum Mirror
nodes.hint: A beautifully furnished altar is a strong altar. Study Calm Stones.

pages.t: Weavings give a tool, a weapon, armor, a bow, a shield or a Conduit flux properties no enchantment has: loot into your inventory, three by three, a whole vein at once, a quicker step, a seeking arrow, a shield that sends arrows back. A weaving is a current poured into the thing itself: lay it on the central plinth, the weaving's things around, its distillate in vessels nearby. No enchanted book is needed. Each further weaving of the same thing costs a third more, and the third makes the thing tense.

Pull (Want and Drift: a lead, gold, an ender pearl) — spoils of what you break and kill flow into your inventory. Sweep (Edge and Blast: iron and gunpowder) — pickaxe, shovel and axe break three by three. Vein (Strata, Root, Alloy: raw iron and copper, a log) — a whole vein of ore or a trunk, for the flux of the land.

Echo Sounder (Echo and Prism: amethyst and a note block) — strike stone with the pickaxe, and the ores around answer. Splash (Tide and Bane) — a hit splashes the foes beside. Cadence (Tempo) — every third hit in rhythm strikes harder.

Dodge (Wing and Drift: a feather, a rabbit's foot, a membrane) — on leggings: now and then a blow misses, a step aside. Swiftwater (Tide and Drift: prismarine and kelp) — on boots: lighter going in water.

Panning (Tide and Strata: concentrate, gravel, a bowl) — on a pickaxe: ore washes itself as you break it, and half the raw iron, gold, copper and antimony comes out as concentrate — two ingots in a furnace. With Fortune on the pickaxe, Panning keeps still. Fireflies (Gleam and Bloom: a Bottled Glint, glow berries, glowstone dust) — on a tool: where it breaks a block in the dark, a firefly settles and shines until the daylight sky stands over it.

Extract (Soul and Brew: two vials, a ghast tear) — on a weapon: distillate from the hunt. Half the time, a creature you slay that gives experience fills an empty vial from your inventory with its main current — keep empty vials on you.

Hoard (Bind and Want: a flux coil, a copper block, a bundle) — a thing that runs on flux charge holds half again as much. Trickle (Root and Tide: pointed dripstone, hanging roots, glow lichen) — such a thing, worn or on the hotbar, slowly draws charge from the land's flux by itself. Both go onto the Waders, the belts and charms, the Grapnel, the Flux Ruling Pen, the Deep Mirror and the Still Conduit.

Stride (Drift and Gale: sugar, a rabbit hide, a Gale Shard) — on any armor piece: a quicker step, every piece adds, and all four nearly match a Swiftness potion. Keel (Strata and Bind: a chain, a nautilus shell, a heavy pressure plate) — on leggings: blows push you less, and not at all while you crouch. Stepstone (Strata and Drift: two stairs, a feather) — on boots: step up a block without jumping.

Clearsight (Gloom and Sense: a golden carrot, sculk, an ink sac) — on a helmet: the Darkness of the Deep Dark and Blindness do not take hold of you. Wariness (Sense and Fang: a rabbit's foot, a spider eye, a sculk sensor) — on a helmet: you see who hunts you — whoever takes you as a target glows, even behind a wall.

Plenty (Root and Bloom: bread, a hay bale, honey) — on a chestplate: farther on the same bread — running, fighting and work tire you a third less. Respite (Bloom and Still: a glistering melon slice, a lily pad, moss) — on a chestplate: healing without food in hand — stand still, and health slowly returns.

Hoarfrost (Rime and Bane: packed ice, snowballs) — on a weapon: against fiery and fleeing foes — a hit freezes, and a frozen foe takes more. Ambush (Fang and Gloom: an ink sac, a bone, a feather) — for the one who strikes first: a blow on a creature nobody has hurt for a while is half again as strong. Culling (Ash and Bane: a bone block, rotten flesh, flint) — ends long fights: strikes harder at a foe near death.

Lesson (Mind and Want: a bottle o' enchanting, a book, lapis) — on a weapon: half again as much experience from the hunt. On a shield: Rebound (Prism and Ward: a speculum sheet, amethyst, a slime ball) — an arrow caught on the shield flies back at the shooter; Breakwater (Tide and Blast: prismarine, a wind charge, stone bricks) — room in a crowd: a blow on the shield throws the attacker back.

On a bow and a crossbow. Seeker (Sense and Wing: an eye of ender, a compass, a feather) — fewer misses: the arrow turns toward a foe in its path. Backwash (Tide and Bind: a lead, string, prismarine) — no walking for arrows: one stuck in a block flows back into your inventory. Hunter's Mark (Sense and Gleam: a glow ink sac, a spectral arrow, a target) — shoot, then strike: the marked creature glows, and the first melee blow on it, yours or a friend's, is stronger.

Long Arm (Edge and Drift: two bamboo, a spyglass) — on a tool: build and dig from where you stand — blocks are reached two farther. Reseed (Root and Bloom: seeds, bone meal, a composter) — on a hoe: harvest without replanting — a ripe crop plants itself again from its own seed. Sieve (Murk and Brew: a lumenash grate, clearwort seeds, silt) — on a thing with charge: charge from the murk of the land, and the land clears.

On a Conduit. Quickcast (Tempo and Weave: a clock, two quickdust) — cast more often: a third shorter cooldown, but never shorter than a mist, pool or moth lens allows. Taproot (Root and Strata: rooted dirt, mangrove roots, a Tide Shard) — for deserts and drained land: a dry place takes half as much strength from your casts.

Groundfall (Strata and Blast: two pointed dripstone, gunpowder) — on boots: jump into a crowd from above — the landing strikes everyone around, the harder the higher you fell; your own fall is no softer. Desperation (Ember and Bane: blaze powder, magma cream, flint) — on a weapon: when you are near death yourself, you strike almost half again as hard. Adit (Tempo and Strata: two rails, a lantern) — on a pickaxe or shovel: long tunnels go faster — each next block straight ahead digs faster, up to half again. Rockbreaker (Alloy and Strata: obsidian, deepslate, iron) — on a pickaxe: deepslate, ores and obsidian twice as fast. Next: "Wootz" and "Flux Sheath".

kp: Кошка Grapnel Бродни Waders Проводник Conduit
nodes.hint: A Confluence weaves properties of flux into a tool, a weapon or armor. Read an enchanted book with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Full-Moon Apple is an enchanted golden apple no one can craft: Confluence fills a golden apple with Bloom, and a Full Moon Mark brings the hour of the full moon (the "Hour Marks" entry). A golden apple on the central plinth, two gold blocks, a Full Moon Mark and a glistering melon slice around it; Bloom, Halo and Gleam in the vessels. It is a simple Confluence: a bare altar holds it steady, at any hour.

kp: Зачарованное золотое яблоко Enchanted Golden Apple
nodes.hint: A golden apple filled with Bloom under a Full Moon Mark. Read a golden apple with the Loupe.

pages.t: A still plinth keeps a stormy item calm: the stream from a side still plinth to the Heart never churns — not by itself, not from the item's temper, not at a crossing. The price is time: each such plinth slows the Confluence, one by about a tenth, four by almost a third. Put the stormiest items on them. In the middle of the altar it is a plain Plinth.

A still column does the opposite: when all four columns are still ones, a Confluence runs half again as fast and the streams have less time to churn, but it takes 15% more distillate. Mixed columns are ordinary. Still plinths and still columns balance each other: slow calm streams and a quick run.

kp: Стылый постамент Still Plinth Стылая опора Still Column Стылый постамент Still Plinth
nodes.hint: A stream that never churns. Study Reckoner Plinths and Stillmetal, read Stillstone.

pages.t: A Self-Rising Loaf is food that never runs out: an eaten slice grows back on the land's flux, a pinch a slice. Confluence makes it from a cake, wheat, honey, bread and a hubstone: it gives the loaf its Tide spoke and comes back without it. The crust is not eaten: the loaf grows back from it.
On drained land the loaf waits, and in the Stillness it does not rise at all: nothing flows there.

kp: Неубывный каравай Self-Rising Loaf Неубывный каравай Self-Rising Loaf
nodes.hint: Bread that grows on flux. Read a cake.

pages.t: Waders are boots for water and rivers: while charged you walk on still water — a river, a lake, the sea — as on land, and faster on its surface; you swim easier in them, go faster along the current, step higher and fall softer. Crouch to sink in, and climb back on top at the bank; a fall onto the surface does not hurt. Waxed leather to the thigh, a thread of fluxsteel along the seams. They give almost no protection, and without charge they are only boots.
A Charging Basin or a Flux Locket fills the charge. How much is left shows in the boots' tooltip and as a bar on the icon. Next come "Spring Tools", and after them "Weavings".

nodes.hint: Boots that carry you through water like a fish. Read leather boots.

pages.t: Spring Tools are fluxsteel with a Spring melted in: twice as durable, and each has its own ability — the axe fells whole trunks, the pickaxe smelts part of what it digs, the shovel lays a layer of blocks. A fluxsteel tool on the central plinth, two shards of a Spring around it: the Confluence pours the Spring into the steel itself. The tools grow in mastery not by fighting but by work: ore, logs, soil.

Tide Axe: while you hold the button, loose things swim to you on a stream; it fells whole trunks. Ember Pickaxe: sets alight what it strikes, hears the ores around, washes half the raw ore into concentrate (it is born with the Echo Sounder and Panning weavings) and smelts part of what it breaks.
Gale Blade: raised, it lowers you on the wind and throws back whoever crowds you. Strata Spade: lays a whole layer of blocks from your inventory across a face.

Pole Hoe: Lattice tills a whole bed at once, Fray takes overgrowth apart into bone meal. Sneak and use it in the air to change the pole. The next entry is "Weavings": properties of flux for any tool and armor.

kp: Топор Прилива Tide Axe Кирка Жара Ember Pickaxe Клинок Порыва Gale Blade Лопата Пласта Strata Spade Мотыга Полюсов Pole Hoe Топор Прилива Tide Axe
nodes.hint: Fluxsteel with a Spring poured into it. Read a fluxsteel tool.

pages.t: Dam Plate holds the line against a crowd: blows build up a head, and you loose it as a wave on the foes or let it ebb back as health. Dark bronze and steel laid like the stones of a weir. On two pieces part of every blow does not pass through but builds a head of water — the line over the hotbar shows how much; on three a full dam opens the spillway on its own and the foes around are thrown back. The plate is heavy: you walk slower in it.

Open the spillway at will. Crouch twice and a head of four or more runs ahead as a wave in a wedge seven blocks long: every foe in it takes four fifths of a damage for each point of the head, is thrown back and soaked. Backflow: a head that ebbs away by itself out of battle comes back as health — half a point for each. Loose it as a wave or heal with it — your choice.
The pieces are made by a Confluence over fluxsteel armor. Diviner's Spectacles are set into the Dam Helm on a crafting table — the helm then sees what Crucibles and devices hold. Next: "Visors".

kp: Плотинная кираса Dam Cuirass Плотинный шлем Dam Helm Плотинные поножи Dam Greaves Плотинная кираса Dam Cuirass
nodes.hint: Armor that holds a blow as a dam holds water. Study Waders and Fluxsteel Gear.

pages.t: A visor adds its own property to a Dam Helm: quieter visions, a foe that bogs down, a blow that heals. It is set into the helm's grille on a crafting table; the helm stays the same. Diviner's Spectacles carry no Dissonance; the three visors of Dissonance give it while worn, and the helm takes their name.

The Calm Visor (hush salt) softens visions of Dissonance. The Drowned Visor (mire threads): whoever strikes you up close is silted. The Leech Visor (a fermented spider eye): a full-strength hit heals you a little.

kp: Плотинный шлем Dam Helm Плотинный шлем Dam Helm
nodes.hint: Masks set into the Dam Helm. Study Dam Plate.

pages.t: A Towline Belt speeds up a long straight road — up to a third faster. A belt of towing rope with a brass hook: walk straight and every step is lighter than the last; a sharp turn drops the way. While the way is up, the belt spends its charge little by little. Belts go in the belt slot — there is one, so you choose a belt for the road. Next: "Riffle Belt".

kp: Бечевой пояс Towline Belt Бечевой пояс Towline Belt
nodes.hint: Way that gathers, like a boat on a towline. Study Waders.

pages.t: A Riffle Belt is for wet roads: fresh out of water or under rain you jump higher and run faster. Blue pebbles on a strap, like water on a riffle; on dry ground the belt is no different from a plain one. Next: "Landslide Belt".

kp: Пояс переката Riffle Belt Пояс переката Riffle Belt
nodes.hint: A riffle is the shallow, quick stretch of a river. Study the Towline Belt.

pages.t: A Landslide Belt is a strike from above: it throws you down and heaves the ground in a wave that scatters foes. Sneak in the air and the belt throws you down. Where you land from a height, the ground heaves in a wave of Strata: foes around are thrown back and held for a moment, the damage grows with the height, blocks stay whole. Your own fall hurts half as much. The wave costs charge.

kp: Пояс оползня Landslide Belt Пояс оползня Landslide Belt
nodes.hint: To come down like an undercut bank. Study the Riffle Belt.

pages.t: Settings are the base of trinkets: Confluence fills an empty pendant, ring or belt with power. A pendant, a ring and a belt of speculum — empty: no stone in the socket, no power of their own. They are worn in the slots of a slot mod. Opaline settings are finer: stronger weavings hold in them. Next: "Gale Ring".

kp: Бронзовая подвеска Speculum Pendant Бронзовое кольцо Speculum Ring Пояс с пряжкой Buckled Belt Опаловая подвеска Opaline Pendant Опаловое кольцо Opaline Ring Опаловый пояс Opaline Belt Бронзовое кольцо Speculum Ring
nodes.hint: Empty trinkets that power is poured into. Study the Confluence.

pages.t: A Gale Ring gives a dash in the air — wherever you look. A tiny brass vane sits on the band. Press jump in the air and the wind throws you forward, not up. One dash per flight, again after a short rest. Next: "Inquirer's Browband", "Bloom Charm", "Last-Minute Watch" and "Swift Feather".

Bond: a trinket with an effect grows by its own deed — a Gale Ring by dashes, a Locket by the charge it pours, belts by walking and by waves. Every bond brings a bead, and you set the bead into one of the trinket's numbers: dash reach, rest, rhythm. At bond five comes the turn: a new skill of the same deed. Right-click with the trinket in hand, or press Bond on the details screen, to open the bond window. It grows only while worn; the beads can be unstrung for experience levels and set anew.

kp: Кольцо Порыва Gale Ring Кольцо Порыва Gale Ring
nodes.hint: A second jump — where you look. Read a feather.

pages.t: A Swift Feather gives a second jump: press jump in the air and you push off the air itself, as if from the ground, one more block up. Once per flight and free: no charge, no rest — touch the ground and it is back. It is worn in the charm slot, with any armor.

If something else on you answers a jump in the air, the feather goes first, then the Gale Ring dash, and the Vane Mantle opens its vane last. A quick double jump in the Freshet Mantle still lifts you into flight. A swift's tail feather sits in a brass clasp with wing runes. Next: "Gale Treads".

kp: Перо стрижа Swift Feather Перо стрижа Swift Feather
nodes.hint: A second jump — off the air itself. Read a breeze rod.

pages.t: Gale Treads are boots for height: every jump from the ground throws you 3 blocks up — onto a ledge, a three-block wall, over a fence. The fall after your own jump is soft: only what lies below the spot you pushed off from counts. Crouch, and the jump is an ordinary one: for building, caves and low ceilings. They give almost no protection.

They jump on a flux charge but drink very little of it: one unit of charge lasts 32 jumps, a full charge about two thousand. In a chunk with at least three quarters of its bed in flux the boots drink it back by themselves, so in living places they do not run dry. Empty, they are plain boots and the jump is ordinary; a Charging Basin or a Flux Locket fills them. They make no sound: only a gust under the sole. Next: "Samara Hood".

kp: Ветроступы Gale Treads Ветроступы Gale Treads
nodes.hint: Boots that throw you three blocks up. Read a rabbit's foot.

pages.t: A Samara Hood guards you from falls: falls do not hurt at all, from any height, and from a height you fall half as fast as usual — not a glide, but time to look around. It needs no charge: protection that runs out would fail you over a cliff. It is worn on the head.

A fall speeds up as usual, but the hood falls no faster than six tenths of a block a tick: forty blocks take three and a half seconds instead of under two, a hundred take eight and a half instead of three; jumps and steps off a ledge stay the same. After eight blocks of falling, down streams behind your shoulders. The hood guards the head poorly, and no helmet goes over it; it is worn together with Gale Treads, the Vane Mantle and the Freshet Mantle. Its two brass-ribbed wings are cut like lumenash samaras.

kp: Капюшон-крылатка Samara Hood Капюшон-крылатка Samara Hood
nodes.hint: Falling — slower and painless. Read a phantom membrane.

pages.t: An Inquirer's Browband turns fights and digging into knowledge: part of the experience goes into Codex notes. A leather browband with a glass eye at the brow. The notes are of the chapter the strongest current of what you slay or dig up leads to. It is worn on the head, in the hat slot.

kp: Очелье пытливых Inquirer's Browband Очелье пытливых Inquirer's Browband
nodes.hint: Whatever you slay or dig up teaches you something. Study the Gale Ring.

pages.t: A Bloom Charm lifts poison and withering — while it has charge, and each time costs charge. A second Confluence over the charm teaches it a mode: the Healer heals when health runs low, the Provider feeds when you are hungry.

kp: Оберег Цвета Bloom Charm Оберег Цвета Bloom Charm
nodes.hint: A living flower that keeps poison away. Study the Gale Ring.

pages.t: The Last-Minute Watch saves you from death once a day: a deadly blow winds you back five seconds. You return to where you stood, with part of your health, and the watch stops for a day. The hands stop just short of twelve. It is a great Confluence: the altar needs calm.

kp: Часы последней минуты Last-Minute Watch Часы последней минуты Last-Minute Watch
nodes.hint: Once a day — the last few seconds back. Read a totem of undying.

pages.t: Wootz is steel with the property of currents in its pattern: sabers and garb made of it set alight, slow, heal or guard against lava. Brew Alloy, Lattice and Fray in equal measure in a Crucible on strong heat — the Poles argue, and that is where the pattern comes from — and add any currents you like. Throw in a brightsteel ingot: it will not float up but lie on the bottom. Take the heat away, and the Crucible cools for a minute.

Cooled, the Crucible gives up a wootz ingot: the pattern of the two strongest remaining currents shows on it, and all the distillate goes into the ingot, without murk. Touch the cooling Crucible — throw something in, bring the heat back — and the ingot turns to slag and the distillate to murk.

The pattern works as a faint weaving of its currents: Ember sets alight, Tide quickens in water, Rime slows, Bloom heals, Venom poisons, Fray strikes past armor. A thing of wootz takes the pattern of its ingots only if they all share it; different patterns or a plain ingot give motley wootz with no property. In a chunk where murk is above a third of the bed, the pattern goes dull. Next: "The Wootz Retort", "The Wellspring", "Wootz Saber" and "Wootz Garb".

kp: Полоса булата Wootz Strip Кусочек булата Wootz Nugget Слиток булата Wootz Ingot
nodes.hint: Steel with currents frozen in its waves. Study Weavings and Brightsteel.

pages.t: A Wootz Saber hits like a diamond sword and acts by its pattern as well: Ember sets alight, Rime slows, Bloom heals the hand. Two wootz ingots of one pattern and leather. With mastery the pattern bites harder. In a murky chunk it is only a saber.

kp: Булатная сабля Wootz Saber Булатная сабля Wootz Saber
nodes.hint: A blade whose strength is in its pattern. Study Wootz.

pages.t: Wootz Garb guards against the danger of its place: sewn with Ember it laughs at lava, with Tide it breathes long under water; the Vane Mantle for gliding grows from it too. Wootz damask — flux cloth woven with wootz wire — takes the pattern of its wootz nuggets. On two pieces the pattern is faint, on four it is at full strength.

Pattern's Answer: on four pieces a foe that strikes you up close gets the pattern's currents — Ember burns, Rime freezes, Tide throws back, Strata roots, Venom poisons, Bloom heals you. Pattern Flare: crouch twice and for ten seconds the pattern works twice as strong; it rests a minute. Flare before lava, the deep or a fight. Wet damask and a murky chunk silence both the answer and the flare.
The flaw: damask drinks water. In water the garb grows heavy, and for ten seconds after it the pattern stays silent. Diviner's Spectacles lenses are set into the hood.

Gliding. The heart of an Updraft on fluxsteel wire is a Vane; a Confluence grows it onto a Wootz Coat, and out comes a Vane Mantle. A jump in the air opens the vane: a slow glide forward, hold jump to hover, sneak to fold. It does not lift you: height comes from an Updraft or a cliff.

The mantle pays with flux: over a chunk with flux above three quarters of its bed, with the land's flux, otherwise with its own charge; in rain it glides for free. In a murky chunk and under water the vane will not open, and a strong blow folds it.

kp: Булатный дамаст Wootz Damask Булатный кафтан Wootz Coat Булатный капюшон Wootz Hood Булатные поножи Wootz Leggings Булатные сапоги Wootz Boots Крыльчатка Vane Крыльчатая мантия Vane Mantle Булатный кафтан Wootz Coat
nodes.hint: Cloth that guards against its own place. Study Wootz, the Fluxionist's Garb and the Updraft.

pages.t: The Freshet Garb gives free flight, as in creative mode, forever and with no flux: you need the mantle and any other piece. It also keeps you: the whole garb gives 20 more health and experience mends the thing in your hand, the hood sees in the dark, the leggings bring luck. Wootz damask re-melted in a Confluence with freshet sheets becomes Freshet Damask: streams run across it all the time. A Confluence remakes each Wootz Garb piece into a freshet one, and the Vane Mantle into the Freshet Mantle. The pattern of the damask is lost.

Flight. The mantle and any other piece: double-tap jump to take off and land, jump to rise, sneak to sink, sprint to fly twice as fast; falls cannot hurt you. The mantle drinks neither the chunk's flux nor a store of its own — fly as long as you like, and no blow knocks you out of the air. The garb's leggings carry you a third faster, and over running water and rivers flight is faster still.

In the Stillness the mantle is cold: before the Restart no one flies there, and after it only those who have studied Flight in the Stillness. The hood sees the currents, breathes in running water and gives steady night vision (take it off and it goes at once; a potion of night vision it leaves alone). The leggings give Luck +1: better catches when fishing, rarer finds in Reckoner coffers and murky geodes. The boots land in a splash. Running water mends the garb. The whole garb gives 20 more health, washes off what ails you in the rain, and picked-up experience mends the thing in your hand: two durability a point, and only what is left after Mending — experience is never spent twice.

kp: Вешний дамаст Freshet Damask Вешняя мантия Freshet Mantle Вешний капюшон Freshet Hood Вешние поножи Freshet Leggings Вешние сапоги Freshet Boots Вешняя мантия Freshet Mantle
nodes.hint: A garb of free flight. Study Freshet Steel and the Wootz Garb.

pages.t: The Freshet Scythe knocks down a crowd on open ground: hold the swing, and a spring wave runs along the ground, striking every foe in its way. It is made by Confluence: a wootz saber drawn out with freshet sheets becomes the Freshet Blade, willow bound in freshet steel becomes the Freshet Snath, and one more Confluence joins them into the Freshet Scythe.

Hold the swing until the scythe gathers water and let go: a spring wave runs along the ground — down slopes, a step up, on over water — knocking down every foe in its way. Water does not fly: at the edge of a cliff the wave breaks. It touches no blocks. In the Stillness the scythe gathers no water.

kp: Вешнее лезвие Freshet Blade Вешнее косьё Freshet Snath Вешняя коса Freshet Scythe Вешняя коса Freshet Scythe
nodes.hint: A scythe that sends a wave along the ground. Study Freshet Steel and the Wootz Saber.

pages.t: Bound Spring Tools serve without end: at rest — off the hand, in a lively chunk above three quarters of its bed — they mend themselves, a point every four seconds, and in the Stillness they do not wear at all: time stands there. Their ability and mastery stay as they were — the binding does not erase what the tool has learned. The price is Dissonance while the tool is in hand.

A great Confluence: a Spring Tool on the central plinth; around it a Hubstone, two stillmetal ingots and a thing of its Spring. The Confluence breaks the Hubstone's spoke of that same Spring; the hoe needs both Pole spokes. A bound tool is tougher than before and strikes a little harder.

kp: Bound Spring Tools Окованные орудия Истоков

Окованная кирка Жара Bound Ember Pickaxe Окованный топор Прилива Bound Tide Axe Окованная лопата Пласта Bound Strata Spade Окованная мотыга Полюсов Bound Pole Hoe Окованная кирка Жара Bound Ember Pickaxe
nodes.hint: Spring Tools bound in stillmetal: they mend themselves and never wear in the Stillness. Study Stillmetal and the Spring Tools; read a Hubstone.

pages.t: The Dissonant Eye makes flux crafting and casting cheaper at the cost of your Dissonance: each point of deep and ordinary Dissonance takes a hundredth off the price, up to a quarter. Ripple and gear Dissonance do not count. While the Eye is worn, Hush clears no Dissonance — neither hush water nor the Hush Fork: to calm your mind, take it off.

The Still taught that whoever has seen the stop no longer pays full price for motion. The Dissonant Eye is a novice's thing of theirs: stilled glass between two stillmetal lids, its iris never closing.

kp: Глаз разлада Dissonant Eye Глаз разлада Dissonant Eye
nodes.hint: A charm that takes its payment in Dissonance. Study Stillmetal and the Inquirer's Browband; know Dissonance above 10.

pages.t: Inscription gives any enchantment of the game at the level you want — exactly, without the enchanting table's lottery. A Confluence altar writes it like this: lay a thing the enchantment suits, or a book, on the central plinth, the inscription's things around it, vessels of its distillate nearby, and touch the Heart with the Conduit. A book comes out enchanted: an anvil lays it onto a thing. To begin: Sharpness I on a sword — two flints, an iron ingot and two parts each of Bane, Edge and Lattice.

The level of an enchantment is how much opaline lies on the plinths: the inscription's things give the first, each opaline beyond them one level more. Opaline remembers a level as it remembers the cut of a lens. Each level costs twice the distillate: Sharpness I is six parts, Sharpness V ninety-six. Raising Sharpness II to IV costs only the difference.

The higher the level, the more things on the plinths and the more distillate — and the heavier the Confluence: Sharpness I is simple, a bare altar holds it steady; Sharpness V is great and needs weirs and calm stones. The Heart tells you before you begin whether the calm will hold.

Inscription does not get around the rules of the world. Enchantments that contend will not lie on one thing: Sharpness, Smite and Bane of Arthropods; the protections among themselves; Fortune and Silk Touch; Mending and Infinity. Nothing goes above its highest level, and every other enchantment on the thing makes the price a quarter higher. The Heart tells you if the thing will not take the inscription.
The blade: Sharpness, Smite and Bane of Arthropods — on swords and axes, by Bane, Grave and Fang.
The blow: Knockback by Gale, Fire Aspect by Ember, Looting by Want.
Sweeping Edge — on swords; Lunge — on spears.
The tool: Efficiency by Edge, Fortune by Want, Silk Touch by Shift (it contends with Fortune).
Unbreaking — by Strata and Lattice: on anything that wears.
Armor: the four protections contend among themselves — choose what to guard against.
Projectile Protection and Thorns — on any armor; Feather Falling — on boots.
Underwater: Respiration and Aqua Affinity — on a helmet, Depth Strider — on boots.
The bow: Power, Punch, Flame.
Infinity (it contends with Mending) — on a bow; Multishot and Piercing contend — on a crossbow.
Quick Charge — by Tempo.
The trident: Loyalty, Riptide and Channeling — Riptide contends with the other two.
Impaling — on a trident; Luck of the Sea and Lure — on a fishing rod.
The mace: Density and Breach — they contend with Sharpness and with each other. Next: "Forgotten Enchantments".

nodes.hint: A Confluence writes an enchantment of the world into a thing — any one, at the level you need. Read an enchanting table or an enchanted book.

pages.t: Mending, Frost Walker, Soul Speed, Swift Sneak and Wind Burst never come from an enchanting table — but Confluence writes them. The table teaches what it has seen; these are found only in chests and with villagers. The currents remember them — and the altar writes them like the rest, only heavier: none of them is ever a simple Confluence.
Mending — a thing that heals itself with experience. It is always a great Confluence: build the altar with weirs and calm stones. It contends with Infinity, as it does in the world.
Frost Walker by Rime, Soul Speed by Soul: both on boots. Frost Walker contends with Depth Strider.
Swift Sneak by Sense and Gloom, on leggings; Wind Burst by Gale, on a mace. Next: "Unweaving Cloth" and "Rite Repair".

nodes.hint: There are enchantments an enchanting table does not remember. Read something that does: a bottle o' enchanting, soul sand, an echo shard, blue ice or a wind charge.

pages.t: Unweaving Cloth moves an enchantment from a thing into a book whole, at the same level — a grindstone would erase it. The cloth is sewn of flux cloth, and its flux thread can be drawn back out. Lay the cloth, a thing and a plain book on a crafting table: the cloth draws one enchantment out of the thing and lays it into the book. What comes out shows in the slot before you take it; the thing keeps all the rest.

The cloth draws the finest thread first — the rarest enchantment: Silk Touch, Mending or Fortune before Unbreaking and Sharpness; at equal rarity, the higher level. Curses it leaves alone. An enchanted book with several enchantments the cloth splits: the rare one goes into a plain book.
Without a book the cloth unravels the thing's last weaving: it is gone, and the strain goes with it. Enchantments it does not take without a book — a grindstone can wipe them all.

A cloth holds twenty-four threads. A transfer costs a thread per level, a forgotten enchantment twice that, a weaving three. The cloth gives back no distillate and no experience: what is taken does not flow back into the vessels, and the book takes the anvil's work cost from the thing.

kp: Расплетающий плат Unweaving Cloth Расплетающий плат Unweaving Cloth
nodes.hint: A grindstone erases enchantments — a cloth carries them over. Read a grindstone.

pages.t: Rite Repair gives a worn item back its durability and leaves everything else on it: enchantments, weavings, the Forge's tempering. The anvil's work cost does not grow — an item the anvil will no longer take ("Too Expensive!") the Confluence mends again and again. Lay the worn item on the central plinth, pieces of its material on the side plinths (the one an anvil takes: iron for iron, diamond for diamond), vessels of distillate nearby, and touch the Heart with the Conduit.

A piece of material mends a quarter of the durability. No more pieces than the item needs: the Heart asks you to take the extra ones off, and it will not take a whole item. The distillate goes by the wear: for each quarter, two parts of Craft and half the currents of the material itself (at most six parts of those). An iron pickaxe worn by a tenth needs three parts; one worn by nine tenths, nineteen.

A repair is a simple Confluence; a dear item (diamond, netherite, the workshop's metals) badly worn makes it middling, and then the altar needs its calm. An item with no repair material — a bow, a fishing rod — the rite does not mend. A repair changes only the wear: a tempered item stays tempered, a bought one stays bought.
Iron by iron, diamond by diamonds: on the card the item is worn by three quarters.

nodes.hint: A Confluence mends a worn item with its own material — the enchantments stay, and the anvil's price does not grow. Read an anvil.

pages.t: The Flux Sheath is a shield over your armor: golden hearts of absorption that refill from the land's flux. Each level of the Sheath on a piece of armor or a trinket setting gives half a heart of shield; everything you wear together gives no more than ten hearts. The shield refills half a heart every two seconds for one unit of the flux of the chunk under your feet; in a murky chunk, where murk is above a third of the bed, it does not charge, and once broken through it keeps still for five seconds.

The Sheath is written by Inscription: the thing on the central plinth, around it two pinches of quickdust and one opaline for each level above the first; Ward and Halo in the vessels, doubling with each level. The Sheath goes no higher than level five; it can be written into a book too, and the book goes onto a thing at an anvil.

nodes.hint: A shield of flux over your armor: golden hearts that refill from the land's flux. Study the Weavings and read a shield with the Loupe.

pages.t: Tuning Pegs let you switch a thing's weavings and enchantments off and on — each one on its own. What is off does nothing at all until you turn it back on: one pickaxe holds both Silk Touch and Fortune, Vein works only when you want it, and Pull stops dragging loot into a full inventory. The pegs are made on a Flux Workbench and put on at a crafting table: the pegs and a thing that holds at least one weaving, in any slots.

Over a pegged thing, hold the "Gear Details" key in any window with slots — a sheet of its weavings and enchantments opens, each with its own peg in a brass groove. A click on the row slides the peg: on the right, flux runs along the groove and it acts; on the left, the groove is empty and it is off. A thing of the world or of another mod gets the same sheet, only without lore. Pegs slide on a thing in your inventory; in a chest you can see them but not slide them.

Enchantments that contend lie on one thing together, but only one acts: turn Silk Touch on and Fortune falls asleep, and the other way round. That is how you gather them: switch Fortune off and lay a Silk Touch book on with an anvil. The pegs never switch off a curse. One enchantment never lies twice: a book or an Inscription over a sleeping one raises it no higher than the greater of the two.

While an enchantment is off, a grindstone, an enchanting table and an anvil (as the right-hand item) will not take the thing — turn it on first. The pegs do not change the anvil's work cost. A weaving that is off does not strain the thing: only the ones that are on make it tense, while the next weaving costs more for all of them.

kp: Колки Tuning Pegs Колки Tuning Pegs
nodes.hint: A weaving can be slackened like a string — and tightened again. Read a note block with the Loupe.

pages.t: A Memory Vessel keeps your experience safe: experience orbs within eight blocks flow to its neck and sink in — up to thirty levels' worth. Put it by a farm or wherever creatures fall, and no experience is lost while you are away. Right-click it with an empty hand and it gives you experience up to your next level; sneak, and it gives all of it.

Broken by hand, the vessel carries its experience along and keeps it when placed again; shattered by an explosion, it spills it out as orbs. A player close by takes orbs before the vessel does: an orb flies to the nearest. A comparator reads how full the vessel is.

The vessel is a good neighbor. Beside a Reckoning Desk it gives the Echo of Readings technique: the vessel's experience pays for a fork and a lock on a Riverbed board, and your notes stay whole. By an enchanting table it counts as a bookshelf.

A Frozen Thought sits in the vessel's neck — it froze along with a Laggard and remembers what was not its own. Confluence teaches it to remember yours too: experience that sinks into the jar becomes a pale light, and the thought's amber thread reaches down to it as to its own.

kp: Сосуд памяти Memory Vessel Сосуд памяти Memory Vessel
nodes.hint: A jar that keeps experience. Read a Frozen Thought or a Laggard.

pages.t: A second lining doubles the satchel: 108 slots, two panes side by side in one window. The Confluence remakes the same satchel — there is no need to take things out; they pass into the new one together with the pickup switch.
The seam between the linings glows with Weave — you can tell the step by it on your back too. The workshop takes from the double satchel just as from the plain one.

kp: Double-Lined Satchel Сума с двойным подкладом
Сума с двойным подкладом Double-Lined Satchel Сума с двойным подкладом Double-Lined Satchel
nodes.hint: Twice the room, the things stay. Study the satchel.

pages.t: The Gorge Ring holds a whole quarry of one block: tune it to stone, dirt, gravel or planks and everything above one stack goes inside — up to 100,000 blocks — and the stack in your inventory is topped up again when it runs low. For a digger, an empty inventory; for a builder, stock at hand: the Strata Spade and the Flux Trowel take blocks from it.

Use it on a block: an empty ring tunes to it, a filled one places a block from itself, the way a hand places from a stack. Sneak and use it to switch modes: asleep, gathering, grinding. In a window, a stack of the block onto the ring puts it in; a right click takes a stack out. It works worn in a ring slot or lying in the inventory.

A grinding Gorge Ring turns cheap stone and earth — cobblestone, gravel, cobbled deepslate, netherrack — into the chunk's murk: a pinch per stack, the way a dredge grinds its spoil. A full gathering ring grinds such surplus too and leaves anything of worth in your inventory. The ring takes only simple blocks with no data of their own: anything renamed or holding something stays with you.

kp: Прорва Gorge Ring Прорва Gorge Ring
nodes.hint: A ring of one block — a quarry in your pocket. Read obsidian.

pages.t: Automatons work for you: they gather and carry, reap and fell, quarry, stoke furnaces and guard the yard — by sigils painted on blocks. An automaton is not a game golem but a fluxionist's handiwork: a hull, a head with a mind, arms, legs and, if you like, an attachment. It is launched from a Slipway like a boat: the parts go on the cradle, the Slipway takes Cog distillate, and the finished automaton slides off down the runners.

The Slipway is woken with quickdust: set a piston, an anvil beside it, a chain above the anvil and a siphon above the piston — and sprinkle the anvil. Leave room in front of the anvil: the runners go down there.

The siphon above the frame pours only Cog into the oiler — up to 64 parts. An assembly costs 6 parts plus the price of the parts; a part goes every five ticks, and the parts show up on the cradle one by one. If the Cog runs out, the assembly waits.
Every part gives traits. Incompatible ones — Fine and Coarse, Buoyant and Ballasted, Brittle and Plated, Waterborne and Ballasted — the Slipway will not assemble, and it says why.
A roller is faster than legs but cannot jump: a one-block step is fine, anything higher is not.

An automaton works within 24 blocks of its home — at first, home is by the runners. It knows only the sigils it has seen, within eight blocks around: set them in a chain, closer than eight blocks to each other — that is its path. With nothing to do, it walks to the next sigil it knows and looks around. Sigils are painted with the Sigil Brush — the next entry, "Sigils".

A boundary keeps an automaton in its yard: two Boundary Stones stretch a veil of Ward that people and animals walk through, but automatons and monsters do not. An automaton goes around it like a wall.

kp: Счётный узел Tally Engine Простая голова Plain Head Ивовый корпус Willow Hull Простые руки Plain Arms Ноги Legs Каток Roller Межевой камень Boundary Stone Автоматон Automaton
nodes.hint: Workers of brass, wood and runes that read the sigils along their way. Read a golem.

pages.t: The hull decides where an automaton can work and what it does not fear. A willow hull is light and floats. An iron one is heavy, does not burn and shrugs off blasts. A terracotta one does not burn. A copper one oxidizes and slows down like copper — honeycomb on the automaton stops the patina.
A fluxsteel hull is as heavy as iron, but where the flux runs above its bed it works a fifth faster. A stillmetal hull mends itself — but only while it stands idle: still metal loves rest.
A wax hull holds two current inlays: runes press into soft wax best (the entry "Current Inlays"). But fire and lava burn it twice as hard — keep it away from forges and the Nether.

A burl hull is a living burl of wood that is still growing: under the open sky by day it closes its wounds three times faster than Self-Mending, and it holds two inlays. It is the frailest of hulls, and in a cave or at night it does not mend at all.

kp: Железный корпус Iron Hull Терракотовый корпус Terracotta Hull Медный корпус Copper Hull Флюкс-стальной корпус Fluxsteel Hull Восковой корпус Wax Hull Наплывной корпус Burl Hull Железный корпус Iron Hull
nodes.hint: What the body is made of decides what it can do. Read iron or copper.

pages.t: Sigils are orders for automatons: a mark on a block says what to do within its circle. A sigil is not carried in your inventory — it is painted. Take the Sigil Brush, the ink of your sigil in the other hand, and press a block face: the mark shows on it. A pot of ink lasts sixteen strokes.

Ink is brewed in the Crucible: Ink Base — glowing ink with Bind and Craft — and each ink is the base and the currents of its task. The first inks are Gather and Stow (the entry "Gather and Stow"): the automaton picks up what lies about and carries it to a chest.
To erase a sigil, wet the brush: dip it in water or a cauldron, and it washes off eight sigils. Someone else's sigil cannot be erased: it belongs to whoever painted it.

Use the Bosun's Pipe on your sigil to set it up: its circle (how many blocks it takes), its flag, its filter. A sigil with a flag calls only automatons with a flag of the same color — the flag is given on the Slipway with a dye.

kp: Кисть сигилов Sigil Brush Основа туши Ink Base Кисть сигилов Sigil Brush
nodes.hint: Command marks painted right onto blocks. Read an ink sac.

pages.t: Gather and Stow tidy up for you: the automaton picks up what has fallen and carries it to a chest. Gather: the automaton picks up what has fallen within the sigil's circle. The filter says what to take; empty — everything.
Stow is painted on a storage — a chest, a barrel, a box: that is where the automaton puts its load. Without a Stow that will take it, it carries the load around. Next: "Unload" and "The Porter".

A Stow set to "like with like" sorts a mixed chest for you: switch on "Like with like" in the sigil's window, and that Stow takes only what its storage already holds. Put one sample in each chest, paint Stows "like with like" on them and Unload on the mixed chest: the automaton carries everything to its place and leaves what has no place.

kp: Gather and Stow Подбор и склад
Тушь «Подбор» Gather Ink Тушь «Склад» Stow Ink Тушь «Подбор» Gather Ink
nodes.hint: Pick up what fell and put it in a chest.

pages.t: Unload empties a storage for you — a furnace into a chest, a chest of spoils into a store. Painted on a storage, it says to take from it, but only what some known Stow on another storage will take. Next: "Issue and Reserve".

kp: Тушь «Выгрузка» Unload Ink Тушь «Выгрузка» Unload Ink
nodes.hint: Take from a storage and carry it off. Discover Hollow.

pages.t: Patrol guards the yard: fighters strike monsters in the circle and walk the ring of sigils. Only fighters read Patrol: an automaton with a Combat Core on its back or with fighting arms. Set Patrol sigils around a yard. Next: "Cull", "Hooks and Slings" and "Sentry Arbalests".

kp: Тушь «Дозор» Patrol Ink Боевой узел Combat Core Тушь «Дозор» Patrol Ink
nodes.hint: Fighters guard a circle. Discover Bane.

pages.t: Cull keeps a herd in check: the automaton culls the extra grown animals and leaves two for breeding. Cull is for retentive fighters: the kind comes from the filter, the animals from the circle.

kp: Тушь «Забой» Cull Ink Тушь «Забой» Cull Ink
nodes.hint: Two are kept for breeding. Discover Fang.

pages.t: Operate uses a thing on a block as a player would: bone meal on a sapling, a bucket on a cauldron, a hand on a lever — it needs Fine Fingers. Fine Fingers are for fine work. They are brittle: no Plating goes with them.
Operate says to use an item on the block it is painted on, as a player would: bone meal on a sprout, a bucket on a cauldron, a bare hand on a lever or a button. The fine and retentive read it.

The filter is the item for the hand: the automaton takes it from its load, or unloads it from a storage with Unload; an empty filter means a bare hand. It presses once every few seconds — the number in the sigil's window. Whatever is left in the hand goes into the load and on to a Stow. Next: "Reap".

kp: Тонкие пальцы Fine Fingers Тушь «Рычаг» Operate Ink Тонкие пальцы Fine Fingers
nodes.hint: Fine fingers press like a player. Discover Edge.

pages.t: Reap is a farm without hands: the automaton harvests what is ripe and plants again. A fine, retentive automaton reads it: it harvests in the circle and replants from the same harvest — grain, wart, cocoa, berries off the bush, pumpkins and melons by the stem, the upper joints of cane and bamboo. The filter is what gets planted: a seed or the crop. The harvest goes into the load and on to a Stow.

kp: Тушь «Урожай» Reap Ink Тушь «Урожай» Reap Ink
nodes.hint: Harvest what is ripe and plant it again. Discover Root.

pages.t: Pick Arms are for quarrying: a quarrying automaton breaks blocks but cannot carry. Picks instead of hands. Next: "Quarry and Fell" and "Clinging Legs".

kp: Кирочные руки Pick Arms Кирочные руки Pick Arms
nodes.hint: Arms that break stone. Read a pickaxe.

pages.t: Quarry and Fell mine stone and timber for you. Quarry breaks the filtered blocks in the circle — layer by layer, from the top down; an empty filter breaks nothing, and storages and sigils are never touched. With a double outline — with silk touch: the block comes away whole.

Fell is for the retentive: the automaton fells trees in the circle (not log buildings — a tree has a living crown) and plants a sapling of the same tree in its place if it carries one. Saplings fall from the leaves — let a Gather pick them up.

kp: Quarry and Fell Выработка и рубка
Тушь «Выработка» Quarry Ink Тушь «Рубка» Fell Ink Тушь «Выработка» Quarry Ink
nodes.hint: Break by filter, fell and plant.

pages.t: The Bosun's Pipe commands automatons: call them along, leave them working here, send them back to the Slipway. A whistle is a signal to your automatons within 24 blocks; on an automaton — to it alone. Sneak and whistle into the air to change the signal: "Follow me", "Stay here" (home is where it stands; it works around), "To the Slipway" and "Follow and gather".

The pipe in hand shows the circles of the sigils around and the path between them — marks closer than eight blocks are joined by a dashed line — and over your automatons a diamond in the color of their signal. Sneak and use the pipe on your automaton: it folds into its item with everything it carried. Next: "The Porter" and "Tally Ledger".

kp: Боцманская дудка Bosun's Pipe Боцманская дудка Bosun's Pipe
nodes.hint: A whistle automatons obey.

pages.t: A Porter follows you and picks up what falls — with twice the load. A Pannier on the back doubles the load. On the signal "Follow and gather" such an automaton follows you. It does not teleport: one left behind waits, and the pipe in hand shows where it is.

nodes.hint: An automaton with a Pannier follows you.

pages.t: A Quickened Thought makes an automaton retentive: it reads double outlines and works faster with experience. In the Stillness people stopped mid-step, and their thoughts stand still with them. A Confluence can wake a thought within a Tally Engine — it will remember and learn. It takes a Frozen Thought: Laggards drop it.
A Thinking Head makes a retentive automaton: it reads double outlines and gains knack — five steps, each an eighth faster. It is brittle; under a helm it is not.

Double outline: press your sigil with the same brush and the same ink — a second ring lies down in gold (two strokes). A sigil in a double outline has a filter of nine items and "all but these"; Patrol gets a choice of targets, Quarry silk touch, Stow a limit per item.

A thought remembers whose it was. Standing idle near its owner, a retentive automaton now and then murmurs a scrap of someone else's life — the one who froze mid-step: where he was going, what he never finished. It is neither an order nor a fault; a Thinking head also holds one more current inlay (the entry "Current Inlays").

kp: Ожившая мысль Quickened Thought Мыслящая голова Thinking Head Мыслящая голова в шлеме Helmed Thinking Head Ожившая мысль Quickened Thought
nodes.hint: A thought thawed out of one who froze. Discover Mind, read a Frozen Thought or a Laggard.

pages.t: An Eyepiece widens the yard: a Seeing Head makes a far-seeing automaton that works up to 36 blocks from home. It is brittle.

kp: Глазок Eyepiece Зрячая голова Seeing Head Зрячая мыслящая голова Seeing Thinking Head Глазок Eyepiece
nodes.hint: An opaline lens sees farther. Discover Sense.

pages.t: Clinging Legs are for walls and cliffs: a clinging automaton leans on a wall and climbs it like a spider. Next: "Float" and "Paddles".

kp: Цепкие ноги Clinging Legs Цепкие ноги Clinging Legs
nodes.hint: Walk up walls. Read a spider.

pages.t: A Float lets an automaton hover in the air. A waxed bladder over a swirl of Gale: the automaton hovers, slower and more brittle.

nodes.hint: Hover on Gale. Read something that flies.

pages.t: Paddles are for work in and under water: such an automaton is waterborne. Paddles do not go with Ballasted.

nodes.hint: Work in water. Read a fish.

pages.t: A fighter's arms: Hooks strike up close, Slings from afar, Plating takes the blows. Hooks hit hard and knock back, but cannot carry.

Slings throw stones from afar: a fighter with Slings keeps ten blocks away and never closes in. The stones are its own: give the automaton gravel or cobblestone (up to a stack of one kind); without them the Slings stay silent, and the Loupe says "Slings empty". One throw, one stone.
Plating means more armor and a heavier step; it does not go with Brittle.

kp: Hooks and Slings Крючья и пращи
Крючья Hooks Пращи Slings Обшивка Plating Крючья Hooks
nodes.hint: A fighter's arms and armor. Read a dispenser.

pages.t: Issue and Reserve keep supplies on their own: a furnace always has coal, a workbench always has planks. Issue, painted on a storage, answers orders: things are taken from it for a Reserve, for an Operate and by the Ledger. By itself it carries nothing out.

Reserve keeps a number of the filtered items in its storage (the number is in the sigil's window). The automaton takes the shortfall from a known Issue or Stow on another storage and carries it over — so the furnace always has coal and the workbench always has planks. Next: "Tally Ledger".

kp: Issue and Reserve Выдача и запас
Тушь «Выдача» Issue Ink Тушь «Запас» Reserve Ink Тушь «Выдача» Issue Ink
nodes.hint: Storages that order and hand out by themselves. Discover Want.

pages.t: The Ledger brings a thing from your chests straight to your hands — an automaton fetches it. It lists everything that lies in your chests with a Stow or an Issue sigil within 24 blocks: a stow chest is a store in itself and needs no second sigil. Click an item and a free automaton of yours that knows such a chest takes it and brings it: left click — a stack, right click — one, with Shift — as much as it can carry. A long list scrolls with the wheel.

kp: Ведомость Tally Ledger Ведомость Tally Ledger
nodes.hint: A book of everything kept at Issue. Discover Mind.

pages.t: A Sentry Arbalest guards the yard by itself: it turns on its post toward a monster within 16 blocks and shoots arrows from its drum while it sees the target. Load it with arrows — by hand or with a hopper; sneak-use empty-handed to unload. The arrows can be picked up.

The Keen Arbalest reaches 24 blocks, shoots faster and truer, and hears: a step or a voice in its circle — and it has already turned. Empty-handed, its owner chooses the targets: monsters, plus players, plus animals, or all. Next: "The Dredge".

kp: Сторожевой самострел Sentry Arbalest Зоркий самострел Keen Arbalest Сторожевой самострел Sentry Arbalest
nodes.hint: A crossbow that keeps watch by itself. Read a crossbow.

pages.t: The Dredge digs a tunnel and picks the ore out of its walls on its own while you are busy with other things. Put a pickaxe in its wheel and give it a redstone signal — it gnaws a tunnel ahead step by step, up to 64 blocks. The pickaxe's enchantments work — Fortune, Silk Touch, Efficiency, Unbreaking — and the pickaxe wears out.

Above all, it sifts: ore within two blocks of the tunnel — in the walls, floor and roof and behind them — is picked out on the way. With Vein on the pickaxe it takes the whole connected vein and digs up to 96 blocks.

Choose the cut in the Dredge's window — use it empty-handed: 1×2, 3×3 or 5×5, and 7×7 with a Survey III lens in the wheel. The wider the cut, the more blocks a step and the more flux it costs; the wheel takes one block at a time, so a wide tunnel takes longer. Sweep on the pickaxe takes 3×3 of the cut in one blow.

A cut Conduit lens goes into the wheel's hub — use the lens on it; its nodes change the work. Scorch smelts: ore comes out as ingots. Chill freezes water and lava around the tunnel without spending stone. Crack splits soft rock faster, Excavate takes blocks whole, Reverb gives ore an echo of Fortune, Fork sifts four blocks out. Each costs flux; a cheap lens muddies as well.

Holes, water and lava around the tunnel are sealed with its own stone — the tunnel neither floods nor caves in; every eight steps it sets a torch if there is one in the chest behind it. The spoil goes into that chest: valuables first, then rubble; when the chest is full it waits and spills nothing. Every block costs flux from the chunk being dug, and the deeper, the dearer.

A Stow sigil painted on the chest behind it decides what to keep: its filter is what goes into the chest. Rubble the filter refuses, the wheel grinds away — rough work that leaves murk in the chunk; ore and anything of value is never ground: what the filter refuses goes down the chute.

Put the Dredge on a minecart and the tunnel no longer ends at block sixty-four. The Minecart with Dredge crawls along the rails, and where they end it digs a cut, sifts the ore out of the walls, lines it and lays a rail from its own box. Only the rails and torches in its box, the pickaxe and the flux hold it back. It does not haul rock — it grinds it (murk in the chunk); the box is for ore. A powered activator rail stops it.

kp: Землечерпалка Dredge Вагонетка с землечерпалкой Minecart with Dredge Землечерпалка Dredge
nodes.hint: Buckets that dig a tunnel and sift out ore. Discover Strata.

pages.t: An inlay makes a finished automaton faster, stronger, keener or fiercer — without taking it apart. Use the inlay on your automaton to press it into a plank of the Sigil ring around the window on its chest: the plank lights up in the color of its current. There is one slot; speculum, fluxsteel, wax and burl hulls have two; a Thinking head adds one more. At most two of one current.

Gale is lightness: a step 12% faster, Operate presses a quarter more often. Strata is strength: one more stack of load, fells and quarries faster, hits harder. Ember: its blows set foes alight. Tide is senses: sigils seen farther, a wider circle of work, truer Slings.
Lattice is order: a fighter strikes whoever hurt its owner. Fray is thorns: whoever strikes it is struck back. Angle has its own use for each inlay (the entry "Angle").

Shears on your automaton take an inlay off whole — the last one first. When the pipe takes an automaton apart, its inlays go into its item and come back with it; one that is destroyed loses them with its hull.

kp: Накладка Порыва Gale Inlay Накладка Пласта Strata Inlay Накладка Строя Lattice Inlay Накладка Жара Ember Inlay Накладка Прилива Tide Inlay Накладка Распада Fray Inlay Накладка Порыва Gale Inlay
nodes.hint: Planks of the Sigil ring filled with a current. Read a Spring shard.

pages.t: Trappings are a small but visible help: each sits on the model and gives something. Use one on your automaton to put it on: one on top of the head, one on the face, one under the throat. Shears take trappings off whole; a destroyed automaton drops them.
The Tricorne gives a quarter more health. The Willow Wreath: living twigs mend one health every four seconds. The Opaline Monocle: sigils seen two blocks farther (a Seeing head has no use for it).

The Brass Visor gives a fighter two armor, and foes it slays drop experience and loot as if by your hand, when you are within 32 blocks. The Wax Rosette quickens its step. Helmed and Seeing heads cannot wear a visor.

kp: Треуголка Tricorne Ивовый венок Willow Wreath Латунное забрало Brass Visor Опаловый монокль Opaline Monocle Сургучная розетка Wax Rosette Треуголка Tricorne
nodes.hint: A hat, a monocle, a rosette — each with a use. Read wool.

pages.t: Angle feeds you fish without you: an automaton with Fine Fingers stands by the sigil and fishes in the still water of its circle, carrying the catch to a Stow. Give it a fishing rod with a right click (or let Unload take one from a chest) and paint Angle by the water. The rod wears with every catch, as yours does; its Lure and Luck of the Sea work.

The catch is the same as a rod's: fish, junk, and in open water (five by five blocks and more than one deep) treasure too. The sigil's filter says what to keep: the rest goes back into the water. An automaton brings no experience.
Inlays for Angle: Gale sometimes lands two at once; Ember cooks the fish at once (for the chunk's flux); Tide makes them bite sooner; Lattice brings more luck; Fray throws junk back once more.

kp: Тушь «Лов» Angle Ink Тушь «Лов» Angle Ink
nodes.hint: An automaton with a fishing rod fishes for you. Read a fishing rod.

pages.t: A Mooring Bollard puts your automatons' work on a clock, a daylight sensor or a lever. While the bollard has a redstone signal, every automaton that comes within two blocks of it drops its task and stands on a rope of light. When the signal goes, the rope fades and it goes back to work.

kp: Причальная тумба Mooring Bollard Причальная тумба Mooring Bollard
nodes.hint: Hold automatons on a line while a signal burns.

pages.t: Laggards drop Frozen Thought: you inhale it for notes of the Stillness, the Memory Vessel stands on it, and no automaton's thought can be quickened without it. A Laggard freezes mid-step, and a pale double walks ahead of him toward you: where the double stops, there he will rush — three times as fast as a zombie. Strike while he stands, and do not stand where the double stopped.

His touch drags time: for two seconds you are slowed. By day he does not burn but stands twice as long, and after a minute of light time catches up with him — he crumbles into rime and leaves nothing. A Laggard drops a Frozen Thought two times in five; Looting adds a tenth per level.

A Laggard Brute froze longer than any: he roams the Stagnant Backwater by night and the Midstep Outskirts at any hour. Every blow shakes time back into him — he stands shorter, rushes farther and faster, his cracks burn brighter, the rime crust on his shoulder falls away; up to five times, and without blows he falls behind again, once every six seconds. Let him stand, and strike when you mean to finish. He always drops a Frozen Thought, and now and then a Still Memory.

Everything in the world is a frozen current. The Stillness leaks into the world, and now and then a man falls behind his own moment: he stands while time moves on, and then rushes after it. He cannot catch it — time is always a step ahead, and only the morning brings them together.

nodes.hint: People who fell behind their own moment come out at night. Read a Laggard with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Sentry Conduit guards your yard with your lens: it turns its bracer toward a monster within 12 blocks and casts at it while it sees it. With a Mend lens it is a healer at the gate: it heals your wounded — players, tamed animals, villagers — and, with none of them hurt, burns the undead. Use a cut lens on it to set it, sneak-use empty-handed to take it out, use it empty-handed to see what it is doing; only its owner touches the lens.

It takes flux from its own chunk by the rules of a cast: the lens's price, strength by how dry the place is, a weak cast and a fizzle at the bottom; murk as the lens blank leaves it. It never changes blocks: lenses with Survey, Excavate, Swap or Washout do not fit it, nor do traceries. Jet, Droplet and Moth strike as a beam, Palm point-blank, Mist and Pool as a flash of a circle at the target, Spray at several targets, Fork hops, Echo repeats at half strength. It casts at most once a second; sentries heal one wounded friend at most once a second, however many of them stand there.

The sentry sleeps while no player is within 64 blocks and under a redstone signal: no searching, no flux. Awake, it looks for a target twice a second and hears like the Keen Arbalest: a step or a voice in its circle — and the bracer has already turned. It never strikes its owner or your own: its targets are monsters only, and it leaves calm endermen and zombified piglins alone. What it kills gives no experience — as with an arbalest's arrows.

kp: Сторожевой проводник Sentry Conduit Сторожевой проводник Sentry Conduit
nodes.hint: A lens that keeps watch by itself. Study Sentry Arbalests and Lenses.

nodes.n: The Order of the Still Hour

pages.t: The Order of the Still Hour is the fluxionist's enemy: its bands set Halt Stones by workshops, and its masters guard the Stillness. Among the Reckoners were clockmakers: they measured Tempo, how fast everything in the world flows, and decided that perfection lies in rest: a stopped current does not spoil. They worked the Great Stilling, and a part of the world froze whole.

A Still Grain is a seed of that frozen world. It holds Alloy and Still, and the Loupe hears a silence in it that no living metal has. A Snarl gives the grains up when it is untangled: what got stuck in the dead flux came from there. The sign of the Order is the Hour Dial: a clock face whose hands stand at the Still Hour. It is on the Order's banners too: Bellringers pray at such a banner, and a Still Hour Pattern weaves it on a loom.

kp: The Order of the Still Hour Орден Недвижного Часа
nodes.hint: Those who once stopped the world want to do it again. Read a Still Grain or a person of the Order with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Clockbound are the Order's fighters: they strike in series of three, faster than any living man, and then lie open — that is when to strike. A novice who joins the Order gives up his Tempo; in its place a wind-up is set into his chest, a brass case of gears with a key in the back. When the wind runs out, the doors on his chest swing open, and he stands until the key turns again.

Strike while he unwinds: the open mechanism takes blows half again as hard. Dying, a Clockbound sets free its Escapement, the heart of its movement, still ticking and looking for a bare head. Crouch and it falls off; a helmet keeps it away entirely.

nodes.hint: The Order's novices tick. Read a Clockbound or its Escapement with the Loupe.

nodes.n: The Rule of the Still Hour

pages.t: The Rule tells what to expect from the Order: to a workshop where flux runs at twice its riverbed, the Still will come to set a Halt Stone. First rule: all that flows spoils. Second: what is stopped is perfect. Third: the Tempo of the world is a debt, and the Order will collect it. The Rule bids its people wear wax on their lips, for words flow too, and ring a bell with no tongue.

The Still come into the ordinary world on a round: to a workshop where flux runs at twice its riverbed, a party steps out of a Still Window and sets a Halt Stone; around it water turns to glass and devices stand, until the stone is broken. The Rule calls this mercy.

kp: The Rule of the Still Hour Устав Недвижного Часа
Устав Недвижного Часа Rule of the Still Hour
nodes.hint: The rules of the Order open to one already drawn to rest. Read the Rule once your Dissonance passes 25.

pages.t: The Stillness is the world of the Great Stilling: Stillmetal Veins and Grain Drifts, the Order's cities, its masters and the Heart of the Stilling are there. There is no flux: the Conduit and devices are silent, and only what lies in a Thaw Lantern's circle flows. The sun stands at the horizon — the very Still Hour. Water is glass, fire is cold light, dust and drops hang in the air, people froze mid-step.

The way in is the same Sluice Arch that leads to the Quickstream: flux pays the way there, stillness pays it here. Build a frame four by five of Reckoner stone (corners as you like) and leave the two-by-three opening empty. Keep three Still Grains in your inventory and throw a pinch of Quickdust on the frame: the opening is veiled with stilled air. Step into it and stay — the world freezes, turns white, and you are there. Grains found earlier wait for this entry: without it the arch to the Stillness stays cold.

On the other side an arch of stillstone bricks waits for you: stand in its veil the same way and you return to your own. What you bring flows only in the circle of a Thaw Lantern. The Conduit, devices and the Flux Workbench are silent there: there is no flux.

nodes.hint: A world where nothing flows. The arch is learned in the Quickstream: pass an arch into it, then read a Gauge Ring — an arch once stood in its middle.

pages.t: A Thaw Lantern is your light in the Stillness: in its circle everything flows again, and a Stillmetal Vein gives Freshet Ore. A brass lantern with a current shard burning in its cradle. While it burns, for eight blocks around water pours, fire burns out, hanging dust settles, stilled people finish their step: some crumble into rime, leaving a Still Memory, others walk on as Laggards. When the lantern goes out, the circle stills again.
