A primal current shard burns for a minute, an Ember shard for two; the cradle holds up to four minutes. Use the lantern with an empty hand to see how long it will still burn. A Stillmetal Vein broken in its circle gives not grains but Freshet Ore: metal that began to flow again.

kp: Талый фонарь Thaw Lantern Талый фонарь Thaw Lantern
nodes.hint: A light by which the stilled moves again. Read Stilled Water or a Halted Flame with the Loupe.

pages.t: Stillmetal mends itself while it lies idle; it makes armor that cannot be stopped, weapons that slow a foe, and still devices. Still Grains thrown into a Crucible boiling over lava with Alloy and Still fuse into an ingot. Grain Drifts and Stillmetal Veins of the Stillness give the grains; the veins want an iron pickaxe.
Stillmetal loves rest: what is made of it mends while it lies idle, and Dissonance presses on whoever wears it. Nine ingots make a block, three ingots make three plates.

From plates the Flux Workbench forges stillmetal armor: whoever wears it cannot be stopped, and a foe who strikes it up close freezes with rime; on four pieces stopping effects do not take hold at all. Crouch twice while walking forward — Unstoppable Rush: six blocks along your gaze, foes in the way are thrown aside and slow. The stillmetal sword and tools strike so that the foe lingers. Stillmetal wears out fast, but idle in your inventory it mends itself.

kp: Слиток стылого металла Stillmetal Ingot Блок стылого металла Block of Stillmetal Пластина стылого металла Stillmetal Plate Стылая кираса Stillmetal Cuirass Стылый меч Stillmetal Sword Слиток стылого металла Stillmetal Ingot
nodes.hint: The metal of things that do not change. Read a Still Grain or a Stillmetal Vein with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Restart Sluice lets the land of the Stillness go, forever. Set it anywhere in the Stillness and put in a trophy of an Order guardian — a Bell Tongue or a Prior's Seal: a thaw patch, a scrap of the Thawed, opens forty blocks around. There water flows and fire burns, you can sleep and set your spawn, beasts come, the riverbed is 120, above a river's, and Stillmetal Veins give Freshet Ore. It is a place for a home and a workshop in the Stillness, before the Restart and after.

The trophy goes into the sluice in five seconds: the sluice's clock stops, runes of Tempo gather in a ring, and the land gives way in a wave from the sluice. Break the sluice sooner, and the trophy falls out whole. Thaw patches do not merge: at least 32 blocks of still land lie between two. The land of the Founder's Hall the sluice does not let go: only the Restart does. The sluice itself can be taken up and set again: what was let go does not freeze back.

By the founder's dais in the Founder's Hall the sluice waits for something else: the Heart of the Stilling. A lantern lets time go for minutes; the Heart held it for ages. Set the Heart in while all four riverbeds of the Springs flow: the streams gather to it around the Wheel, and it beats faster and faster. The Order will not allow it: the stilled at the edge of the Hall step from their places and put out the riverbeds; light them again with shards of their Springs. This is the Restart: the Stillness is started once for the whole world.

kp: Пусковой шлюз Restart Sluice Пусковой шлюз Restart Sluice
nodes.hint: Can the Stillness be let go? Read an Order guardian's trophy or the Heart of the Stilling with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Restart has thawed the land around the Founder's Hall forever — its flux is richer than a river's — and now the Stillness gives up its artifacts. The heart beat. For the first time since the day of the Great Stilling, the Stillness took a step, and it could not stop. The glass waterfalls fell as water, the fire that stood as light burned out, and the people caught mid-step finished their step.

The Reckoners wanted to reckon the world, the Still wanted to stop it. Neither came true: a stopped current does not die, it waits. By the founder's dais it has waited long enough: the land around the Hall flows like spring, and its flux runs richer than a river's. Beyond it, the Stillness stands as it stood.

In the Bell Tower, in the Clock Tower and in the City of Midstep the last of the Still keep their hour. They say the Order can repeat it: wind the Pendulum and raise the founder onto his dais. The Restart Sluice beats: a Heart set into it comes out started.

nodes.hint: The Heart of the Stilling goes into the Restart Sluice by the founder's dais while the four riverbeds flow. Be there at the Restart, or start your own heart in the beating sluice.

names: the Restart Sluice beating under the Loupe

pages.t: The Watch of the Unmoving stops time around you — for eight blocks and four seconds: blows on what is frozen build up and land all at once. The Order dreamed of carrying the still moment with them; a heart that was never started is that very moment: set it into a watch in place of the works, and the lid, clicking, stops time.

Inside the sphere creatures, arrows, falling blocks and items stand; blows on the stilled do not land, they gather and fall all at once when time goes on. Masters only slow down, and the Unmoving himself is not touched: this is his time. Then the watch winds for two minutes from the flux where you stand; in the frozen Stillness it does not wind. Each stop costs Ripple 3.

kp: Watch of the Unmoving Часы Неподвижного
Часы Неподвижного Watch of the Unmoving Часы Неподвижного Watch of the Unmoving
nodes.hint: A Heart of the Stilling that was never started keeps the stop inside it. Read one with the Loupe after the Restart.

pages.t: A Restart Heart gives a workshop that cannot run dry: wherever it stands outside the Stillness, the 5×5 chunks keep a riverbed of at least 120, and what you drink refills three times faster. A started heart beats once a second, and the land around flows like spring.

Cleanliness is the condition. Murk in its chunk above a third of the riverbed makes the heart stumble, and the land around goes back to its own riverbed until the murk falls below a sixth. Two hearts closer than four chunks do not beat together: the later one keeps silent. A comparator by the heart catches every beat, a clock for redstone.

nodes.hint: A heart started in the sluice comes out warm. Read it with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Rewind Weight gives back the damage of the last five seconds as health and strikes everyone nearby with its swing. A pendulum swings there and back: the weight on your belt remembers the blows, and when they add up to two fifths of your health and you still live, it swings back.
The weight does not undo death: the Last-Minute Watch does that, and you may wear both. After a swing the weight rests for a minute and a half. Damage from players it returns only by half.

kp: Возвратный груз Rewind Weight Возвратный груз Rewind Weight
nodes.hint: After the Restart the gate clock of the Founder's Hall runs on its own, and the Pendulum Bob is free. Read it with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Crown of the Wheel will not be stopped: slowness, fatigue, the Numb Hand, Under the Bell, the circles of Halt Stones and another's Watch of the Unmoving slide off it; it is also the strongest boon to a Confluence and a view of the world's flux. It is a thin circlet with six spokes: whoever wears it holds the Wheel. Only the masters of the Order break through the Crown by half: their stop holds half as long.

The Crown is the strongest gift to a Confluence of all the gear: more calm, calming every second, lighter eddies, less distillate. It is made first: the other finale artifacts are great Confluences. In its set it counts as the Stillweave Hood.

With the Gaze key the wearer sees the flow of the world: streams run along the ground from a full chunk to an empty one in the colors of the local currents, murk hangs as a dark haze, Skeins and Snarls shine as marks through walls, and whatever you look at shows its currents at once. A pale wheel turns above the gazer's head, and others see it too. Reading is still the Loupe's work.

kp: The Crown of the Wheel Венец Колеса
Венец Колеса Crown of the Wheel Венец Колеса Crown of the Wheel
nodes.hint: The head of the Order wore his power on his lips, as a Seal. Read the Prior's Seal with the Loupe after the Restart.

pages.t: The Repeat of the Hour lets you fight the Unmoving and the Great Pendulum again — harder and for greater rewards. The Order answers the Restart: its hour can be wound again. Set the Winding Key into the founder's dais and the Unmoving comes out, and while he lives the riverbeds of the Hall stand as glass again; into the dead dial of the Clock Tower, and the Great Pendulum. Sneak with the key to turn it once, twice or three times.

Every turn is stronger: more health, heavier blows, shorter rests between moves; at three turns he is also harder to hurt, and the Sentinels come out at once. From two turns he calls for help in the first phase already, and one more; at three "the Hour holds": every half minute a Still Ring runs out from him — jump it or stand still. A trophy and a Hubstone go to each who dealt a tenth of the damage; at two turns the Hubstone is whole, at three there are two trophies, and the first time also a Running Dial.

kp: The Repeat of the Hour Повтор часа
Заводной ключ Winding Key Заводной ключ Winding Key
nodes.hint: The last of the Still keep their hour even after the Restart. Read their Rule with the Loupe.

pages.t: A whole Hubstone in the Conduit's socket becomes the hub of a wheel with four lenses on the rim, one per Spring. In the Wheel mode the lenses strike at once: the carrier of the Tide lens, the actions of all four (the same action one step higher), three quarters of the pressure each. It costs three quarters of the sum and rests half again as long as the slowest lens.

Opposite Springs clash at the target without murk: Scorch with Chill as blinding steam, Gust with Crack as rubble that throws foes up and cracks soft blocks. The Pole spokes in the hub hold them in check, as Lattice holds the threads of a skein. The mode — the Wheel or one lens of its socket — is picked on the lens wheel: hold …; sneak and right-click for the next mode.

The Wheel needs a Great Lens Blank: a Lens Blank grown by strong Confluence — a Hubstone gives it its Lattice spoke, opaline grows the glass, stillmetal rings it. Thirty-six facets, up to three carriers in a conjunction and four actions; its lenses leave no murk, and their cooldown grows half as fast. It is cut at the same Lens Grinder.

kp: Проводник Колеса Wheel Conduit Большая заготовка линзы Great Lens Blank Проводник Колеса Wheel Conduit
nodes.hint: A Hubstone of six spokes holds the four Springs at once. Read a Hubstone with the Loupe after the Restart.

pages.t: The Eye of the Hour leads to the lairs of the Order. Use it and it finds the nearest one — its needle points there, in your hand and in your inventory, and a line names the place, the side and the distance. In the overworld the Eye sees the Chapels of the Still and the Gauge Rings — the way into the Stillness lies through a ring; in the Stillness it sees the Bell Tower, the City of Midstep, the Clock Tower and the Founder's Hall, where the guardians and the masters wait. Sneak and use it to choose what it seeks: everything at once or one place. The Eye sees about a thousand blocks around, in the Stillness two thousand.

The Order's clockmakers carried the Eye so as not to lose one another in the stopped world: its needle does not run round the dial but looks to where the hour stands. It is made at the Flux Workbench from a clock, an opaline, two Still Grains and a speculum sheet — an unraveled Snarl and the Seine give the grains, so the Eye can be made long before the Stillness.

kp: The Eye of the Hour Око Часа
Око Часа Eye of the Hour Око Часа Eye of the Hour
nodes.hint: An eye of the Order that knows the way to its own. Study the Order of the Still Hour.

pages.t: Dissonance is the price of knowledge: it sends visions and shadows, and the Hush takes it away. Whoever has seen the Stillness in the records, broken a flowing Confluence or seen more than was meant to be seen finds their mind falling out of step. It comes in three kinds. Ripple fades by itself, drop by drop. Dissonance stays until Hush takes it away. Deep Dissonance stays forever: only the Stillness itself leaves it.

Dissonance presses. Every few minutes the mind tests itself, and the harder it presses, the likelier a vision: a clock ticking behind you, a standing fog, shadows that repeat your steps. Heavy Dissonance brings heavier visions. Things of stillmetal and things strained by three weavings press while you wear them.

Dissonance can be heard. A metronome in your hand ticks evenly while the mind is calm, wavers with Dissonance and stumbles in advance when a vision is near. On screen it stands as a small metronome: behind its glass, a scale filled with Dissonance by kind. Hover over it in your inventory to read the numbers.

nodes.hint: The price knowledge takes from the mind. It opens by itself the first time your mind falls out of step.

pages.t: A warning: past twenty-five measures of Dissonance the visions grow heavier — calm it with the Hush before it is too late. The further your mind falls out of step, the clearer it hears an even ticking beneath everything that flows. It is not the clock in your pocket. It is the Still Hour, the beat in which the Stillness froze. It does not threaten: it promises rest.
The Still hear that beat always and call it mercy. A fluxionist hears a warning in it: visions will grow heavier, shadows bolder. The Hush still helps. Do not wait until it no longer does.

kp: The Whisper of Stillness Шёпот покоя
nodes.hint: It opens once your Dissonance passes twenty-five.

pages.t: A warning: past fifty measures of Dissonance the world sometimes stops entirely — the Halt, an echo of the Great Stilling in a single mind. Drops hang, sound dies, only your heart can be heard. It passes. But each one leaves a place in memory where nothing flows, and the mind returns there on its own.

This is where the road of the Order begins: whoever stops arguing with the beat one day seeks the way into the Stillness on their own. Only the Stillness leaves Deep Dissonance, and only there can it be understood to the end.

kp: The Edge of the Beat Край такта
nodes.hint: It opens once your Dissonance passes fifty.

pages.t: The Hush lifts Dissonance and drives the visions off: stand in hushed water and keep still. Stillness heals Dissonance. The Still are partly right, and that is their temptation: where nothing flows, the mind stops falling out of step. A fluxionist takes from stillness exactly as much as is needed, and moves on.

Hush salt is brewed in the Crucible over gentle heat: quickdust with Still, Soul and Lattice. A pinch dropped into a source of still water — a pond or a well, never a river or flowing water — hushes nine sources of the same surface.

Step into hushed water and stay still. On the third breath the Hush comes: while it lasts, no visions come. Keep standing, and Ripple leaves every four breaths, Dissonance every eight. One step, and it all begins again.

kp: Соль тишины Hush Salt Соль тишины Hush Salt
nodes.hint: How to quiet a mind out of step. It opens once your Dissonance passes ten.

pages.t: A Hush Fork lifts Ripple and some Dissonance anywhere, with no hushed water — if you hear the ring out. Copper tines, an amethyst shard and Lattice at the Flux Workbench. Strike the fork and stand while it rings: when it fades, all Ripple leaves you and two measures of Dissonance, four under the Hush. One step cuts the ring short, and it is wasted. The fork dulls with every ring heard to the end.

kp: Камертон тишины Hush Fork Камертон тишины Hush Fork
nodes.hint: A ring that lifts Dissonance, if you hear it through to the end.

pages.t: A Hush Sachet gives the Hush on the road: two minutes without visions, wherever you stand. A knot of plum-dyed wool with a pinch of Hush Salt inside — wool, thread, dye and salt at the Flux Workbench. Wear it at your neck or hold it: with Dissonance on you, stand still for three breaths, and the sachet takes a pinch of salt from your inventory. The sachet does not lift Dissonance: for that, hushed water and the Fork.

kp: Саше тишины Hush Sachet Саше тишины Hush Sachet
nodes.hint: A pinch of Hush on a cord, for one who can stand still.

pages.t: A figment is a vision of Dissonance: usually harmless, but under heavy Dissonance it strikes, so know it by sight. It is a shadow invented by a mind out of step: it walks your own path over your last steps, at your own pace. Only the one whose Dissonance it is can see it; a companion beside you sees nothing. Hit one and it scatters into ink.

nodes.hint: Shadows that repeat your steps. Read a figment with the Loupe.

pages.t: Sentinels are dangerous shadows of heavy Dissonance and wardens of the Stillness: a blow takes a second from you, a cry leaves Ripple. The first Vowkeepers of the Order froze with the Great Stilling and have stepped once a second ever since, on the beat of their hour. From afar a Sentinel casts a Still Bolt that lurches on the beat of the hour: step out of its path while it hangs.

nodes.hint: Elders of the Order, frozen in the Great Stilling. Read a Sentinel with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Font keeps hushed water around itself on its own — a lasting place to lift Dissonance. The Reckoners' weirkeepers carved fonts from flowstone. Pour a bucket of water into the Font and drop in a pinch of Hush Salt: the salt melts, the water rises to the rim, the runes light up, and a few breaths later the Font brims over from its four spouts.

Hushed water settles on the eight spots around the Font, but only where it has nowhere to run: each spot needs a floor, and the ring needs a rim. Lay a low stone basin around the Font and it will always hold hushed water. One pinch, one brimming; the water in the Font stays. Scoop a spot out and the Font fills it again while salt is left. It holds up to four pinches.

nodes.hint: A basin that pours hushed water around itself.

pages.t: The Mute Bell is the master of the Bell Tower in the Stillness; defeating it gives its Bell Tongue and a Hubstone of three or four spokes. This bell tolled the Great Stilling and swallowed its own peal, and every sound around it with it. It hangs from the beam at the top of the Bell Tower; come close and it wakes. Its hall is as quiet as deep water: watch rather than listen, and jump the silent rings on the floor.

The Bell Tongue weaves into armor as Resonance: a loud blow — an explosion, a Warden's sonic boom or lightning — is swallowed whole, as the Bell swallowed its peal. Each woven piece swallows one blow, then rests 30 seconds. On the plinths: the Bell Tongue, a bell and an amethyst shard; Echo and Still in the vessels.

nodes.hint: In the Bell Tower of the Stillness hangs a bell that no one can hear. Read a Bellringer or the bell itself with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Prior heads the Order in the City of Midstep; defeating him gives the Prior's Seal and a Hubstone of three or four spokes. He kneels before the Still Gate with wax on his lips. Come up to the gate and the Order steps out of it in waves, and last of all, him. When he raises his hand bell, his people freeze into statues: strike him while he rings.

nodes.hint: The head of the Order prays beyond the Still Gate of the City of Midstep. Read the gate or a Vowkeeper with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Great Pendulum is the machine of the Stilling in the Clock Tower of the Halted Blaze; defeating it gives the Pendulum Bob, the key to the Founder's Hall, and a Hubstone of five spokes. The dead dial at the top wakes it: set in four Hour Marks — dawn, noon, dusk and midnight; no hour passes in the Stillness, so write them with the Loupe at home. The Pendulum sweeps the hall: take cover behind the columns in time with its swing.

nodes.hint: Whose swing holds the Stillness in a single hour? Read the dead dial at the top of the Clock Tower with the Loupe.

pages.t: Defeating the Unmoving gives the Heart of the Stilling, the key to the Restart, and a Hubstone of five spokes. The Founder's Hall lies under the glass of the Dead Calm; its gate opens to the Pendulum Bob set in the dead clock above it. Bring four Thaw Lanterns and shards of the four Springs: a lantern and a shard in a riverbed sluice, and the riverbed flows. He moves only while you move: freeze, and so does he.

kp: Сердце Остановки Heart of the Stilling
nodes.hint: Who stopped the world? He waits in the Founder's Hall under the glass of the Dead Calm — the Eye of the Hour finds the Hall. Read a riverbed sluice in the Hall or the dais itself with the Loupe.

pages.t: Mire is what murk threatens: it silts the ground, breeds creatures and clings to your feet. Keep murk below a third of the riverbed, and there will be no mire. Past that threshold the ground silts over, stone turns porous, mire creeps up the trunks, grasses turn into threads. Mire grows down and along the water sooner than up: it runs. Every silted block eats a little murk.

Mire has a heart — the Mire Hummock: it throbs, smothers the ground around it, raises sprouts and lashes. A Mire Vent breathes in four beats and exhales gnats, a ripe blister bursts with silt or with a leech, and thick ooze gathers into a Mire Clot. Silting heals mire creatures; the living it mires and wounds.

Mire lasts as long as the murk does. Bring the murk below a third of the riverbed and the ground falls back to mud, stone to Pitted Stone, blisters run off as ooze, and ooze dries into silt. A hummock without murk withers on its own. Murk is cleared by the Purifier, lumenash, Clearwort and the Murk Druse — or carried off in a flask. The place's current settles into the pores of Pitted Stone: a pickaxe without Silk Touch now and then knocks a shard out of it.

Some places need no workshop to grow murk. In a Stagnant Backwater the water has not moved for years and the murk settles on its own: the land holds a little over a third of its riverbed from birth. Mire lives there through no one's fault, the trees stand as dead husks, gnats swarm over the water and gas bubbles up from the bottom. A cleansed backwater silts up again within hours, and the mire does not spread past its edge: the neighbors have nothing to feed it.

nodes.hint: A blight that grows out of settled murk. Read silted soil or a mire creature with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Purifier turns murk back into flux: it cleans a workshop and saves the land from mire. It strains the murk of its patch of land through a lumenash filter — the Lumenash Grates above it: a cluster where each touches the next by a face, up to sixteen. The first takes the most, each next one a fifth less.

It runs on distillate of any current but Murk: set a vessel, an Alembic or a Gyre beside it or below, run a siphon to its side or pour a vial — it holds four parts, and one part lasts four turns. Silt clogs the grates; throw a clogged one into running water, and in a few seconds it rinses clean.
To clean a chunk: grates on top, fuel beside or by siphon. The Loupe on the Purifier says what it lacks. Next: "Clearwort".

kp: Очиститель Purifier Ясеневая решётка Lumenash Grate Очиститель Purifier
nodes.hint: A device that turns murk back into flux.

pages.t: A Murk Flask carries murk out of a workshop all at once — to wherever it shatters. Brewed from Murk and Tide, it draws murk the way a sponge draws water, and silts everyone standing near where it lands. The workshop is cleaner — the other place dirtier: murk does not vanish.

kp: Склянка мути Murk Flask Склянка мути Murk Flask
nodes.hint: A flask that carries murk away.

pages.t: Clearwort drinks murk with no distillate: plant it by a workshop, and it slowly cleans its patch of land. It grows on grass, dirt and even silted soil — mire does not take it. It drinks murk once in bloom, slower than the Purifier. The seeds are brewed in the Crucible from wheat seeds, Bloom and Gleam; a flowering plant drops them itself.

kp: Семена чистотела Clearwort Seeds Семена чистотела Clearwort Seeds
nodes.hint: A flower that drinks murk.

pages.t: Roiled beasts are the monsters of murky places: stronger and hardier than usual, but they drop Murky Geodes with loot. Where the murk passes a third of the riverbed, a monster born on its own may rise Roiled: twice as hardy, striking half again as hard, shedding flakes of murk. The murkier the place, the more of them — up to one in eight — and the richer the geode: plain, deep, black.

The murk stirs a sediment into each. Brisk — faster. Barbed — turns part of a blow back. Shelled — tougher. Mighty — hits harder. Withering — its blow withers. Filmed — a film shields it and grows back. Dissonant — its blow brings Ripple. Tenacious — heals before your eyes. Scorching — sets you alight.

Starving — its blow starves. Venomous — poisons. Draining — drinks health with each blow. Leechy — wounded, it lets out Mire Leeches. Mired — taken by the mire: its blow silts, and Silting heals it. The sediment shows above the head of the Roiled beast.

nodes.hint: Monsters the murk has stirred up. Fight a Roiled beast or read a Murky Geode.

names: an encounter with a Roiled Beast

pages.t: A Snarl is the bane of a rough workshop: it drinks murk and tightens, and left alone it tears open into a Breach down to the Stillness itself. Untangle it with a Pike Pole and it gives up what it caught, still grains, Snarl Thread and shards of the currents of its place — and a tightly twisted one, now and then, a rare Snarl Core. Where murk settles and the flux is drawn and drawn again, the current has nowhere to go: it twists like wet linen in a washerwoman's hands and tears along the fold. Through the tear you see the underside of the flux — a dark depth where threads of current drain away.

A Snarl drinks the murk of its patch of land and with each sip twists one turn tighter — and longer. It drags loose things toward the seam: dropped items, sand, gravel, leaves; everything snags in the fold and shows in it. Whoever touches the seam gets squeezed. Without murk a Snarl dries up and crumbles into silt.

A Snarl's tension rises on its own; a Weir nearby calms it. The Loupe shows tension and twists. A taut seam gapes wider, thrashes and burns crimson; it lets out Murky Glints and clouds the air around, and at the limit, left for more than a minute, it breaks through — down to the very bottom, where the Stillness lies. Do not wait.

A living Snarl gets in the way of work long before it breaks through. Within eight blocks of the seam devices falter: the Flux Workbench, the Crucible and the Conduit pay more flux — up to a quarter more, the tauter the tension, the more — and now and then misfire. The flux of this patch of land and its neighbors flickers, so thresholds like "no lower than three quarters of the riverbed" turn unreliable; whoever stands by the seam catches a Ripple. A taut one — 60 and up — drinks the flux of its patch of land into its twist: the workshop dries before any Breach opens. The Loupe writes this under the tension, and a Snarl untangled with a Pike Pole gives the flux it drank back.

nodes.hint: A tear in the current, hanging in the air. It rises where murk is above half the riverbed and flux is still being drawn: be near when one rises, or read it with the Loupe.

pages.t: A Pike Pole untangles a Snarl — only it: neither sword nor arrow takes one. A fluxsteel hook on a lumenash pole catches the kink and takes off a twist with each blow — a fresh Snarl comes apart in five. The seam lashes back, so keep clear of the lips. An untangled Snarl gives up what it caught and its spoils — the richer, the tighter it was twisted.

The tighter a Snarl was twisted, the richer its spoils. Still grains — by the murk it drank, more for tightness; Snarl Thread — one to four; shards of the currents of its place — the Springs and Poles that make up the currents of that land, one to three; and now and then a Snarl Core — three times in a hundred from a fresh one, up to a third from a tight, taut one. A Seine and a Snarl that unravels on its own leave only grains. A thread pays for a missing shard at the Lens Grinder and goes into the Silt Shell weaving; a Core dissolves in the Crucible into thick Bind with Still.

A rare Snarl Core — the kink of a tight Snarl, condensed into a solid — forged into the hook at the Confluence turns a Pike Pole into a Toothed Pike Pole: it takes off two and a half twists per blow. Besides a Maw Tooth, this is the only way to one.

kp: Багор Pike Pole Зубастый багор Toothed Pike Pole Багор Pike Pole
nodes.hint: A hooked pole that untangles a Snarl.

pages.t: A Seine quiets a Snarl on its own and gathers still grains from it — no fighting at the seam. It takes flux from its patch of land and combs the nearest Snarl within eight blocks: the lips press shut, the seam weakens, and the murk it drank settles in the net as grains. A Snarl combed to the end comes apart on its own. One untangled near a Seine gives no murk back to the ground. Next: "Still Rye".

nodes.hint: A net that combs the murk out of a Snarl.

pages.t: A Breach is a window into the Stillness right in the world: Grain Drifts and Stillmetal Veins grow at its lips, and closed on purpose — with living flux or a Thaw Lantern — it collapses into a Still Sky Shard. But it chills the flux and the living around it. A Snarl left alone twists the flux to the very bottom, and the bottom splits: the ground opens into a Breach. Look into the crack — its walls drop away into a chasm, and from below shines the sky of the still hour: a low amber sun, stars by day, dust that hangs and does not fall.

Still air rises from a Breach: everything living slows near it, and whoever falls into the crack freezes. The flux of your patch of land drains down and stills; rime creeps over the lips, grass turns into still turf, water into glass. At night a Laggard may climb out of the crack.

The Stillness brings up its own: after a minute a grain drift full of still grains gathers at the lips (it glimmers), then one every three minutes; stillmetal veins show in the walls. After half an hour a Breach seals over by itself and leaves only a scar of rimed stone. Close it sooner and the Still Sky collapses into a Still Sky Shard, leaving stillmetal and rimed stone at the lips. A Breach drinks the flux of its patch of land, so hold it at three quarters of the riverbed or more for half a minute — with a Wellspring, a skein, a Reservoir — or set a Thaw Lantern nearby: it thaws the Breach, and the drifts and veins give up freshet ore as well.

A Still Sky Shard goes into the Crown of the Wheel and into windows on the Stillness: it is the sky of the still hour itself in a piece of glass. From one shard and eight glass the Flux Workbench makes eight Stillsky Glass: a window that always shows the Stillness — a slate sky with stars by day, a low amber sun, clouds that do not drift and dust behind the glass. Panes side by side join into one window.

nodes.hint: A crack in the ground with the Stillness showing through. Be near when it opens, or read the Still Sky.

pages.t: The Sunken feed the mire: their creatures silt and drown, their shrines murk the land around, and their Procession comes to murky water by your workshop. They are a branch of the Reckoners' schism, once keepers of the weirs. They were the first to see stagnant flux settle into murk and wake as mire, and decided the mire is no blight but the bottom, where nothing is lost: they call it the Mother Below.

The Sodden walks the bottom and rises out of the water beside you; its blow silts you. Step back from the shore, and it has to climb the bank. The Keener sings a lament: whoever she can see loses air as if under water, and at zero drowns even on dry land. Get out of her sight behind stone, or break her song with a heavy blow.

The Mirebearer carries a living hummock on his back. His blow to the ground sends out threads that bind your legs. Let him reach murky water, and he presses the hummock into the bottom: mire will grow there.

Mire Shrines stand by swamps and quiet rivers: a ring of thread-wrapped stakes and a driftwood Mire Idol. The idol feeds murk to its patch of land and the ones around it until it is broken. And at night after rain, a Sunken Procession may come out toward murky water near you. Clear the water before they arrive, and it turns back: murk is the invitation. Next: "Sunken Laments".

nodes.hint: The mire has those who feed it. Read a Sodden or a Keener with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Laments lead to the Sunken Sanctum, where the Mire Maw sleeps; its tooth on a Pike Pole untangles a Snarl in two blows. A Sunken Lament is a scroll in soaked wax, a song rather than a rule. "All things settle," the Sunken sing: every flux will one day sink to the bottom and become mire, and the mire remembers all that sank into it.

The laments name where the threads of every Mire Idol lead: to the Sunken Sanctum. Read an idol with the Loupe — the strands of murk point the way to the sanctum and tell how far it is. The sanctum is a half-drowned temple on stilts around a lake of ooze, and its locks open only to what is hidden inside.

In the sanctum lake sleeps the Mire Maw, the mouth of the Mother Below. It never leaves its place, but it drags you in on a current of ooze, and while Keeners sing on the stilts it drags twice as hard: take them down first. In its second phase the floor silts over in rings — stand on stilts and stones.
A Maw Tooth set on a Pike Pole untangles a Snarl in two blows.

kp: Зубастый багор Toothed Pike Pole Зуб Пасти Maw Tooth
nodes.hint: Their teaching is written in soaked wax. Find a Sunken Lament: Keeners carry them, and Mire Shrines keep them.

pages.t: The Lees is the world at the bottom of the murk: niello, a pure store of Murk, Lees Shells with pearls and the life of the bottom are there. The way in is a Whirlpool from a Sounding Lead in murky water. Stagnant flux does not vanish: it settles — through the flux, like silt through water, all the way down: layer upon layer, all the murk the fluxionists have spilled since the Great Stilling lies there, and the living mire on it is ground, not blight.

The door to the Lees is murky water itself. Throw a Sounding Lead into water at least three blocks deep, with a surface of at least 3 × 3, where the murk of the chunk is at least half the riverbed: the lead sinks, the cord runs down knot by knot, and the water turns into a Whirlpool. Step into it — it spins you and pulls you down. The Whirlpool drinks the murk of its chunk; cleanse the chunk, and it fades and the lead floats up. By a Mire Shrine the water need not be murky: a Whirlpool rises in clean water too and never fades.

On the bottom a Rising Column will meet you — a column of pale bubbles. Stand in it, and it carries you up to the surface of your Whirlpool, even if it has faded. Down there you cannot sleep or set a spawn point. The depth holds you softly: you jump higher and fall slower. Above the Ooze Basins the air thins, as under water.

Flux on the bottom is only what you make: the riverbed there is the smallest in the world, and the murk flows from chunk to chunk the way flux does above. Bring a Purifier with grates, a lumenash sapling, fire — mire creatures fear it twice as much — and Clearwort seeds. The skeins of the Lees are murky; in the Bright Shallows they are bright.

kp: Донный лот Sounding Lead Донный лот Sounding Lead
nodes.hint: The underside of the flux shows through the seam of a Snarl. Read a Snarl with the Loupe.

pages.t: A clean camp is a place where you can live and work on the bottom: the mire recedes there and Glowbloom grows. Every chunk of the Lees holds its own bed murk — one and a half riverbeds — and pulls back toward it: a cleansed chunk fills again, from its neighbors and from the bed. A single Purifier in the middle of the mire will not cope. A camp of 3 × 3 chunks is held together: three or four Purifiers with grates, and lumenash trees.

Where the murk drops below a third of the riverbed, the mire recedes into silt and stone, and Glowbloom breaks through the revived silt — the glowing grass of the bottom, the sign of a camp. Murk Fry do not swim into a clean camp. Bubblebacks graze on Mire Threads and breathe out bubbles — you can take a breath in them. In the Bright Shallows there is no bed murk at all: the bottom took that grove in clean.

nodes.hint: On the bottom it is clean only where someone keeps it clean. Read a Glowbloom or the Bright Shallows.

pages.t: Niello is a pure store of Murk: a Murk Flask is brewed and a Murk Fumer fed with it without muddying the workshop, and a Niello Inlay catches the Conduit's murk. It is murk pressed by the depth into black stone with a violet sheen. Its veins lie in the Layerstone of the Lees, larger deeper down; it needs an iron pickaxe. In the Crucible a piece of niello is eight shares of Murk, with no grime and no other currents.

A Niello Inlay is niello in a speculum setting for the Conduit: hold the Conduit in the other hand and use the inlay. The murk of a dry lens, a weak cast, a rough draw and a cheap blank goes into the inlay, not into the chunk — up to sixteen. Rinse a full one in running water, like a Purifier grate: drop the Conduit into a stream for five seconds.

kp: Чернёная накладка Niello Inlay Чернь Niello
nodes.hint: The depth presses murk black. Read Niello Ore.

pages.t: A Lees Shell grows a pearl out of murk, and with a ripe pearl it is the best calm stone for a Confluence altar. It lies on bare silt — only in the Lees, and only where the murk is at least a third of the riverbed: each stage of the pearl eats half a share of the chunk's murk. A ripe pearl glows between the valves.

Take the shell with silk touch, and the pearl stays in it; otherwise it crumbles. A shell with a ripe pearl by a Confluence altar is a calm stone: the bottom is the quietest water. It holds the reserve more firmly than a Weirkeeper Figurine (+8 instead of +5) and takes its place among the four nearest stones.

nodes.hint: What grows on the bottom out of murk? Read a Lees Shell.

pages.t: The life of the bottom tells you where it is clean and where it is dangerous: Murk Fry leave a clean camp, the Bubbleback gives air, the Silt Ray silts. The fry swim in shoals through the depth as if through water: they glow with murk, gather where there is more of it and scatter from light. A Silt Ray lies in the Bedsilt with only its eyes showing; whoever steps close, it leaps at in an arc, and its barb silts.

The Bubbleback is big and peaceful: it grazes on the mire, eating Mire Threads, and breathes out bubbles — whoever stands in them can breathe even above the basins. It follows Clearwort held in hand. The Sunken hunt Bubblebacks.

A Ray Barb can be woven into a weapon by Confluence: two barbs and Silt on the plinths, Murk and Bane in the vessels. Sting — a hit brings Silting, and a hit on one already silted deepens it. Mire creatures are untouched by the Sting: silting heals them.

The Silt Delver, a big crayfish of the bottom, plows the Bedsilt with its claws and every few minutes turns up a find: a concentrate, a bone, an Antimony Flake, a Lees Shell, now and then Niello or a Flux Pebble; on the Still Bed, Still Grains. It never digs the same spot twice — follow it, and the finds are yours. It never attacks first, but touch it, and it pinches.

kp: Life of the Lees Жители дна
nodes.hint: Not only the Sunken live on the bottom. Read a Silt Ray, a Bubbleback, Murk Fry or a Silt Delver.

pages.t: The Great Dam is the lair of the Elder Weirkeeper: beating him opens the strongroom under the crest with a Hubstone, and he drops the Weirkeeper's Anchor, which a Confluence turns into a Mire Anchor. The dam closes a channel of ooze from shore to shore; the guardian sleeps on the crest, and inside the dam lie galleries, water chambers with sluices and hidden rooms. Piles hold, the ooze does not: keep high and breathe at the bubbles.

The sluice chambers open with water: each pit has two wheels — one lets some spans in, the other lets them out; the gate rises when the water stands at the lit mark. The lectern of the chamber names the wheels' measures. The dry bed under the dam lies in the thin air of the basin, but under a vault the air holds: breathe in the alcoves under the body of the dam. The weirkeepers built dams to measure and hold water; the first of them chose to hold the murk itself — and guards the wall to this day.

kp: Кладка из слоистого камня Layerstone Bricks
nodes.hint: A weirkeepers' dam closes a channel of ooze. Read a groove of its crest with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Mire Anchor is a weapon of control: cast on its chain, it strikes the first foe it meets, pulls it to you and holds it slowed — it drags an archer off a wall and plucks one out of a crowd. Guardians and lords do not budge. It is heavy: while the anchor is in your main hand, water and ooze drag you to the bottom — put it away to swim up.
It is drawn by a Confluence from the Weirkeeper's Anchor, the Elder Weirkeeper's trophy: niello, iron chains, a Ray Barb and leather around it, with the currents of Murk, Bind and Tide.

kp: Тинный якорь Mire Anchor Тинный якорь Mire Anchor
nodes.hint: The dam guardian's anchor held the wall for an age. Read the Weirkeeper's Anchor with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Quickstream is the main channel of the flux: by its races the riverbed is twice that of a river, the current of the place is any of the forty-two, quickwater fills the sea under the islands, and the way between two arches through it is four times shorter. Under the flux of the world runs the main stream: all forty-two currents flow side by side in it as races — rivers of living flux in the air — and the riverbed of every chunk is one of its branches. The Reckoners measured it with great locks; the Tollkeepers dammed it with barrages and drink it.

The way in is the same Sluice Arch that leads to the Stillness: a 4 × 5 frame of Reckoner stone and a pinch of Quickdust. But the lock takes its toll in flux: it wakes toward the Quickstream only where the flux of the chunk is at least 1.4 riverbeds — and drinks it down to the bottom. What the flux of the chunk lacks the lock takes from the Toll Reliquaries in your inventory: with them the arch wakes in a plain chunk too. With three Still Grains in your inventory the arch leads to the Stillness: the toll decides the level — stillness leads to stillness, living flux to living flux.

The islands of the Quickstream hang over a sea of quickwater, and the races carry whatever enters them: step in and the stream carries you, crouch and you go slowly, step aside to leave. The islands are high: take a Grapnel or a Vane Mantle. You can live here — beds and spawn points work — and the days are half as long. The arch on the far side leads back; a new arch woken in the Quickstream leads out four times farther from where it stands.

nodes.hint: Someone drinks the flux by the Gauge Stones — where does it go? Go down to the Lees, then read a Master Gauge Stone and a Toll Tap.

pages.t: A race carries you and gives its current to the place. Step in and it carries you along, faster than running; jump into it even from an island — it catches you and holds you. Crouch and you go slowly; the movement keys steer across the flow — that is how you step out sideways, and jumping lifts you toward the edge. Inside you cannot fall: weight fades away. Races carry items, creatures and arrows too. By a race its current is the current of the place: by a race of Ember the Flux Workbench sees Ember, and Current Seeds grow by a race of their own current — any of the forty-two.

Neighbors on the Wheel merge: races of Tide and Gale flow on below their confluence as one race of Drift. Opposites never merge: where Tide and Ember, Strata and Gale, Lattice and Fray would meet, there is a clash — rough water that throws everything out and gives birth to Clashers. Races rise from the sea of quickwater and fall back into it; the riverbed by a race is 200, between races 30, deep inside the islands 16. Murk cannot settle here: the stream carries it away.

Where races meet there is nothing to choose: at a confluence the tributaries flow into the main race — their threads braid and swirl into an eddy, and you cannot go up a tributary, the stream brings you back to the confluence. You choose at a fork: halfway along, a main race lets out an arm, and both ends flow away from the fork. As you come up to the fork, press the movement key toward the arm — a short press is enough — and the arm catches you; press nothing or the other way and the main race carries you on. At a fork the sideways keys only choose: they never throw you out of the race there. The arm, like the main race, falls into the sea.

nodes.hint: Rivers of living flux run through the air between the islands. Read a race with the Loupe — or a racefish swimming up it.

pages.t: Fell into the sea under the islands? Quickwater brings you back up by itself: it carries a swimmer to the mouth of the nearest race rising from the sea — at the mouth the water wells up and hands you to the race, and the race lifts you to the islands: step off it sideways. No mouth nearby — an upwelling column rises by the nearest island and sets the swimmer on its top. Items you dropped are carried onto an island by the same column. Crouch to dive — then the water does not carry you.

Quickwater carries flux with you: a bucket poured outside the Quickstream gives the chunk a quarter of its riverbed — but not above one and a half riverbeds — and lies as plain water. This is how the flux of a chunk is raised under a Sluice Arch or in a dry workshop. It is scooped with a bucket from the sea under the islands of the Quickstream; standing in it slowly heals. It does not multiply: two pools make no new source.

A Crucible filled with quickwater while empty boils over without murk: the living flux carries the surplus away. Scoop it — it is quickwater again; add plain water — it becomes plain. In the Stillness a poured bucket thaws a circle of three blocks for a minute — a short thaw on the move; it gives no flux there: the Stillness has no riverbed.

kp: Ведро живой воды Bucket of Quickwater
nodes.hint: The sea under the islands of the Quickstream is flux in liquid form. Read quickwater.

pages.t: Break the barrage — and the race flows again, and the Drained Isles around turn green, for everyone and for good. The barrage is a Tollkeeper fortress across the main race of the Drained Isles: an old Reckoner lock on a captured island, a copper shield in the gap, cisterns of reliquaries on the quays. Below the gate the race stands gray and carries no one — that is how a barrage is found: follow the gray race upstream, and it ends at the gate.

On the hub of the Toll Wheel above the gate sleeps the Tollfarmer, head of the Tollkeepers; the ramp of the east tower leads up. Do not pay him in his own current: under the seal of ransom a blow or cast of that current heals him, and the opposite Spring tears the ransom at once. The paddles of the wheel sweep the hub — jump over them. Under the hub lies a cast counting chamber: it opens when the Tollfarmer falls, and the Tollfarmer's Reliquary drops from his back — a Confluence draws a Belt Reliquary from it.

nodes.hint: The Tollkeepers dammed a race of the Drained Isles. Follow a gray, stopped race upstream — it ends at the barrage; read any stone of it with the Loupe.

pages.t: In the vault of the Great Lock the Reckoners left a Hubstone and all five Reckoner Records — they are yours if you pass both puzzles of the lock. The lock stands on the main race of the Channel Reaches: the race runs straight and level through a stone chamber between two walls. Step into the race upstream — it carries you into the chamber — and step aside onto a quay.

In the west wall lies a vane hall: a thread of the race bursts from an intake. A vane along the thread lets it pass, a vane across stops it, a vane aslant turns it aside. Turn the vanes with an empty hand until the thread reaches the gauge mark — then the seals of the door in the east wall crumble. Behind the door is the lock chamber: raise the water with the valves to the lit mark of the pit, and the gate of the vault in the lower head rises.

Lock Tenders, Reckoner automatons, set back every vane and valve you touched until the puzzle is solved: be quick, lead them away or break them. A solved puzzle they leave alone. A pickaxe takes the masonry of the walls, but the vault is cast on every side — only the gate leads in.

nodes.hint: The Reckoners measured the main race with locks. Find the chamber the race runs through straight and level, and read any stone of the Great Lock with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Belt Reliquary carries flux to where there is none. Wear it on your belt: in a chunk at three quarters of its riverbed or more it takes flux from the ground by itself — one unit every two seconds, up to 64. Where the chunk is dry, the Conduit and the Flux Workbench take what they lack from the reliquary — a full cast, no murk, as from a skein. In a rich chunk it is left alone: it is a store for dry places. In the Stillness the reliquary stills — there only the Still Conduit works.

It is drawn by a Confluence from the Tollfarmer's Reliquary, the trophy of the Toll Barrage guardian: a Buckled Belt, two Toll Reliquaries, a Toll Charter, Fluxsteel Wire and leather around it, with the currents of Drift, Want and Alloy. There is one belt slot: the reliquary is a choice against the other belts. A Charging Basin and a Flux Locket fill it too.

kp: Поясной ковчег Belt Reliquary Поясной ковчег Belt Reliquary
nodes.hint: The Tollfarmer's Great Reliquary held what a whole barrage drank. Read the Tollfarmer's Reliquary with the Loupe.

pages.t: The Still Brink is the lower reach of the Quickstream, where the flow stops: the races here are slow and glassy, and their ends fall into the haze as frozen falls. Here the Stillness is closest — bent grass, Still Grains in drifts — but the way into the Stillness itself does not start here: it goes through the Gauge Ring.

nodes.hint: Somewhere the Quickstream slows and stops. Read the Still Brink with the Loupe.

pages.t: Under the Gauge Stones the flux of the world does not run straight — it goes round in loops. The Reckoners built the Counting Ways there to set every current against every other, and in the heart of each loop they seated an Auditor to sum it up. The sum did not reconcile — and the order split. The loops still stand: in each, a Keywarden by the Descent Gate, an Auditor in the Heart, a Hubstone for his share, Reckoner coffers and a dark stone found nowhere else.

The way in is the Wayfinder Cord: hold it on the head of a living Gauge Stone for three seconds — the cord winds round the stone and you go down into the loop of this land. All the stones of one land lead to one loop. Each descent costs a knot of the cord; mend it with Knotted Cord.

While the cord is in your hand, a golden thread runs along the floor — the way back to the Tether Hall where you came down. The way out is at the Tether: press it and stay close. An emergency pull: crouch and hold the cord for six seconds without moving — two knots. No one sleeps in the Meanders: the walls go on moving while you dream.

kp: Путеводный шнур Wayfinder Cord Путеводный шнур Wayfinder Cord
nodes.hint: Where the flux of the world goes round in loops, the Reckoners built a maze. Read Knotted Cord and a Gauge Stone.

pages.t: Every two and a half minutes the loop recounts: in some doorways a shoal grows from the groove in the floor — amber and lilac of stilled flux — and in others it melts away. Ten seconds before, the Counting Bell tolls, and the doorways about to close shimmer amber while the shoals about to melt shed lilac grit.

In either phase of the Recount there is a way back to the Tether Hall from every cell of the loop: the passages change, but the maze never locks you in. The thread of the cord follows the present way. A shoal will not rise on someone standing in the doorway. Where the Auditor falls, the Recount stops for good.

nodes.hint: The passages of a loop grow shut with stilled flux and open again. Read a shoal.

pages.t: A Summing Plaque holds the seals of the way into the Heart of the loop and of the Summing Niches. Its sum burns in it — a compound current; Tally Dials sit on the wall beside it. Turn each dial with an empty hand to the rune of a Spring or a Pole, press the plaque — and if the dials together are what the sum is made of on the Wheel, the seals crumble.

The sum is what it is made of, not what it looks like: keep the Wheel open. If the dials add up to another current — "the sum does not reconcile": the plaque strikes with that current and stays dark for three seconds. If they add up to nothing — only a puff of murk.

nodes.hint: A brass plaque with the rune of a current and tally dials below it. Read a Summing Plaque.

pages.t: The Descent Gate locks the wing of the loop that holds the Descent into the Heart: seals and a socket for a Knot Key. The key lies in the pit of the Keyhall — a round hall with door niches — under the seals of its keeper. The Keywarden is a Reckoner automaton, the warden of the ways; the creed of the loop rewound him its own way. Any Knot Key opens any Gate.

Watch the keyholes of the niches: he steps into one and out of another with a blow — the one that lit and clicked is the way out. In the second half of the fight he locks you in a pen of shoals: find the weak bead — two blows, and the pen falls. The Keywarden's Ward, his trophy, makes a Keyed Cord out of a Wayfinder Cord — twice as fast.

kp: Ключевой шнур Keyed Cord Узловой ключ Knot Key
nodes.hint: The way down to the Heart of the loop is locked. Read the Keywarden — or a Knot Key.

pages.t: The Auditor summed the loops into the Sum — the count of the whole world. Three masks ring his dome: the Order's, the Tollkeepers' and the Sunken's — the three sums he was rewound to. The walls of his Replanning rise along the lines of the floor: watch where the lights run and walk the dark squares — there is always a way to him.

In the second half of the fight the mask of the loop's creed turns forward and he fights with its weapon: the Order's Halt Stones (break a stone), the Tollkeepers' Deduction (casts nearby go into the book and come back as a volley — strike with the opposite Spring), the Sunken's Silt (get off the mire). A fallen Auditor gives a Hubstone with two spokes to everyone who fought and an Audit Seal; the Vault of the loop opens and the Recount stops.

nodes.hint: In the Summing Hall of the Heart a great automaton sits over the book of the Sum. Read the Auditor — or an Audit Seal.

pages.t: The Auditors summed the Sum three times, and three times it came out different. One sum said every current must be stopped — and the Order of the Still Hour was born. Another said every current must be tolled — and the Tollkeepers went their way. The third said every current must be let down to the bottom — and the Sunken went down. Each branch took loops for itself and rewound their Auditors to its sum.

No branch took the Reckoned loops: their Auditors sum all three in turn and settle on none. The Reckoners who stayed write that the Sum did not reconcile not because the count was wrong — the Wheel does not sum to a single current.

nodes.hint: Why the Reckoners split into three branches. Read a Summary Record.

pages.t: The pillars trade murk and flux in their hour: the Dawn Pillar cleans murk into flux, the Dusk Pillar grows murk for murkcaps, murk druses and the Roiled. The Dawn Pillar works from dawn to noon: every half minute it turns a pinch of its land's murk into flux. Now and then it slips and gives a pinch of murk back.

The Dusk Pillar works from sunset to midnight: it turns a pinch of flux into murk. It grows murk druses and murkcaps and calls the Roiled — and it is dangerous: mire starts where murk rises above a third of the bed. Next: "The Murk Fumer".

kp: Dawn and Dusk Pillars Столбы зари и сумерек
Рассветный столб Dawn Pillar Сумеречный столб Dusk Pillar Рассветный столб Dawn Pillar
nodes.hint: Murk and flux can trade places — in their hour. Read a snarl.

pages.t: A Murk Fumer turns things to mire with smoke: mushrooms become murkcaps, a pumpkin a mirekin, logs Mirebound Logs. A siphon pours Murk distillate into it from above, and the horn breathes heavy smoke ahead. The smoke does not spread but flows down and creeps along the floor: murk settles. Settled smoke is murk in the land.

In the smoke mushrooms become murkcaps, a pumpkin a mirekin, a jack o'lantern a mire-o'-lantern, logs mirebound logs; the living in it are clouded. A mirebound log gives mirebound planks: they do not spread mire, but a murkcap takes root on them.

kp: Окуриватель Murk Fumer Затянутые доски Mirebound Planks Тинный светец Mire-o'-Lantern Окуриватель Murk Fumer
nodes.hint: Murk can be breathed out as smoke. Read a murkcap.

pages.t: A Still Anvil mends without the cost growing: an item does not remember the mending, and the anvil itself never cracks — not from work, not from a fall. It is made of three blocks of stillmetal and four ingots at the Flux Workbench.

kp: Стылая наковальня Still Anvil Стылая наковальня Still Anvil
nodes.hint: A metal that does not change does not change the thing either. Study stillmetal.

pages.t: A Still Cast carries a creature: frozen into a figurine in the hoop, it thaws wherever you set the cast. A hoop of still ingots and nuggets around a still grain. Put it to a creature and it stills with all it carries; set the cast on a block and the creature thaws as it was.
People, hosts and villagers the hoop does not take, nor someone else's pet; take the rider off first. What is stopped does not age and does not wait: it simply stands.

kp: Стылый слепок Still Cast Стылый слепок Still Cast
nodes.hint: Stillmetal stops the living too. Study stillmetal.

pages.t: Still rye grows still grains and ergot in a garden bed — no trip to the Stillness. Wheat seeds, four still grains on the plinths, Still and Root — and the Confluence gives a seed of still rye. Sow it on farmland like wheat, but the rye grows only in calm: while nothing moves within eight blocks — not you, not a beast, not a fish. It does not take bone meal.
A ripe ear gives seeds, still grains and, rarely, still ergot — a black horn. Whoever eats the ergot sees the still hour: they remember the Stillness, but Ripple knocks the mind off its beat.

kp: Семена стылой ржи Still Rye Seeds Семена стылой ржи Still Rye Seeds
nodes.hint: A grain of the Stillness sprouts if all around stands still. Read a still grain.

pages.t: A whole Hubstone is not broken into spokes but bound in a brass wheel on an ash haft. Out comes a mattock: a pickaxe, a shovel and an axe at once, tougher and faster than netherite. Whichever spoke looks forward, that current does the digging; pick a spoke on the lens wheel — hold … — or sneak and use it to turn the wheel to the next spoke.

Tide — Panning: ore gives one more raw piece, but not with Fortune. Strata — Sweep: 3×3 across the face. Fray — Vein: the whole vein of ore at once. Ember — Smelting: what you mine comes out smelted. Gale — Passage: a man-high tunnel five blocks deep in one blow. Lattice — Whole: blocks drop as with Silk Touch.

The mattock pays for Panning, Smelting, Passage and Vein with the flux of the chunk; when the flux falls below a quarter of the bed they fall silent, and the mattock digs like a plain one. Sneaking, it takes a single block. It carries Dissonance while in hand, and in your inventory, in a full chunk, it slowly mends with the flux of the place.

kp: Кайло Колеса Wheel Mattock Кайло Колеса Wheel Mattock
nodes.hint: A Hubstone that digs with all six spokes. Read a Hubstone.

pages.t: Flux cloth sewn through with still-thread holds flux reluctantly, and whoever wears it spends less: the whole vestments take up to half the price off crafting and casting. Diviner's Spectacles lenses are set into the brim of the hood.

Rime Shroud: in the full vestments crouch twice, and for four seconds a shroud of stopped time five blocks wide stands around you. Arrows, fireballs and everything thrown that flies into it freeze in the air and drop when it lifts; foes under the shroud slow. It rests 45 seconds. The Crown of the Wheel counts as the hood.

The thread remembers the Great Stilling: the vestments press with Dissonance while worn. In a murky chunk, with murk above a third of its bed, the still-thread holds no flux and the thrift is gone. The robe gives little protection.

kp: Стылый капюшон Stillweave Hood Стылая ряса Stillweave Robe Стылые шаровары Stillweave Leggings Стылая ряса Stillweave Robe
nodes.hint: A robe flux passes through reluctantly. Study Stillmetal and Dam Plate.

pages.t: Order gear gives the Order's skills: the Bellringer's hearing and toll, the Vowkeeper's vow, the midstep of the Boots. It is not made but found in the Bell Towers, the Chapels of the Still and the City of Midstep. The Bellringer's habit: bells and steps nearby show as ripples. Vowkeeper plate: stand still and the vow of rest is taken, blows from the front come weaker; the full plate cannot be moved, and your blow under the vow strikes like a mace. The step in it is heavy. In Order Boots your steps make no sound, and crouching you are hard to see.

The skills — crouch twice. In the full habit — the Mute Toll: a ring of rime rolls ten blocks, and every foe it reaches slows and shines through walls; it is seen, not heard. In Order Boots while moving — Midstep: five blocks through a stopped instant, blows miss you, and pursuers who lose you fall behind; at the edge of a drop the step stops.

The Prior's Seal remakes Vowkeeper plate into his vestments, piece by piece, in a Confluence: allies nearby hold firmer, and an ally who takes a killing blow keeps one health — once a minute. Foes falling nearby give the reliquary taken time; crouch twice and it heals you and your allies. A stillmetal sword with the Seal is the Prior's Blade: its blow slows and starves. The vestments, the blade and the habit all press with Dissonance.

kp: Кираса Настоятеля Prior's Cuirass Клинок Настоятеля Prior's Blade Печать Настоятеля Prior's Seal
nodes.hint: What held the Order together. Study the Prior; read a Bellringer's habit, Vowkeeper plate or Order Boots with the Loupe.

pages.t: A Stillmetal Vein broken inside the circle of a Thaw Lantern gives not grains but Freshet Ore: stillmetal that began to flow again. Outside a thawed circle and with no flux nearby the ore stills back within a day. It is smelted in a Crucible at a strong boil with Drift and Tempo: one piece of ore, one freshet ingot.

Freshet steel flows: what moves is made of it — the flight of the Freshet garb, the wave of the Freshet Scythe, the overflow of bands. The Flux Workbench rolls three ingots into three sheets; nine ingots pack into a block.

kp: Слиток вешней стали Freshet Ingot Лист вешней стали Freshet Sheet Блок вешней стали Block of Freshet Steel Слиток вешней стали Freshet Ingot
nodes.hint: Stillmetal that flows again. Study Stillmetal and wootz; read Freshet Ore with the Loupe (a vein gives it inside a Thaw Lantern's circle).

pages.t: Studying this entry opens the Freshet Garb's flight in the Stillness — for you alone. Before the Restart the mantle is cold here for everyone; after it, it carries only those who have reached the beating sluice themselves: read the Restart Sluice by the founder's dais — the one where the Restart happened — with the Loupe, and study this entry. The sluices of thaw patches do not give this knowledge.

While the Stillness stood, freshet steel remembered how to stand and went cold in it. The Restart moved the hour: the beating sluice drives a faint current through the halls, and the mantle that hears it remembers that water runs here too.

kp: Flight in the Stillness Полёт в Застылье
nodes.hint: The Freshet Mantle will carry you in the Stillness too. After the Restart, read the Restart Sluice where the Restart happened with the Loupe.

names: the Restart Sluice beating under the Loupe

pages.t: A Deep Mirror takes you through a Through-Mirror: you step into one and out of its pair. Home and mine, workshop and altar become a single step — within one world. Right-click a mirror that has a pair and stay close for a second and a half while the glass opens; step away and it closes.

A full mirror holds three steps (a step is 16 charge of 48); fill it at a Charging Basin. A step leaves a Ripple: the mind does not like being in two places at once. Under the Hush there is no Ripple. The mirror does not lead between worlds, nor through the frozen glass of the Stillness until the land thaws. Someone else's mirrors let you through only if their owner opened them to guests. Sneak and right-click a mirror with it, and it will send things into that one, like a Pocket Mirror.

In the Stillness mirrors stand like water — smooth and empty. The Still believed a mirror is a moment stopped: you look, and time does not pass. The Deep Mirror argues with them: in its glass the flux runs even where feet cannot go.

kp: Глубинное зеркальце Deep Mirror Глубинное зеркальце Deep Mirror
nodes.hint: Step into a mirror and out of its pair. It needs a mind that has fallen out of step before.

pages.t: A Murk Druse cleans a workshop where a Purifier cannot reach: plant the seed on any solid face in a murky chunk, and as it grows it drinks nine murk out of it. You want it when the mire creeps in and there is no flux for a Purifier — and when you need Murk: a ripe druse dissolves in the Crucible.

The seed is brewed in the Crucible: Silt as the catalyst, Murk and Bloom in the brew. It grows in three steps, and each drinks three murk; with less murk in the chunk it waits. In a clean chunk, and in the Stillness where nothing flows, it does not grow. Now and then a Mire Hummock drops a seed.

Take a druse with a Pike Pole and the murk stays locked inside; a ripe one gives two druses — one to plant again, one to dissolve. Broken any other way — by hand, with a pickaxe, by an explosion, a piston, losing its support — it bursts, and all it drank returns to the chunk as murk; you get just the seed.

Murk is stagnant flux. A druse gives it a shape: inky columns grow like drops, with lilac smoldering inside. Fluxionists call it an honest sink — it does not destroy murk, it holds it until someone drops it.

kp: Друза мути Murk Druse Друза мути Murk Druse
nodes.hint: A crystal that drinks a chunk's murk. Discover Murk.

pages.t: This is a key to the finale: the Stillness holds on a beat that never was. The founder's heart stopped first, and its beat did not happen but went into the ground — the Sanguine Weald drinks it. While there is no beat, there is no hour: the Stillness stands. The heart that stopped the world can be started again — and then the beat will happen.

The Order tried to stop the beat in the weald too: a ring of sanguine slate pillars, chains to a monolith, and in the monolith a heart of still stone where the beat stands. The beat did not stop. The stillness leaked instead, and the aspens around the ring turned gray and glassy. The vein in this heart glows and never beats — the only motionless light in the weald.

The Hourless Wood gives Still without the Stillness. When it rains, the rain does not fall here but hangs in beads: an empty bottle raised under the open sky takes a Halted Drop (Still 2, Tide 1) — for the Crucible and for the flame of the Lull Lamp, whose light never flickers. Lullstone and the glass leaves of halted birches make a slate-blue house with amber light. Halted caravans stand on the old roads: their chests hold goods, Frozen Thoughts, the Order's writings and, rarely, Still Grains.

Where to look: in place of a snowy taiga — a grove of white birches with glass leaves, all leaning the same way: each world its own way, along the frozen gust. There is no snow here and no music, only the glass chiming now and then. Glassfinches caught in mid-flight hang among the birches: come close and one thaws for a heartbeat, darts off and stops again. The light here is wrong: Laggards walk by day too, and morning does not crumble them.

When the Stillness tore away from the world, the stilling burned through the groves along its edge, and they stand in a single instant still: a gust froze in the grass, dandelion seeds hang around their heads, those who walked with the caravan stopped by the road. The Stillness is closer than it seems: dust and drops hang there just the same.

kp: Затишная лампада Lull Lamp Застывшая капля Halted Drop
nodes.hint: A grove caught by the Great Stilling: rain hangs in the air, the birches all lean one way. Read it with the Loupe.

pages.t: Racestriders are the herd beasts of the floating isles and food for whoever lives in the Quickstream: mutton, leather and, from one you slay, a pinch of Gale or Tide Grit. The races are their roads: a frightened Racestrider runs to the edge of its isle, leaps into the nearest race, and the race carries it off to another isle; if it misses, it glides down. A running person scares them — come at a walk.

On the Drained Isles, where the Tollkeepers dammed the races, Dustfins swim in the gray dust — fish of the dried courses. Only a fin shows above the ground: whatever circles you is about to strike from below, and its bite leaves you hungry. They cannot swim in stone, tuff or planks — stand on stone, and a Dustfin only circles at the edge. Slain, it gives the land back the flux it held, and sometimes drops a Strata Shard.

kp: Life of the Isles Жители островов
Яйцо призыва: стрежник Racestrider Spawn Egg
nodes.hint: Herds roam the isles of the Quickstream, and something swims in the dust of the Drained Isles. Read a Racestrider or a Dustfin with the Loupe.

pages.t: Guard your Thaw Lantern from Rime Moths. These moths of hoarfrost hang in the air of the Stillness, frozen in flight, and the warmth of a lit lantern wakes them from twenty-four steps away: a moth settles on the lantern and drinks its store — three moths drink a shard's minute in ten seconds, and the circle freezes. One that has drunk glows warm inside. It is fragile: strike it down near the lantern, and the warmth goes back into it. It sometimes drops a Still Grain.

The Salamander, the fire lizard of the alchemists, is the lantern's friend. In the Halted Blaze it stilled together with the fire; in a lantern's circle it thaws, lies down beside it and breathes into it — the lantern burns longer — and it snaps up Rime Moths. Having given a minute of warmth, it rests for ten minutes. Outside the circle it stills again; in the Thawed it lives free.

kp: Rime Moths and Salamanders Инеевки и саламандры
Яйцо призыва: саламандра Salamander Spawn Egg
nodes.hint: Not everything in the Stillness is dead: Rime Moths and Salamanders wake by a Thaw Lantern. Read a Rime Moth or a Salamander with the Loupe.

pages.t: Distillate is not a fluid, and ordinary AE2 buses do not carry it: import, export and storage buses do not see currents. Currents have buses of their own, and they go by the rules of siphons: the Siphon Bus draws at the side or under a holder, the Pouring Bus pours from above, into the mouth, the Store Bus sees a store from any side.

A bus in the wrong place stays silent: distillate does not flow out of a mouth or pour into a spout. The bus windows are as in AE2: config slots (set a current with a vial), card slots, redstone. AE2 cards work as you know them, and the fuzzy card has a meaning of its own — a branch of the Wheel.

nodes.hint: Buses of their own for distillate

pages.t: AE2's Charger, Inscriber and Growth Accelerator work without a network too — if someone turns them. An automaton cannot turn AE2's wooden crank, but it can turn the brass one: set it on a face of the device, paint an Operate sigil on it, and the automaton gives the device a turn with every press.
A device that needs no turn (charged, nothing to press) does not take it — the crank clicks idly. You can turn it by hand as well.

kp: Латунная рукоять Brass Crank Латунная рукоять Brass Crank
nodes.hint: An automaton turns AE2 devices

pages.t: A Confluence Provider gives the Heart distillate from an ME network: set it within 12 blocks of the Heart, like a vessel, and run an AE2 cable with a channel to it — the Heart sees every current of the network in it and draws whatever it needs part by part. A ribbon the colour of each drawn part flows from the Provider's lens to the Heart.

A part leaves the network the moment it is drawn: a network without power or a channel leaves the Provider empty, and the Confluence waits as without a vessel. While the network lives, the beads of the abacus glow round in turn and the lens shines.
Made by Confluence: an AE2 Interface on the central Plinth; opaline, a speculum sheet, a Marked Tile and AE2 quartz glass on the side ones; Lattice 8 and Craft 4.

kp: Поставщик Слияния Confluence Provider Поставщик Слияния Confluence Provider
nodes.hint: The Heart draws distillate from an ME network

pages.t: The Steward makes Confluences on order from an AE2 terminal. Set it by the altar, within 8 blocks of the central plinth, with an AE2 cable, and beside it a Pattern Provider with a processing pattern: the Confluence items (centre and sides) — what is made. The pattern needs no distillate: the Heart draws it itself — from vessels and a Confluence Provider.

Given an order, the Steward lays the centre on the central plinth and the rest on free side plinths in an even ring, waits until the Heart's reckoning says "enough" or "barely", and touches the Heart for whoever set it down — with their knowledge, their calm, their boons. What is made goes into the network, and the AE2 order is done.

It bends no rules: it never starts against the reckoning, waits for a Heart woken with quickdust, and starts only while whoever set it down is in the game. If an eddy knocks an item off, it picks it up by the altar and lays it back on the same plinth. If the Confluence fails, what is left on the plinths and by the altar goes into the network too. The Loupe on the Steward says what it waits for.

kp: Распорядитель Слияния Confluence Steward Распорядитель Слияния Confluence Steward
nodes.hint: A Confluence on order from the terminal

pages.t: With Applied Energistics 2 distillate is kept as a count, not in glass: hundreds of thousands of parts of any currents in one rack of drives, runes in the terminal beside items, a vial that fills at the terminal, buses of its own between vessels, the Crucible and the Brewing Tower, a Confluence on order from the terminal and a Heart that draws any current from the network.

It does not replace the craft: currents are born in the Crucible and in distilling, the Wheel and the clash work as ever. The network only keeps and carries. Its power comes from a Flux Mill beside an AE2 Energy Acceptor — the flux of the land, which dries up as with any work; distillate is never burned for power.

The Reckoners wanted to "solve the world" — to reckon every current. Their cords and tablets held the measure of a current, but not the current: a written count does not flow. The masters of quartz can do what the Reckoners only wrote of — turn a thing into a number and the number back into a thing.

A reckoned current does not flow: it does not clash, boil away or turn to murk until it is let out as distillate. That is how the Order of the Still Hour began — with a count, with a stop. What is reckoned must be let out, or it is dead.

nodes.hint: Currents in an Applied Energistics 2 ME network

pages.t: A Gauge Card keeps a holder at a mark — a quarter, a half or three quarters: a Siphon Bus takes nothing below it, a Pouring Bus pours nothing above it, a Store Bus leaves the store everything below. So the network shares a store with the Heart, siphons and vials instead of draining it dry.
Move the mark by using the card in hand: a light on the gauge rule of the icon shows where it is. The Reckoners set a gauge rule by every sluice — counting levels is older than counting parts.

kp: Мерная карта Gauge Card Мерная карта Gauge Card
nodes.hint: Keep a holder at a mark

pages.t: A Brewing Tower brews Crucible recipes on order from the terminal: a processing pattern "the currents of the recipe and a catalyst — the brew" in an AE2 Pattern Provider above the tower. The provider pours the currents into the dome and lays the catalyst on top, a Siphon Bus at the tower takes the brewed distillate, and a hopper below takes items.

The tower accepts only the currents of the recipes it remembers and no more than for two brews — the provider keeps the rest and pours it later. Teach the tower as always: with a catalyst, and a potion with a sample.

kp: The Kettle by Pattern Самовар по шаблону
nodes.hint: A Brewing Tower on order from the terminal

pages.t: Murk is not counted alongside clean currents: ordinary and Still cells refuse it, and with no room for it the network takes none — neither by vial nor through a Tally Vessel. A Sump Cell holds Murk alone: with one, Murk gathers in the network — for Murk Flasks, Druses and vats.

A Siphon Bus takes no Murk, so it gathers in the holder. With a Bleed Card the bus first bleeds the Murk out: into a Sump Cell, or, with nowhere to go, as murk into the land by the holder, a quarter part per part. The holder stays clean, but the workshop grows murky in plain sight — flakes by the bus.

kp: Murk in the Network Муть в сети
Отстойная ячейка Sump Cell Выпускная карта Bleed Card Отстойная ячейка Sump Cell
nodes.hint: The Sump Cell and the Bleed Card

pages.t: The Pouring Bus feeds a holder from the network: above it, facing down, it pours the currents of its slots part by part while the holder accepts — in turn, so that one current does not take the whole stroke. So the network keeps vessels by the altar, the Crucible, a tower and a Purifier full (into its side inlet).

The network makes no murk: the bus never pours into a Crucible a current whose opposite Spring is already there, nor beyond its limit. With a fuzzy card a current in a slot calls its branch of the Wheel — everything made from it that the network holds.

kp: Наливная шина Pouring Bus Наливная шина Pouring Bus
nodes.hint: From the network into a holder's mouth

pages.t: The Siphon Bus takes distillate into the network: from a vessel, a Gyre, a Crucible, a Separator — anything that gives to a siphon. Set it at the side or under a holder (at a Crucible only at the side: heat is below). It takes what a siphon would and only what the network accepts: from a Crucible, the fullest.

The currents in its slots are a filter: empty — it takes everything. With a fuzzy card a current in a slot lets through its branch of the Wheel — itself and everything made from it (Tide — and Rime, Drift, Bloom and on); with an inverter — everything but. Speed and capacity are as on an AE2 import bus.

kp: Сифонная шина Siphon Bus Сифонная шина Siphon Bus
nodes.hint: From a holder into the network

pages.t: A Still Tally Cell is for a network that holds the whole Wheel at once: 63 currents instead of 18 and over six million parts in one cell, and not a drop of power while idle. Use it when ordinary cells outnumber the slots of your drives.
Stillmetal remembers the Great Stop: what is reckoned in it stands like the Still Hour and needs no power to stand. It takes no Murk either — that belongs in a Sump Cell.

kp: Стылая счётная ячейка Still Tally Cell Стылая счётная ячейка Still Tally Cell
nodes.hint: The whole Wheel in one cell, with no idle draw
